26ai Duality Views: Build Updatable JSON Documents 12010 4375 Database jeff.d.smith@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed A bite-sized, hands-on introduction to JSON Relational Duality Views in Oracle Database 26ai. In 15 to 25 minutes, learn how to create single-table and multi-table duality views and perform CRUD operations on relational data through an updatable JSON document interface using SQL, with embedded worksheets integrated directly into the lab. In this hands-on, bite-sized lab (15 to 20 minutes), you will build a small conference schema, create single-table and multi-table JSON Relational Duality Views, and perform full CRUD operations through the document interface. The lab also demonstrates querying nested JSON documents with SQL using JSON_TABLE and applying fine-grained controls such as read-only attributes.

This workshop is designed as a concise introduction to JSON Relational Duality Views and uses embedded FreeSQL worksheets directly within the LiveLabs experience, allowing participants to run SQL and explore Oracle Database 26ai features without leaving the lab. 8 Partitioning Techniques in Oracle Database 10061 938 Database madhusudhan.rao@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Oracle Partitioning enhances the manageability, performance and availability of large databases. Oracle Partitioning enhances the manageability, performance and availability of large databases. It offers comprehensive partitioning methods to address different business requirements. We can apply Database partitioning on transactional, data warehousing, and mixed workload applications without changing any code. We can use partitioning on large tables and indexes to make them smaller objects that can be managed and accessed at a more advanced level of granularity. 

In this workshop, the user will learn how to create eight different types of partitioning based on their business and data requirements. The examples provided are simple, easy to run and great to understand the business use-cases behind the different types of partitions. In this track, Kubernetes experts from Oracle will teach you everything you need to know about deploying secure scalable apps on Oracle Container Engine for Kubernetes (OKE). You will gain comprehensive knowledge, from creating a cluster to implementing the best practices for managing and deploying microservices and containerized applications, that will enable you to develop and operate distributed applications successfully. ·        Integrating applications with your networking pattern

Accelerate Analytics on OAC with Generative AI, AIDP Data Platform, and Autonomous AI Lakehouse 11972 4278 AI Services luke.farley@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Jumpstart your journey into modern data engineering and analytics on Oracle Cloud. In this hands-on workshop, you’ll use Oracle AI Data Platform (AIDP) to build a lakehouse pipeline from raw data to actionable insights, leveraging Autonomous AI Lakehouse for analytics and OAC for compelling visualizations. Unlock the power of Oracle’s next-generation analytics ecosystem in this hands-on workshop designed for new data professionals and cloud practitioners. You’ll explore the “lakehouse” paradigm by working with real airline operations data, learning to ingest, transform, and analyze large-scale datasets using Oracle AI Data Platform (AIDP).

You’ll build an end-to-end pipeline—loading raw data into the cloud, performing scalable cleansing and enrichment with Spark and Delta Lake in AIDP, serving curated analytics in Autonomous AI Data Lakehouse (ADL), and discovering actionable insights through interactive dashboards in Oracle Analytics Cloud (OAC). This session requires no prior cloud experience and leaves you prepared to accelerate analytics projects using Oracle’s robust Lakehouse patterns.

Key takeaways:

Understand the basics of the lakehouse architecture in Oracle Cloud.
Build and deploy ETL pipelines in AIDP using Spark and Delta Lake.
Prepare and analyze data in Autonomous AI Data Lakehouse.
Create visual dashboards and reports using Oracle Analytics Cloud.
Experience hands-on, end-to-end data flow—from raw files to business-ready insights.
No prior experience with Spark or Oracle Cloud required—just curiosity and readiness to learn! Accelerate Auto Claims Process: Insights with Oracle Analytics Cloud and Autonomous AI Database 11969 4287 Analytics jadd.jennings@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Join this interactive lab to set up Oracle Autonomous AI Database and Analytics Cloud for modernizing insurance claims. Learn to use AI-driven tools to categorize and summarize data, flag suspicious claims, detect premium leakage, and improve processes—boosting accuracy, efficiency, and compliance. In this hands-on live lab, you’ll learn how to provision and set up Oracle AI Autonomous Database and Oracle Analytics Cloud to modernize and optimize the insurance claims process. Guided by practical scenarios, you’ll use advanced analytics and AI-driven tools to automatically categorize and summarize claims data, helping to detect and reduce premium leakage.
Participants will walk through the provisioning and setup of Autonomous AI Database and Analytics Cloud. Upon completion, you will have a working environment that can be used to flag suspicious claims for investigation and foster clear communication with policyholders or agents about missing details. The workshop spotlights the collaboration between Claims Team Supervisors and Claims Analysts, demonstrating how Oracle’s AI solutions enable teams to efficiently analyze complex data, identify instances of fraud and inefficiency, and implement process improvements.
Through a series of interactive exercises, you’ll explore how to uncover trends, patterns, and anomalies within policy and claims data, realizing benefits like increased accuracy, substantial time savings, and actionable insights—all while maintaining strong oversight through human-in-the-loop processes. Harnessing built-in AI and machine learning capabilities, you’ll learn to unify diverse data sources, detect inconsistencies, and predict potential premium leakage, empowering your insurance organization to make smarter decisions, ensure compliance, and reinforce the integrity of claims operations. Accelerate insurance claim processing with AI Data Platform and Generative AI 12038 AI Services kaushik.kundu@oracle.com Workshop Approved Jumpstart your journey into modern data engineering on Oracle Cloud. In this hands-on workshop, you’ll use Oracle AI Data Platform (AIDP) and Oracle Generative AI to summarize video & image claim evidences and automate insurance claim decisions with business rules, and thereby accelerate insurance claim processing. The insurance claim processing workshop shows how you could make life a lot easier for insurance underwriters. Instead of spending hours watching surveillance or inspection footage, underwriters get instant, written summaries that highlight the important details they need for risk assessment and claim validation. This means decisions are made faster, documentation is clearer and more organized, and it’s easier to spot inconsistencies or fraud. The process is more efficient, less prone to human error, and helps underwriters focus on actual risk, not tedious video review. In short, this solution streamlines underwriting by quickly converting visual information into actionable insights and reliable records, making the whole process quicker, smarter, and more accurate.

Key takeaways:

Build and deploy data pipelines in AIDP using Spark and Delta Lake.
Perform Video/Image to Text Summarization using OCI Generative AI - Video Summarization using OCI GenAI Google Gemini and Image Summarization using OCI GenAI xAI Grok
Rules based claim decision automation using OCI Generative AI - xAI Grok
Create visual dashboards using Oracle Analytics Cloud. Access provisioning in OCI using Oracle Access Governance 11852 4152 OCI indiradarshni.balasundaram@oracle.com Workshop Delete Requested Disabled Completed This workshop demonstrates how Oracle Access Governance can be integrated with OCI for user provisioning to groups and application roles Oracle Access Governance is a comprehensive governance solution that supports various provisioning methods, including access requests and approvals, role-based access control (RBAC), attribute-based access control (ABAC), and policy-based access control (PBAC). The service features a conversation-style user experience, offering deep visibility into access permissions across the entire enterprise. It facilitates dynamic, periodic, and automated event-based micro certifications, such as an access review triggered by a job code or manager change. Additionally, it enables near real-time access reviews, providing detailed recommendations with options for reviewers to accept or review an entitlement based on the identified level of risk.

This workshop walks you through the steps to setup OCI integration and perform group and application role provisioning in OCI. You will also explore the Who Has Access To What functionality through the enterprise-wide browser. The workshop walks you through the steps involved in requesting, approving, and getting the groups and roles provisioned in OCI. You will also learn how to configure and use Access Guardrails. records.searchable: Access the Data Lake using Autonomous Database and Data Catalog 7381 877 ADB Serverless lauran.serhal@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Delete Requested Explore accessing the Data Lake using Autonomous Database (ADB) Serverless and Data Catalog. The labs in this workshop walk you through all the steps that you need to access the Data Lake (Oracle Object Storage buckets) using Autonomous Database (ADB) and Data Catalog. First, you set-up the workshop environment and create resources such as a compartment, users, a Data Catalog instance,  an Autonomous Database instance, and the necessary IAM policies to use the Data Catalog, ADB, and Oracle Object Storage resources. Next, you create an Oracle Object Storage data asset in Data Catalog, add its data connections to access three Oracle Object Storage buckets, and create a filename pattern to specify the structure of the generated logical entities. Next, you harvest the data asset and view the harvested data entities. Next, you synchronize the Data Catalog metadata with ADB. Once the synchronization process is completed successfully, you can query data that lives in your Oracle database and combine that with data that is stored in your Oracle Object Storage buckets using regular SQL select statements that includes joined tables. Achieve Data Sovereignty with Oracle Globally distributed database 19c (aka Oracle Sharding) 11453 3850 Database - MAA ajay.aj.joshi@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Oracle Sharding’s User-Defined Sharding Method Implementation can help achieve Data Sovereignty. The proliferation of cloud computing has brought heightened concerns about industry-standard regulations especially around protecting data and its privacy. Today, most organizations want to know where their data is stored, and who has access to it. This creates a key concern about managing data residency—the requirement that data be stored in a specific geographic location.
Data sovereignty generally refers to how data is governed by regulations specific to the region in which it originated. These types of 
regulations can specify where data is stored, how it is accessed, how it is processed, and the life-cycle of the data.


In this Livelabs, learn how Oracle Sharding meets data sovereignty requirements and supports applications that require low latency and high availability.
1. Sharding makes it possible to locate different parts of the data in different countries or regions – thus satisfying regulatory requirements where data has to be located in a certain jurisdiction.

2. It also supports storing particular data closer to its consumers. Oracle Sharding automates the entire lifecycle of a sharded database – deployment, schema creation, data-dependent routing with superior run-time performance, elastic scaling, and life-cycle management.

3. It also provides the advantages of an enterprise RDBMS, including relational schema, SQL, and other programmatic interfaces, support for complex data types, online schema changes, multi-core scalability, advanced security, compression, high-availability, ACID properties, consistent reads, developer agility with XMLTYPE, JSON, and much more. Achieve optimal performance with User-Consumer group mapping in ADB 7361 3153 ADB Serverless goutam.pal@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA See How Easily You Can Add Users To Specific Consumer Groups In Autonomous Database Resource Managers or Consumer Groups or Service names are the integral part of Autonomous Databases as they manage the workload based on the performance characteristics of the Application. Autonomous Database comes with 5 preconfigured database services, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, TP and TPURGENT. The services control the priority of the sessions when the system is under resource pressure and some control the parallel degree used. By default, queries will execute serially when connected to the TP, TPURGENT and LOW services.
Users can specify a parallel degree on an object or uses optimizer hints to trigger parallel execution to be used when connected to the TP and TPURGENT services. Queries will be automatically executed in parallel when sessions are connected to the HIGH and MEDIUM services.

There are cases where we see a lot of application users misusing the consumer groups to their advantage and in doing so leading to performance overhead in the database.
So here in this blog we are going to show how to restrict users to certain consumer groups using database vault built into autonomous database.
One of the many security capabilities built into Autonomous Database is Database Vault. Database Vault implements powerful, unique security controls that restrict access to application data by privileged database users and enforce context-aware policies for data access by any user. Database Vault reduces the risk of insider and outside threats and addresses common compliance requirements. Advanced Text Search on JSON 11498 JSON/XML hermann.baer@oracle.com Workshop Approved Explore the capabilities of the JSON Search Index and the JSON_TextContains SQL operator. JSON search indexes are used to create indexes on all content within a JSON value. You don't need to know in advance the schema of the JSON - everything gets indexed. The Search index is used to accelerate "exact match" and "range search" queries using any of the standard SQL/JSON operators. It is also used by the JSON_TextContains SQL operator to perform full-text, or keyword, searches.

Full text searches use the rich query syntax of Oracle Text, and this lab explores some of the more advanced capabilities such as boolean logic, fuzzy matching and thesaurus operators. AI Agents with ODA: Simple Agent to advanced Multi-Agent Supervisors 11922 4212 AI Services marc.gueury@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed In this workshop, we will see how to build AI Agent using Oracle Digital Assistant.
The lab does not use any code, all is done with Oracle Digital Assistant low code and intuitive user interface.

There will be a several architectures of AI Agents in this LiveLab.
First, a single agent with tools and data to several advanced multi-Agent architectures. In this workshop, we will see how to build AI Agent using Oracle Digital Assistant.
The lab does not use any code, all is done with Oracle Digital Assistant low code and intuitive user interface.

There will be a several architectures of AI Agents in this LiveLab.
-  First, a single agent with tools and data.

AI Data Platform - Build a GenIAI-Powered Release and Performance Analyst - Entertainment Industry 12046 4384 Analytics eli.schilling@oracle.com Workshop Published Event Completed Build and deploy an AI agent on Oracle AI Data Platform that answers natural language questions about movie and TV show performance. Using AIDP Workbench's visual agent flow canvas, you'll combine RAG over internal strategy documents with SQL tools querying box office, streaming, and marketing data — then deploy the agent to a production REST endpoint. No coding required. In this hands-on workshop, you'll design, configure, test, and deploy a Release & Performance Analyst Agent — an AI-powered assistant built on Oracle AI Data Platform (AIDP) that serves entertainment marketing, finance, and content strategy teams from a single, governed interface.
The entertainment industry generates data across dozens of disconnected systems — box office receipts, streaming viewership, media spend, and internal strategy documents — but the teams who need that data are all pulling from different sources with different definitions of success. This workshop demonstrates how AIDP unifies structured data and internal knowledge into an AI agent that any team can query in natural language.
The agent you'll build combines two capabilities: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) over internal release playbooks, marketing measurement guidelines, and distribution rules; and SQL tools that execute parameterized queries against an Oracle AI Database containing box office, streaming, and marketing campaign data.
Lab 1 — Data Environment Setup (15 min): Explore the pre-configured standard catalog and managed volume in AIDP Workbench. Create a Knowledge Base that converts internal strategy documents into vector embeddings for semantic search. Verify the Oracle AI Database tables that contain box office, streaming, and marketing performance data.
Lab 2 — Agent Flow Setup (25 min): Create an AI Compute to host the agent. Build the agent flow on AIDP's visual canvas — configuring an agent node with a foundation model and detailed behavioral instructions, wiring up a RAG tool connected to the Knowledge Base, and adding seven SQL tools that cover box office performance, streaming health, campaign summaries, channel breakdowns, and reference lookups.
Lab 3 — Validate the Agent Flow (15 min): Test the agent in the Playground with real-world scenarios — multi-title box office comparisons (with typo handling), market-specific follow-ups that maintain conversational context, marketing ROI with channel breakdowns, cross-title streaming analysis, and custom tabular output on demand.
Lab 4 — Deploy the Agent Flow (5 min): Deploy the agent to a production REST endpoint on an AI Compute. Retrieve the endpoint URL and understand how external applications, dashboards, and integrations can consume the agent via REST API with OCI authentication. records.searchable: AI Data Platform Workbench Essentials 11988 4310 Analytics miles.novotny@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed In this lab you will learn the basics of the Oracle AI Data Platform Workbench (AIDP Workbench) by walking through a use case creating a medallion architecture. You will provision an AIDP Workbench and work with its components including catalogs, workspaces, compute clusters, notebooks, workflows, and RBAC. You will also learn to connect your AIDP Workbench to OAC and FDI. In this lab you will learn the basics of the Oracle AI Data Platform Workbench (AIDP Workbench) by walking through a use case creating a medallion architecture using supplier data. You will provision an AI Data Platform Workbench (AIDP Workbench), create a catalog, and populate it with data. Then you will create a workspace and compute cluster. Using these you will process your data in the AIDP Workbench notebook interface. While processing the data you will create tables in your catalog to hold the bronze, silver, and gold levels of your medallion architecture. You will leverage models from the OCI Generative AI service to aid in transforming and enriching your data. Then you will create a series of workflows to run your data processing tasks on a schedule. Along the way you will learn about RBAC AIDP Workbench. Then you will connect OAC to your AIDP to visualize your gold tier data. Finally, you will connect your Fusion AI Data Platform (Fusion AIDP) instance to the AIDP Workbench so that you can bring your data assets from Fusion AIDP into AIDP Workbench for further use. records.searchable: AI Data Platform Workbench Essentials - SANDBOX VERSION (PILOT ONLY) 12001 Analytics geoff.fawcett@oracle.com Workshop Delete Requested In this lab you will learn the basics of the Oracle AI Data Platform Workbench (AIDP Workbench) by walking through a use case creating a medallion architecture. You will provision an AIDP Workbench and work with its components including catalogs, workspaces, compute clusters, notebooks, workflows, and RBAC. You will also learn to connect your AIDP Workbench to OAC and FDI. In this lab you will learn the basics of the Oracle AI Data Platform Workbench (AIDP Workbench) by walking through a use case creating a medallion architecture using supplier data. You will provision an AI Data Platform Workbench (AIDP Workbench), create a catalog, and populate it with data. Then you will create a workspace and compute cluster. Using these you will process your data in the AIDP Workbench notebook interface. While processing the data you will create tables in your catalog to hold the bronze, silver, and gold levels of your medallion architecture. You will leverage models from the OCI Generative AI service to aid in transforming and enriching your data. Then you will create a series of workflows to run your data processing tasks on a schedule. Along the way you will learn about RBAC AIDP Workbench. Then you will connect OAC to your AIDP to visualize your gold tier data. Finally, you will connect your Fusion AI Data Platform (Fusion AIDP) instance to the AIDP Workbench so that you can bring your data assets from Fusion AIDP into AIDP Workbench for further use. AI - Develop an AI Agent application using LangChain and Oracle AI Database 26ai 11842 4185 AI/ML Database vijay.balebail@oracle.com Workshop Delete Requested Disabled Completed AI Vector Search series - Explore AI Agentics in our hands-on workshop! Build AI agents using Python & LangChain, integrating with Oracle AI Database 26ai for relational & RAG data. Learn to create custom tools, design prompts, & leverage context memory for tasks like email automation & PDF creation. Perfect for developers & AI enthusiasts to master intelligent systems & streamline workflows. In recent months, the field of AI Agentics has gained significant traction, showcasing the remarkable potential of AI to perform advanced logical reasoning and execute complex, multi-step tasks autonomously. AI agents represent a transformative leap in artificial intelligence, enabling systems to not only process information but also make decisions, interact with diverse data sources, and integrate with external tools to achieve sophisticated outcomes. This workshop is designed to provide participants with a comprehensive, hands-on understanding of building AI agents, empowering them to harness these cutting-edge capabilities for real-world applications.
The session will guide attendees through the process of creating a fully functional AI agent using Python and the LangChain framework. Through a practical example, we will demonstrate how an AI agent can seamlessly interact with relational data and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) data stored in an Oracle AI Database 26ai. Additionally, participants will learn how to extend the agent's functionality by integrating external tools, such as sending emails or generating PDFs, showcasing the versatility of AI agents in automating diverse workflows.

Workshop Highlights:
Environment Setup and Dependencies: Learn how to configure the necessary development environment, including installing required libraries and tools to ensure a smooth agent-building process.

Creating Custom Tools: Discover how to design and implement custom tools that enable the AI agent to perform specialized tasks, such as interacting with APIs or processing specific data formats.

Designing Effective Prompt Templates: Master the art of crafting prompt templates that guide the AI agent’s behavior, ensuring accurate and contextually relevant responses.

Initializing and Running the Agent: Gain hands-on experience in setting up and deploying the AI agent, observing how it processes inputs and executes tasks in real time.

Leveraging Context Memory: Explore the role of context memory in enabling the agent to maintain continuity and make informed decisions based on prior interactions.

Throughout this workshop, we'll explore:

1. Setting up the environment and dependencies
2. Creating custom tools for our agent
3. Designing effective prompt templates
4. AI Experience - Purchase Requisition Advisor Template Extension 11986 4307 Other - I don't see it rick.beck@oracle.com Workshop Published Private Completed This document provides step by step instructions for lab exercises to copy an out-of-the-box Fusion AI Agent Studio Template called Purchase Requisition Status and to add an extension for calling an external REST API to look up inventory stock information. Fusion AI Agent Studio is a design-time environment that empowers you to create, configure, validate, and deploy AI agents to meet your organization’s needs.
With AI Agent Studio, you can extend provided agents or create custom agents or multi-agent teams from scratch with the full suite of studio components.
Design single-agent workflows or multi-step agent teams, tailored to fit your specific needs.
In this exercise we will learn about the overall capabilities of Fusion AI Agent Studio by reviewing the out of the box tools, business objects, deep links, prompts, topics, and Agent types.  You will then learn how to extend the Purchase Requisition Status Advisor Template using the AI Agent Studio capabilities to add an External REST API call for looking up Item Inventory Stock levels.
The Purchase Requisition Status Advisor Template assist personnel with Purchase Requisition status and inventory stock quickly, and easily, so that the Procurement organization can proactively respond to any outstanding issues related to Requisitions and Inventory stock levels.  This leads to better support and supplier or customer satisfaction as issues get discovered and handled before they even know there was an issue. AI for Financial Services 11904 Developers - Database madhusudhan.rao@oracle.com Workshop Approved This workshop provides a comprehensive guide to the digital banking ecosystem, covering online banking, mobile banking, and digital payment systems. Through 23 labs, it covers topics such as user profile management, credit card applications, fraud detection, and business continuity, offering insights for banking professionals, fintech enthusiasts, and anyone interested in in digital banking In today's digital age, the banking and financial services sector has undergone a significant transformation. The rise of online banking, mobile banking apps, and digital payment systems has revolutionized the way customers interact with financial institutions. This workshop provides a comprehensive guide to the digital banking ecosystem, covering various aspects of online banking, from initiating conversations with chatbots to ensuring business continuity through high availability and disaster recovery.

Through 23 labs, this workshop takes readers on a journey through the digital banking landscape, exploring topics such as user profile management, account creation, fund transfers, e-commerce transactions, credit card applications, fraud detection, and spend analytics. The book also delves into the importance of ensuring business continuity, highlighting the need for high availability and disaster recovery measures.

Whether you are a banking professional, a fintech enthusiast, or simply someone interested in understanding the digital banking ecosystem, this workshop and labs provides valuable insights and knowledge to help you navigate the complex world of digital banking.

In this comprehensive learning journey, you will gain hands-on experience with the following technologies:

Oracle APEX and Oracle Database 23ai Technologies

1. Oracle APEX Custom Authentication and Authorization
2. Role-based access, ORDS and and PL/SQL Scheduler Jobs
3. Oracle APEX Workflow/Process and Task Definition
4. Transaction Management, Enqueue, and Dequeue
5. Security and Oracle Database 23ai & PL/SQL
6. Real-time Dashboard Oracle APEX
7. AI and Machine Learning Services

AI Services: Meta Llama Vision Instruct, Speech AI (TTS) and Anomaly Detection AI Service

1. Auto Machine Learning (AutoML) with Oracle Database 23ai and Oracle Analytics Cloud
2. Select AI & AI Vector Search
3. RAG with Oracle Generative AI (Cohere) and AI Agents
4. Document Understanding and Sentiment Analysis AI Service
5. Language AI and Translation Services 
6. Oracle Digital Assistant (FAQs)
  
Data Management and Analytics

1. Converged Database (JSON, Graphs, Maps & Spatial Data)
2. JSON Relational Duality and Data Redaction (Security)
3. Oracle Analytics Cloud and Notifications & Analytics

Integration and Process Management

1. Oracle Integration Cloud (Gen 3)
2. AI Services: Introduction to OCI Vision 8521 931 OCI vaishnavi.kotturu@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Explore OCI Vision within the AI Service group to perform tasks like image classification, object detection, text detection, document AI etc., with a few simple steps. Enterprise image and document data has significant value related to core business activities and their customers. To gain business and customer insights effectively and at scale from this data, vision capabilities are needed. For example, identifying key requirements to understand customer perception of their products to address gaps. Some core capabilities include classifying images & documents, detecting objects, text & languages and extracting table information from the data. These capabilities are typically machine learning algorithms custom built, tuned by Data Scientists and productized for use in applications. Doing this is a time consuming and expensive proposition. 

OCI Vision Service reduces time and effort to perform Vision tasks like image classification, object detection, text detection, document AI etc by providing key vision capabilities via production-ready REST APIs. The service enables applications to automate sophisticated image and document analysis at scale without needing ML expertise. The service functionality is implemented with pre-trained ML models which are often useful. They may also be further customized to understand the patterns of the customer’s context by providing additional data. AI Vector Search - 7 Easy Steps to Building a RAG Application using LangChain 11619 3927 AI/ML Database milton.wan@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Using LangChain and Python you will build a RAG application with  Oracle AI Vector Search and  your choice of LLMs. Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) is an important component in Generative AI.  Here are three reasons why RAG should be included in your Gen AI application.
1.	LLMs can hallucinate or generate incorrect responses to your prompt if it has not been trained to respond to the query in the prompt.  Retraining LLMs to produce the responses you want can be very expensive.
2.	Businesses and enterprises have lots of private and confidential information and they want to leverage the power of Gen AI with LLMs with the least cost.  
3.	Businesses and enterprises have streaming data and need LLM responses to this data in near real time.

And that’s where RAG comes in.  RAG allows important context to be included with the prompt to the LLM.  In this workshop you will provide context and store that information in the form of vectors in Oracle Database 23ai, and use the Oracle AI Vector Search capability to return the context to augment LLM responses. You will use the popular LangChain framework to build the RAG application. Steps include using a sample Java program, Configuring API key, embedding vector tables, and performing basic Vector operations. Oracle Database 23ai introduces a suite of powerful new Vector Database capabilities, including support for Vectors to store generative Al embedding models, Al Vector Similarity Search and powerful new AI Indexes. You can choose from a variety of embedding models, including Cohere, and Open AI. AI4U 12008 4315 Database david.start@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Build AI agents that remember. Learn to create database-powered agents with persistent memory, semantic search, and enterprise data access using Oracle Select AI Agent framework. Hands-on with SQL. Most AI systems can answer questions. AI agents are built to do work.

In this hands-on workshop, you will build AI agents for a financial services company called Seer Equity. Their current systems cannot answer simple questions like loan status or pending applications. Instead of returning results, they explain how to look things up. That breaks trust and frustrates clients.

You will build AI agents that connect directly to a loan database and return real answers. When asked about a loan, the agent queries data and responds with the current status, amount, and owner. You will see exactly what the agent did and why it did it.

During the workshop, you will:

Build AI agents that act on data instead of explaining steps

Store and recall client information across interactions

Use prior decisions to guide new ones

Apply company policies stored in the database

Record every action for audit and compliance

You will use Oracle Database and the Select AI Agent framework to define tools, agents, tasks, and teams using SQL. By the end, you will have a working loan processing system built around AI agents that behave consistently and can be trusted.

No machine learning background required. Just SQL and curiosity. AIStore Cluster in OCI 11819 4095 OCI cristian.vlad@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Complete In this workshop, we will explore in detail how to use AIStore which is a lightweight object storage system with the capability to linearly scale out with each added storage node and a special focus on petascale deep learning. The goal of this workshop is to provide hands-on examples demonstrating the integration and use of AIStore. Participants will gain practical experience with interacting with AIStore in an OCI environment which can be helpful to deploy and scale datasets for machine learning usecases.

In this workshop, you will learn how to:

1. Bring up an AIStore cluster in OCI VM Instance
2. Use AIStore cli commands into OCI VM Instance to list buckets, copy buckets and delete buckets. Analyse Application Dependencies with Graph Studio 11465 3788 Community Oracle Partner Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Contributor: Stephan LaRocca, Senior Business Development Director, PITSS Gmbh.

Explore how to use parsed data from your Legacy application for software modernization, like identifying Bounded Context or adding runtime data to identify Business Processes. The workshop is based on extracted data from a real-world sample and uses Oracle Graph Studio to analyze and visualize the data. Contributor: Stephan LaRocca, Senior Business Development Director, PITSS Gmbh.

This workshop demonstrates how to use parsed data from your Legacy application for software modernization, like identifying Bounded Context or adding runtime data to identify Business Processes. The workshop is based on extracted data from a real-world sample and uses Oracle Graph Studio to analyze and visualize the data. 

Extracting the dependency data out of a data model, the SQL statements, the PL/SQL implementation, and the UI design and finally enhancing all of them with the user behavior of a legacy application is one of the key components of the Product PITSS.CON. It is used, e.g., to Modernize an Oracle Forms Application to APEX. The Graph Data model and various algorithms are integrated into PITSS.CON

The workshop focuses on the capabilities of the Oracle graph engine. 

Learn more: 
Product page: https://pitss.com/forms2apex-modeler/

In this workshop you'll work on Oracle MovieStream, a fictitious on-line movie streaming company. The company is now looking for better, smarter ways to track performance, identifying target customers with campaigns to promote new services, new movies and new viewing platforms.

Many of the analytical scenarios in this workshop will very likely match the challenges you are seeing in your business and we hope the following examples will give you some insight into how Oracle can help you solve these common everyday challenges. Analyze and troubleshoot connectivity in your OCI network 11625 3990 OCI Marketing Workshop Published Disabled Completed Networks can be complex with multiple VCNs, subnets, and gateways connecting many resources. What does your network look like? Why can't resources connect with each other? Learn how to use Network Visualizer to experience a graphical view of your network. Run Network Path Analyzer to determine why resources aren't communicating. You'll gain the skills to troubleshoot your own network. Are your cloud deployments growing with your business needs, have you considered what it takes to visualize your infrastructure and what is available to help troubleshoot resource connectivity. Can you imagine how effective it can be to have cloud resources readily available that can assist in real time with visualizing and troubleshooting your deployments. OCI has the built-in tools and services that provide the insights across all your deployed resources.

In this session we will demonstrate how to effectively deploy an infrastructure consuming of network and compute resources.  We will begin by creating a foundation with the virtual cloud network (VCN), include subnets, security list, routing and the corresponding compute representing client and server resources. The focus of the session will then shift to using the Network Visualizer and Network Path Analyzer to assist in understanding the breadth of your deployment and to assist with troubleshooting. At the end of the session, you will walk away with a complete understanding of the OCI components required to create your application foundation and the tools and services required to effectively manage and troubleshoot your deployment. Analyze Document Store with RAG on Oracle APEX 11861 4187 APEX rachel.ogle@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed In this lab, participants will explore the integration of Oracle APEX with Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) AI services to create a powerful, AI-driven solution for quickly accessing and analyzing relevant information. This workshop is ideal for technical professionals looking to enhance their expertise in developing smart applications that can extract insights. In this hands-on lab, participants will explore the powerful integration of Oracle APEX and Oracle AI services, including Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) and Large Language Models (LLMs), to create a seamless, AI-driven solution designed for document management and analysis. Participants will learn how to build applications that enable users to interact with documents via chat, allowing them to quickly analyze, extract valuable insights, and easily upload documents to Oracle Cloud services, such as Object Storage.
The lab will guide participants through the process of integrating Oracle APEX as the front-end solution for building intuitive applications, while building a native chatbot for conversational AI capabilities. Users will interact with documents, asking natural language questions and receiving real-time responses, empowering them to extract key information quickly. Oracle AI, powered by LLMs, will be used to analyze uploaded documents, such as financial reports, press releases, and news articles, to deliver insights through advanced natural language processing.

On the backend, participants will explore how Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) AI services and Autonomous Database can be used to process and analyze the documents stored in Oracle Cloud, applying pre-built AI models to extract relevant insights. The AI models will be trained to identify key information within documents, such as sentiment, financial highlights, and important trends, helping users make data-driven decisions faster. Each day, these trucks embark on journeys from various starting points, heading to different destinations. Given the vast distances covered, extended travel times, and the varying weather conditions across different road segments, ensuring the safety of both the trucks and their drivers is a paramount concern.

To bolster safety measures, the company has equipped each truck with state-of-the-art safety testing devices, commonly referred to as IoT (Internet of Things). These devices continuously relay real-time information about the truck's location and its operational status to a centralized system. This data is then processed and analyzed by the Oracle Big Data Service (BDS), which offers the following insights to enhance the efficiency and safety of the company's operations:
¿	Real-time monitoring of each truck's location.
¿	Alerts regarding hazardous road segments. Should a truck approach or traverse a risky section, an alert is dispatched to the driver, urging heightened caution.
¿	Comprehensive analysis of driving patterns, including metrics like braking, acceleration, and average speed. Additionally, the system monitors vehicle health indicators such as fuel consumption and engine temperature.

You will create an NBA analytics dashboard with OAC and embed it into Visual Builder using its embedding framework (iframe). Additionally, you will use the Oracle Generative AI service to query the NBA data and ask questions. This workshop brings together the power of Oracle Analytics Cloud, Visual Builder, and the OCI Generative AI Service to deliver an application that provides a powerful tool for analyzing NBA performance. In this workshop you will use NBA datasets to create OAC dashboards which include custom map backgrounds and layers to map statistics onto court locations. These visualizations are embedded into a Visual Builder app using iframes. The app also leverages the OCI Gen AI Service to allow users to ask questions about the data with natural language. This extends the analysis abilities of this tool beyond what the visualizations display, as the Gen AI model can inform its response user questions using the underlying datasets of the dashboard. This unique use case shows how the OCI Gen AI service can be used alongside other Oracle products to improve upon and augment the manner in which users interface with them. records.searchable:
APEXLang: the future of Oracle APEX application development 11913 Developers - Database jeff.d.smith@oracle.com Workshop Approved APEXLang is a new language, enabling file based development for APEX developers. Your APEXLang files will be compiled back into the database. APEX developers can now more easily leverage CI/CD workflows, e.g.  working out of Git projects, doing DIFFs, etc. all while doing so with modern IDEs such as SQL Developer. APEXLang is a new language, enabling file based development for APEX developers. Your APEXLang files will be compiled back into the database. APEX developers can now more easily leverage CI/CD workflows, e.g.  working out of Git projects, doing DIFFs, etc. all while doing so with modern IDEs such as SQL Developer.

In this lab you will take an existing APEX app, export it to a set of APEXLang files, work with the files directly in VS Code and/or SQLcl, and publish your changes back to the database.

Imagine a page's logo being defined simply with:

logo {
       text: TEST application
         }

Using VS Code with our SQL Developer Extension, you will be able to take advantage of features such as Goto Declaration or Search & Replace ACROSS an entire APEX application.

Since your APEX app will frequently use multiple languages to define a page or feature, SQL, PL/SQL, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, you will be able to get support for all of these alongside the APEXLang grammar as you build and maintain your apps. 

You will learn how to interact with these files, 'compile' them back into the database, and see the changes come to life in your APEX app! Application Continuity made simple with Universal Connection Pool 11169 3396 Database - MAA francois.pons@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Run this hands-on workshop to learn how to use RAC services, configure Fast Application Notification, Connection Draining, and Application Continuity from an Oracle connection pool (UCP). Application Continuity makes planned maintenance activities and unplanned outages transparent to end-users by recovering the in-flight work of impacted database sessions.
Run this hands-on workshop to learn how to use RAC services, configure Fast Application Notification, Connection Draining, and Application Continuity from an Oracle connection pool (UCP).
This workshop is based on a compute instance (a demo application) connected to a 2-node Oracle RAC Database Cloud Service.
The demo application is a simple Java program using a 21c client. Its code shows how to create and use a Universal Connection Pool to the RAC.
The demo program allows one to interrupt a transaction at will and show whether or not it is transparently replayed on a different node of the RAC.
Different database services with or without Application Continuity can be tested. Application onboarding is the process of registering or associating an application with Oracle Identity Manager so that Oracle Identity Manager can provision or reconcile user information in or from that application.
Oracle Identity Manager provides a quick and convenient way to onboard applications by using the Applications option on the Manage tab in Identity Self Service. You can perform all the necessary configurations to onboard an application from a single console.

Applied Developer Course for Howard University 11209 Developers - Database saipriya.thirvakadu@oracle.com Workshop In Development Series of hands on labs to showcase how to use the OCI low-code development platform to build enterprise healthcare applications to improve the efficiency of the operation of Hospitals. Business Problem: The evolving healthcare needs imposes challenges for Hospitals to maintain increasing patients records, address their needs in a timely manner, assist proactively with the patient community and identify groups at risk
Patients also need quick and personalized access to their health information and immediate assistance when required

OCI Solution: Healthcare Administrator, can leverage the Oracle APEX on Autonomous Database to build compelling applications to manage the patient records. Architecting Deep Learning Training Environments on OCI 2961 GoldenGate gloria.g.lee@oracle.com Workshop Approved This lab shows how to run machine-learning and deep-learning workloads on OCI This lab exaplins why you should consider running machine-learning and deep-learning workloads on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. It also provides a framework for IT administrators, machine-learning engineers, and data scientists to build solutions using Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. 

Building on-premises high-performance computing (HPC) environments for machine learning, deep learning, or other performance-intensive workloads can be complex and time consuming. The public cloud can provide a variety of benefits over this more traditional approach, including faster infrastructure updates, easier scaling of resources, lower capital expenditures (CapEx), and fewer personnel dedicated to basic infrastructure maintenance. But the cloud also provokes concerns around performance and cost for those who tried to run performance-intensive workloads on first-generation public clouds.

This validated solution guide explains why you should consider running deep learning workloads on Oracle’s Generation 2 Cloud. It then provides a framework for IT administrators, deep-learning engineers, and data scientists to build solutions using Oracle Cloud Infrastructure.

This guide can help you accelerate the building of cloud infrastructure for your deep learning workloads while providing guidance on customizing the architecture and security throughout. Additionally, it provides guidelines, code, and Terraform scripts for quickly setting up a proof of concept (PoC) using TensorFlow and NVIDIA GPUs for deep learning and image processing for autonomous driving, a rapidly growing area of focus for deep learning. records.searchable: Artificial Intelligence:  Getting Started with Computer Vision using PyTorch 3042 706 HPC brian.bennett@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Explore how to train a model using CPUs and update code to utilize GPU resources. Implementing image classification training is the "Hello World" of computer vision. Although there are many blog posts about the topic, most of them present the solution without adequately explaining the library API, the underlying principals, or both. The "Training a Classifier" guide from PyTorch is a great place to start, but some of the details of the code are explained too sparsely for a reader new to the field. This workshop builds on that tutorial as a base with line-by-line explanations of the code to facilitate a clearer learning pathway. This guide will show you how to train a model using CPUs-only and then explain how to update code to utilize GPU resources. Automate and accelerate inventory analytics 11229 3426 AI Services mark.d.heffernan@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA This workshop features elements of the proof-of-concept developed for Oracle Industry Lab, where an OCI Vision model was used for automating inventory counting in an industry/manufacturing context, using a programmable drone and stacked pipes. Manual inventory management can be a time consuming and labor intensive process. Manufacturers often struggle with keeping an updated stock of inventory and with keeping track of the inventory location leading to lost revenue and under-utilised capital. The inventory counting process on-site for large remote factories or warehouse facilities involves time and resource intensive steps, constraints and is prone to errors.

OCI Vision can be used to supplement manual inventory management efforts by using drones (or other robots) to observe, count and report information more quickly and more reliably.

This lab features elements of the recently developed proof-of-concept for Oracle Industry Lab, where the goal was to use stacked pipes as an example of an automated inventory counting scenario, using a programmable drone and a custom OCI Vision model. records.searchable: Automate Customer Feedback Analytics 11298 AI Services yanir.shahak@oracle.com Workshop Delete Requested Using Oracle Cloud Infrastructure's AI Services, Oracle Integration Cloud and Oracle Analytics Cloud, we would take customer feedback in natural language and produce actionable business insights. Customer feedback saved as text in natural language is a locked box awaiting to be opened. In the past, we would assign people to read each individual review and score them appropriately. Obviously, such a process does not scale well and is error prone. Using Oracle Cloud Infrastructure's AI Services, Oracle Integration Cloud and Oracle Analytics Cloud, we can easily automate the process improving accuracy and scale while extracting actionable business insights. Detecting issues across the areas of vegetation overgrowth, utility assets, and factory machinery can be time consuming and labor intensive, but it can be automated with AI. Keeping businesses running smoothly and minimizing downtime during system failures is crucial for developers and IT teams managing OCI deployments. OCI Full Stack DR provides a complete solution for automating DR across regions or ADs OCI Full Stack Disaster Recovery (Full Stack DR) offers a fully automated and comprehensive disaster recovery solution for all layers of a full-stack cloud application, including infrastructure, database, and application. •	Provide detailed logs with error management and recovery
•	Conduct DR recovery drills
•	Offer a framework to customize DR operations

Automate Disaster Recovery of PeopleSoft environment using Full Stack Disaster Recovery 11383 3678 OCI vinay.shivanna@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Using this workshop, learn how to automate disaster recovery operations for the PeopleSoft application in OCI using Full Stack Disaster Recovery. Full Stack Disaster Recovery is an OCI, cloud-native service providing full stack disaster recovery orchestration for Oracle applications (PeopleSoft in this case), Oracle Database, storage, networking, and compute instances (VMs) between OCI regions. Using Full Stack DR Service you can perform

• Create and automate DR run books and make them more flexible
• Manage DR operations using a single pane of glass
• Provide comprehensive logs with error management and recovery
• Perform DR recovery drills, and

Automate Invoice handling using Oracle APEX and OCI Document Understanding 11675 3948 APEX ankita.beri@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed In this workshop, you learn to integrate Oracle APEX with OCI Document Understanding, highlighting steps to incorporate these technologies seamlessly into your workflow. In the digital transformation era, businesses constantly seek innovative solutions to enhance their processes and maximize efficiency. Oracle APEX and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Document Understanding have emerged as powerful tools to streamline data extraction and processing.

In this workshop, you learn to integrate Oracle APEX with OCI Document Understanding, highlighting steps to incorporate these technologies seamlessly into your workflow.

Within this user-friendly app built with the Oracle APEX low-code platform, users effortlessly upload invoices by selecting the "Select an Invoice or Receipt" option. OCI Document Understanding then extracts form fields from the uploaded image or PDF file. With this functionality, users can streamline their expense management process with ease.

Once your document is processed, you will easily transition to a user-friendly page featuring the Cards Region, which displays critical information in an organized manner. Clicking on a card brings up a Pop-up Dialog page where you will find a clear comparison between your uploaded PDF and the output from OCI Document Understanding. Modern cloud environments often require firewall policies to allow access to Oracle services while maintaining strict traffic control and visibility. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) publishes public IP address ranges in JSON format, including ranges associated with the Oracle Services Network (OSN). records.searchable: Automatic Indexing for Oracle Autonomous Database 11124 3328 ADB Serverless nigel.bayliss@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete The Oracle Autonomous Database can manage indexes without the need for manual intervention. Creating indexes requires a deep knowledge of the data model, how client applications behave, and the characteristics of the data stored in the database. In the past, DBAs were responsible for making choices about which indexes to create, and the decisions made were never reconsidered, even if the database changed. As a result, opportunities for improvement were lost, and the use of unnecessary indexes could become a performance liability. Now, Oracle’s Autonomous Database can manage indexes without the need for manual intervention. Automatic Partitioning in Autonomous Database 9061 935 ADB Serverless nigel.bayliss@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Explore how to use automatic partitioning in Oracle Autonomous Database. The aim of this workshop is to become familiar with automatic partitioning and the several automated tasks executed by it. You furthermore will learn about the controls of automatic partitioning to optimally leverage it for your environment to improve performance. 

In this lab, you will create a 5GB non-partitioned table called APART, filled with random data and run a test workload on the APART table. Next you will run the auto partitioning validate API to confirm that the table meets auto partitioning requirements. Then execute the auto partitioning recommend task in report-only mode. The task will build a partitioned copy of the table and compare performance before vs. after partitioning. Finally, use the apply API to implement the auto partition recommendation. The APART table will be  transformed into an ONLINE ALTER TABLE operation so that the production workload is not interrupted. Automation of Machine Learning Workflows with OCI and Argo Workflows 11822 4103 OCI dragos.nicu@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Complete Learn how to build a fully automated machine learning pipeline by integrating Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) services with Argo Workflows. This lab guides you through creating and deploying a scalable ML workflow for medical imaging, incorporating object storage for data management, OCI Functions and Events for triggering workflows, and Terraform for infrastructure deployment. This hands-on lab demonstrates the integration of Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) services with Argo Workflows to create a fully automated, end-to-end machine learning pipeline. Designed for scenarios such as medical imaging analysis, the lab walks you through the process of managing raw and processed data in OCI Object Storage, automating workflows with Argo Workflows, and deploying OCI Functions and Events to trigger workflows based on real-time data changes.

The lab also includes a comprehensive Terraform script for infrastructure deployment, provisioning the necessary OCI infrastructure, including Kubernetes clusters, object storage buckets, and the associated network configurations. Participants will learn how to customise Python scripts with variables for namespaces during deployment and configure webhook triggers to automate workflow execution. By the end of the lab, you will have a robust and scalable machine learning pipeline integrated with OCI, ready to handle real-world workloads. records.searchable: Autonomous AI Database OCI IAM Deep Data Security Lab 12064 4453 Database  - Security richard.c.evans@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed This lab shows how to integrate Oracle Cloud IAM with Oracle AI Database 26ai and apply Deep Data Security so the database enforces per-user access based on identity. Users like Marvin and Emma authenticate via OCI IAM and see different results from the same query. Autonomous Database Migration Bootcamp 11943 4247 ADB Serverless rodrigo.r.jorge@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed This lab guides users through essential steps for migrating data to Oracle Autonomous Database (ADB), covering how to connect, readiness checks, migration tools, performance analysis, and hands-on data movement exercises using Data Pump over NFS and DB Link methods. This comprehensive lab is designed to provide hands-on experience with migrating on-premises databases to Oracle Autonomous Database (ADB) on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). Participants will develop foundational knowledge of ADB architecture, its core capabilities, and the best practices for secure and efficient migrations. 

The lab begins by demonstrating how to establish secure and reliable connections to ADB, ensuring users are equipped to interact with the cloud database environment. Next, users will perform readiness checks on their existing environments, verifying all prerequisites—such as network connectivity, database and schema requirements, and necessary tools—are in place for a smooth migration.

The lab walks participants through Oracle’s Cloud Migration Analyzer, a utility that scans your source database and offers tailored recommendations on the optimal migration strategy. Users will also measure and evaluate network latency between their systems and ADB to verify adherence to Oracle’s best practices for a successful migration. 

For actual data movement, the lab provides step-by-step guidance on exporting source data using Oracle Data Pump and importing it into ADB, using NFS. In addition, participants will explore migrating data using the DB Link method for direct transfers, giving users practical experience with multiple migration paths. 

After performing data migration tasks, the lab concludes with exercises that teach users how to monitor ADB’s performance, utilize troubleshooting tools, and analyze workload metrics to ensure the migrated environment operates efficiently. 

Throughout the lab, users gain valuable skills in planning, executing, and validating ADB migrations, preparing them for real-world cloud adoption scenarios. AutoREST with JSON Relational Duality Views in ADB 23ai Free Tier 11381 3634 Database animesh.s.sahay@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Complete Enable REST calls with one command on your JSON Relational Duality Views with AutoREST. With Oracle Database 23ai Free Developer Release and the power of Oracle REST Data Service, you can utilize the advantages of relational and document data storage in the same database. JSON Relational Duality is a landmark capability in Oracle Database 23ai that provides game-changing flexibility and simplicity for Oracle Database developers. This breakthrough innovation overcomes the historical challenges that developers have faced when building applications, either when using the relational model or when using the document model.

JSON Relational Duality helps to converge benefits of both document and relational worlds. Developers now get the flexibility and data access benefits of the JSON document model, plus the storage efficiency and power of the relational model. The new feature that enables this convergence is called JSON Relational Duality View.

Interacting with your Oracle Database with HTTPS and REST APIs can be as simple as picking the objects in your database you want to start working with.

Oracle REST Data Service (ORDS) includes a feature known as ‘AutoREST,’ where one or more objects are enabled, and REST API endpoints are automatically published. For example, a TABLE can be enabled for GET, PUT, POST, DELETE operations to get one or more rows, insert or update rows, delete rows, or even batchload multiple rows in a single request. This feature has been enhanced for 23ai to include similar REST access for JSON-Relational duality views. Build a Data Lake with Oracle Autonomous AI Lakehouse 11351 3689 ADB Serverless lauran.serhal@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete With Oracle Autonomous AI Lakehouse, customers can build Data Lakes from scratch or by augmenting existing data warehouse implementations. Data Lakes help customers who want to maximize business output from their data capital. Oracle proudly offers a wide range of database features to help customers to implement the all-data strategy. Data is everywhere stored both locally and on the cloud in different format such as CSV, Parquet, JSON, ORC, Avro, and the new table format that will be available soon such as Iceberg and Delta Share. Although the metadata can stored in different places, Autonomous AI Lakehouse can work with it whether it is stored locally (using PL/SQL,API, and the UI) or in central places in data catalogs (such as OCI DCAT and AWS Glue). AI Lakehouse provides high performance when querying external data at scale. Finally, AI Lakehouse provides multi-language support to process Data Lakes such as SQL, Python, R, and REST.
The labs in this workshop walk you through all the steps that you need to build and access the Data Lake (Oracle Object Storage buckets) using Autonomous AI Lakehouse. First, you set-up the workshop environment and create the necessary resources such as a compartment, an Autonomous AI Lakehouse instance, and Oracle Object Storage resources. Next, evolve object storage files into meaningful business entities by defining the metadata for external data in AI Lakehouse using several methods such as programmatically using PL/SQL scripts, using the Database Actions user interface, or by synchronizing with Data Catalogs (to derive the metadata) such as OCI Data Catalog and AWS Glue. Next, you can gain insights from Data Lakes by querying data that lives in your Oracle AI Lakehouse and combine that with data that is stored in your Oracle Object Storage buckets using regular SQL select statements that includes joined tables. You also move data to Object Storage buckets by exporting your datasets. Finally, you query your data using the SQL Worksheet. Build a Data Pipeline with Big Data Service 11488 3870 Big Data vivek.x.verma@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Completed Building a Data Pipeline using Non-Highly-Available (non-HA) Big Data Service (BDS) and Oracle Analytics Cloud. In this workshop, you'll be guided through the essential steps of building a Data Pipeline using Oracle Big Data Service (BDS). The journey will have you wearing multiple hats, each offering a unique perspective on data handling.

First, as a Data Engineer, you'll tackle the task of cleansing and transforming raw data from Oracle Object Storage. Using Spark, a key feature of our Big Data Service, you'll refine this data and store it in a specific format in an Object Storage bucket. This data will then be placed in an external Hive table. The dataset for this exercise is the well-known Taxi Data Set.

Next, you'll step into the shoes of a Data Scientist. Here, you'll work with a Jupyter notebook, also a part of our service. Your focus will be on building and saving a data model.

This workshop is designed to give you a hands-on experience in the various facets of data processing and analysis, preparing you for the challenges of Big Data.

Finally we'll wear the hat of a Business Analyst where we visualize this data using Oracle Analytics Cloud. records.searchable: Build a Knowledge Graph Layer for Your AI Lakehouse 12160 Database - Spatial and Graph denise.myrick@oracle.com Workshop Completed Build a Knowledge Graph Layer for Your AI Lakehouse explores how to enhance an AI Lakehouse with a knowledge graph layer that adds semantic context to federated data. Learn how to create RDF graphs from structured and unstructured data, connect them with domain ontologies, and enable AI agents to reason more effectively across diverse data sources. AI Lakehouse provides powerful features to federate and query live data in place across multiple data sources, with the security and governance of Autonomous AI Lakehouse. Adding a knowledge graph layer brings a metadata layer of meaning to this data platform, creating richer context for more precise queries. With this layer, AI agents can better reason across data that originates from multiple sources and was created for different uses. In this hands-on lab, learn how to use RDF graph features to create a knowledge layer from structured and unstructured data, link it with domain ontologies, and use standards-based technology to represent meaning and add richer context to your data platform. Build a LLM Slack Bot using OCI 11490 OCI Data Science blake.hendricks@oracle.com Workshop Delete Requested Explore the Oracle Live Lab, where you seamlessly integrate Oracle with a powerful NLP-driven Slack bot. From Oracle setup, Large Language Model integration, Slack connectivity, to bot customization, testing, scalability, and troubleshooting, this hands-on lab guides you through every step, ensuring you use the full potential of NLP in Slack. 1. Setting the Stage:
To begin, we dive deep into the foundational understanding of the Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). Oracle Cloud, renowned for its scalability and flexibility, offers a suite of services that empower developers to build, deploy, and manage applications in a cloud-native manner. With its secure and high-performing computing capabilities, it stands as a choice for developers worldwide. Participants will get hands-on experience in setting up an OCI instance, equipping them with the practical skills required to harness the power of cloud computing.

2. Software Installation and Environment Setup:
A fundamental step in the journey is to prepare our Oracle instance to communicate seamlessly with GPT-3. To achieve this, participants will delve into installing essential software like Python, pip, and other necessary libraries. Step-by-step guidance will ensure even those new to this space feel right at home.

3. Introducing GPT-3:
OpenAI's GPT-3 is a paradigm shift in the domain of AI language models. With 175 billion parameters, its ability to understand context, generate text, and provide relevant responses is unparalleled. Here, we provide an overview of its capabilities, its architecture, and why it's heralded as a game-changer in AI-driven language tasks.

4. Merging Worlds – Oracle Meets GPT-3:
In this exhilarating phase, participants will integrate GPT-3 into their Oracle instance. Leveraging Node.js, we'll construct an API wrapper around GPT-3, transforming our OCI instance into a responsive server ready to generate AI-driven responses. This melding of powerful cloud infrastructure with cutting-edge AI creates a potent tool ready to revolutionize how businesses, developers, and users interact online.

5. Making Bots Alive:
Participants will then be walked through deploying their bots, integrating them with popular platforms like Slack, and ensuring the necessary security configurations are in place. Our bot, now hosted on OCI, will be capable of understanding and responding to prompts, providing intelligent and context-aware interactions.

6. Exploring the Real World:
To cap off our journey, participants will learn how to utilize their bot in real-world scenarios. Whether it's answering customer queries, providing tech support, or engaging users in meaningful conversations, the possibilities are endless. Various test scenarios will provide participants a clear understanding of how their bot behaves and how to refine its responses further.

7. Conclusion and Future Possibilities:
As we wrap up, we'll reflect on the accomplishments and the road ahead. The integration of Oracle Cloud and GPT-3 is just the beginning. The evolving landscape of AI promises even more advanced tools, and with cloud infrastructures like OCI, scaling and deploying them becomes a breeze. Build a Multimodal RAG Pipeline with Oracle Generative AI 11797 AI Services NA Cloud SE Workshop Approved Retrieval Augmented Generation(RAG) is rapidly changing the way enterprises query their data and opening up possibilities for unlocking new insights and better decision making.

In this Livelab, we will build a multimodal RAG pipeline by utilizing Oracle Cloud Infrastructure AI Services and OCI Data Science. Once completed, this will enable you to query your text and image data all the same. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is revolutionizing how enterprises access and leverage their data, transforming unstructured information into actionable insights. By combining retrieval-based techniques with the power of generative AI, RAG enables organizations to query complex datasets, spanning multiple data types, with unprecedented ease and accuracy.

In this LiveLab, you will embark on a hands-on journey to build a fully functional multimodal RAG pipeline. Leveraging Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) AI Services and OCI Data Science, we will demonstrate how to retrieve and process both text and image data seamlessly. This innovative approach allows enterprises to unify their data analysis workflows, enabling queries across diverse formats without the need for manual data transformation or preprocessing.

Through a series of guided steps, you’ll learn how to integrate Oracle’s advanced AI tools, such as AI Vector Search and Generative AI Services, with LLM orchestration techniques. By the end of the session, you will have a robust multimodal RAG pipeline capable of delivering rich, contextually aware responses to queries across text and visual data sources.

Whether you’re looking to enhance decision-making, improve customer support, or drive innovation through AI-powered analytics, this LiveLab will equip you with the foundational skills to harness the full potential of multimodal RAG within your enterprise. Build a Prometheus-Compatible Telemetry Endpoint for Autonomous AI Database Using ORDS 12132 4476 ADB Dedicated vandana.rajamani@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Implement a complete observability pipeline within Oracle Autonomous AI Database on Dedicated Infrastructure, enabling real-time database telemetry to be collected by Prometheus and visualized through Grafana dashboards. Oracle Autonomous AI Database on Dedicated Exadata Infrastructure (Autonomous AI Database) provides access to a rich set of performance and monitoring views, including V$SYSSTAT,V$SYSMETRIC, V$WAITCLASSMETRIC, and many others. However, it does not natively offer a Prometheus-compatible metrics endpoint for external monitoring and observability platforms.

In this workshop, you will learn how to build a custom Prometheus metrics endpoint entirely within the database using Oracle REST Data Services (ORDS), PL/SQL, and the Prometheus exposition format. This approach enables seamless integration of Autonomous AI Database performance metrics with modern monitoring and observability ecosystems.

By the end of this workshop, you will have implemented a complete observability pipeline, enabling real-time database telemetry to be collected by Prometheus and visualized through Grafana dashboards. This solution operates entirely within Oracle Autonomous AI Database, eliminating the need for external agents, exporters, or additional monitoring infrastructure while providing comprehensive visibility into database performance and health. records.searchable: Build A Pure RAG Application with MySQL AI 11963 4266 MySQL perside.foster@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed In this workshop, you will use MySQL Enterprise Edition 9.4.1  or higher with MySQL AI's built-in language models, vector search, and relational capabilities to build a privacy-preserving film recommendation and Q&A application. Compared to traditional RAG pipelines that rely on external providers, MySQL AI keeps data in-database for privacy, cost predictability, and operational control. During this workshop, you'll build a complete application that can answer detailed questions about movies by combining the Sakila film database with MySQL AI-powered embedding and language generation. We'll start by building a standalone chatbot using Claude 4.5 Sonnet as our AI assistant, providing it with predefined prompts to generate the chatbot code based on our specifications. You'll get hands-on experience setting up RAG with MySQL AI capabilities, and we'll leverage preexisting code to quickly deploy and test the finished application. records.searchable: Build A RAG First Responder in Clinical Setting 12031 Database vasile-lucian.brinzei@oracle.com Workshop Approved In this workshop, you will use Oracle AI Database 26ai (SQL) with AI Vector Search, APEX, and OCI Generative AI to build a RAG-powered, chat-first First Responder assistant that performs rapid intake, safe triage/routing, and generates clinician-ready handoff summaries grounded in clinic-approved content. In this workshop, you will build a prototype AI-powered mental health first responder chatbot for a clinical setting using the Oracle stack end-to-end. You’ll store and manage structured intake data in Oracle AI Database 26ai using SQL, and enable AI Vector Search to retrieve relevant, clinic-approved guidance (triage scripts, crisis workflows, policies) to ground the assistant’s responses via a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pattern. You’ll create a secure, low-code chat and intake experience in Oracle APEX, implement orchestration and system-to-system flows with Oracle Integration (e.g., routing to scheduling, case management, or notifications), and optionally leverage OCI OpenSearch for operational search/log analytics and observability of interactions (within your governance model). The workshop emphasizes safe-by-design behavior—crisis escalation triggers, refusal boundaries, and citation/grounding—plus practical testing to reduce hallucinations and ensure privacy, security, and auditability appropriate for sensitive clinical workflows. In this hands-on workshop, learners build RecipeShare, an Android app powered by Oracle Backend for Firebase. This Oracle offering follows the Firebase design, API patterns, and rules-based authorization. In this hands-on workshop, learners build RecipeShare, a SwiftUI iOS app powered by Oracle Backend for Firebase. In this hands-on LiveLabs workshop, you build a modern web application step by step using Oracle Backend for Firebase (Fusabase). records.searchable: Build a RESTful API with MySQL REST Service (MRS) 11483 MySQL Workshop Approved Configure MRS on MySQL Router to bootstrap a RESTful API in minutes to securely expose existing MySQL data to HTTP requests with authentication, pagination, and more! MRS enables fast and secure HTTPS access for your MySQL data. Implemented as a feature on MySQL Router, MRS lets you publish RESTful Web Services for interacting with the data stored in MySQL. Therefore, MRS is the ideal choice for serving JSON Documents to your progressive web apps (PWA) or mobile apps. It also supports popular OAuth2 authentication services and advanced features like row-level security to greatly simplify web app development. In this workshop, we will configure MRS on a local MySQL Router instance using MySQL Shell for VS Code (an extension for the popular code editor Visual Studio Code) to securely expose existing MySQL data to HTTP requests and CRUD operations with authentication and pagination.
