Build a Self-Service, Infrastructure as Code Platform for Oracle Cloud with Pulumi 11643 4037 OCI eli.schilling@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Completed This workshop is designed to accelerate the learning curve for platform engineers and DevOps teams on their journey with Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), leveraging Infrastructure as Code (IaC). Participants will be guided through the steps to customize and deploy Backstage on an OCI Container Instances and to design their first Backstage templates for core OCI services. Platform engineering is all about building consistent, repeatable practices the streamline development and deployment activities across an organization. Oracle Cloud provides an open ecosystem running on next gen compute infrastructure to deliver fast, functional solutions. 

Backstage is an open source framework for building developer portals. Powered by a centralized software catalog, Backstage restores order to your microservices and infrastructure and enables your product teams to ship high-quality code quickly — without compromising autonomy. Backstage unifies all your infrastructure tooling, services, and documentation to create a streamlined development environment from end to end.

Pulumi is an infrastructure-as-code platform for full-stack developers and cloud engineers who are interested in using a general-purpose programming language for their cloud resources. Pulumi isn’t just one thing. It’s an ecosystem of components that all work together.

We'll utilize this collection of best-in-class, open source tools to deploy a self-service portal on OCI that will empower development teams to quickly and easily provision the resources they need to deliver business value. Build a SMART on FHIR Application with Oracle Autonomous Cloud Services 11459 3818 Oracle Health Platform alexandru.basarab@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Explore how to build and deploy a healthcare application using SMART on FHIR with Oracle APEX. In this workshop, you will create a healthcare application where users can calculate the 10-year and lifetime risk of heart attack or stroke. While creating the application you will explore how utilizing APEX and FHIR APIs can accelerate innovations in healthcare and integrate with Millennium Electronic Health Record. Using the data from FHIR APIs, you will implement functionality to calculate and validate chances of heart attack or stroke. Once the calculation and validations are in place you will represent data in a chart with recommendations to reduce the predicted risk.
You will also learn about how providers engage with SMART on FHIR applications by launching the application in Oracle SMART on FHIR public sandbox or as a standalone application. Build Agentic AI Solution with Multi-Tool Capabilities powered by OCI AI Agent Framework 11892 4186 AI Services luke.farley@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Unleash your AI creativity with our LiveLab! Build and deploy intelligent agents using OCI's AI Agent Framework. Train and integrate multiple AI tools to create powerful, interactive agents, all within Oracle Cloud. Get hands-on and revolutionize the way AI assists and interacts! Embark on an exciting journey to build and deploy an agentic AI solution using the Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) AI Agent Framework. In this hands-on LiveLab, you'll explore the power of creating intelligent agents that can revolutionize various industries.
During the lab, you will:
- Understand the fundamentals of the OCI AI Agent Framework and its capabilities.
- Learn how to set up and configure the development environment for building AI agents.
- Create and train an AI agent using natural language processing and machine learning tools provided by OCI.
- Integrate multiple AI tools to enhance the agent's functionality, such as document understanding, llm, and sql queries .
- Deploy and test your agent in a simulated environment, allowing it to interact and respond to user queries.
By the end of this LiveLab, you'll have a solid understanding of building and customizing agentic AI solutions, opening up a world of possibilities for virtual assistants, customer support bots, and smart automation. Get ready to unleash your creativity and harness the power of OCI's AI services.
Remember, this lab is designed to provide a practical, interactive learning experience, so feel free to experiment and explore the potential of agentic AI! Build AI Applications with Oracle Autonomous AI Vector Database and Python 12156 AI/ML Database brian.macdonald@oracle.com Workshop Approved Build AI applications with the Oracle Autonomous AI Vector Database Python SDK for vector search, embeddings, semantic retrieval, and Oracle AI Agent Memory. Autonomous AI Vector Database is a fully managed vector database service that enables developers to quickly build AI-powered applications using Python, REST APIs, and SQL. Built on Oracle Autonomous Database, it combines a simple developer experience with enterprise capabilities such as automated provisioning, scaling, backups, and security.
In this LiveLab, you'll provision an Autonomous AI Vector Database, connect using the Oracle Python SDK, create a vector table, load sample data, and automatically generate vector embeddings. You'll then perform semantic searches using natural language and see how vector search can be combined with metadata filtering to deliver more relevant results.
You'll also integrate Oracle Agent Memory to add conversational memory to your application, enabling it to retain context across interactions and deliver more personalized responses.
By the end of the lab, you'll understand the core workflow for building AI-powered search applications with Autonomous AI Vector Database and see how semantic search and conversational memory work together to create richer AI experiences. Build an Agentic Operations Wingmate with OCI Resource Analytics, Oracle APEX, and OCI Generative AI 11870 4448 AI/ML Database nicholas.cusato@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed This lab guides participants through building an OCI-focused Wingmate using Oracle APEX and Oracle Autonomous AI Database 26ai. It shows how to model tenancy data from synthetic files, REST APIs, and Resource Analytics to deliver natural-language operational and security insights. This lab guides participants through building an OCI-focused Wingmate using Oracle APEX and Oracle Autonomous AI Database 26ai. Rather than a generic data-only use case, the workshop now emphasizes tenancy operations and security insights by combining multiple data sources: synthetic CSV flat files, RESTful APIs, and Oracle Resource Analytics for near real-time infrastructure visibility.

Participants learn how to create a data model and dashboard-driven Wingmate experience in APEX to query tenancy data with natural language, explore operational scenarios, and visualize resource relationships (including graph-based views). The lab supports both Always Free Autonomous AI Database deployments and Resource Analytics-provisioned environments, making it a flexible, practical path for users getting started with AI-assisted operations in OCI. Build an AI Chatbot engine with Oracle AI Database and OCI Generative AI Services 11661 3939 Database bogdan.farca@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed By the end of this tutorial, you’ll understand how to transform raw documents into structured data, store them efficiently, and utilize advanced Large Language Models to generate contextual responses. The main purpose of this workshop is to teach you how you can implement a RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) chatbot using vector similarity search and Generative AI / LLMs.

In today’s data-driven world, effectively managing and utilizing information is crucial for any organization. Whether dealing with customer support data, product documentation, or internal knowledge bases, organizing and retrieving relevant information from vast collections can be challenging. This tutorial demonstrates a comprehensive approach to processing, storing, and leveraging textual data using vectorization and retrieval techniques. By the end of this tutorial, you’ll understand how to transform raw documents into structured data, store them efficiently, and utilize advanced AI models to generate contextual responses. Build an AI Interactive Report in Oracle APEX 12084 4406 APEX ankita.beri@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Configuring interactive reports traditionally requires users to manually define filters, sorting, pivots, aggregates, groupings, and column selections. APEX AI Interactive Reports simplifies this process by allowing users to ask questions in plain language, while APEX automatically translates the request into the appropriate report actions based on the user’s intent. Interactive Reports in Oracle APEX already give end users a rich set of capabilities, including filtering, sorting, control breaks, highlighting, aggregations, charts, groupings, and pivots. These features are powerful and well established, but configuring them traditionally requires moving through multiple menus, dialogs, and report settings. In practice, that means some capabilities are not used as often as they could be because they take time to discover and apply.

APEX AI Interactive Reports changes that experience. Instead of manually configuring a report, users can ask a question in plain language and let APEX translate that request into the right report actions. Based on the intent of the prompt, APEX can apply filters, sorting, pivots, aggregates, groupings, and column selections automatically. Each AI-generated configuration is shown as a visible chip, making the result transparent, reviewable, and easy to refine.

This workshop shows how to use that capability with SCM data. Using a Supply Chain Management application and a replenishment-focused view, you will configure AI support, create an Interactive Report on view named SCM_REPLENISHMENT_V, add report-level and column-level context, and use both Search with AI and the chat assistant to analyze replenishment activity in natural language. Use Generative AI to create your data model, enhance dashboards and forms, integrate REST APIs, implement security, and deliver intelligent experiences with RAG—resulting in a secure, scalable, enterprise-ready application. In this workshop, you will build and enhance a modern, intelligent CRM application using Oracle APEX, combining low-code development, secure architecture, external integrations and AI-powered capabilities. You will use Generative AI to create a complete CRM data model from natural language prompts, accelerate application design, and enhance dashboards, reports, and forms.

By the end, you will have built a secure, scalable, and AI-enabled enterprise CRM application using Oracle APEX. Build an AI Procurement Agent in Oracle APEX 12086 4407 APEX sahaana.manavalan@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed This workshop showcases how AI Agents in Oracle APEX streamline inventory and warehouse management through conversational automation. Users can identify stock shortages, evaluate supplier options, review delivery performance, and create purchase orders quickly without navigating multiple reports, improving supply chain efficiency and decision-making. Managing stock shortages and supplier decisions manually takes time that warehouse teams do not always have. When an item drops below its reorder point and the replenishment alert is already CRITICAL, a warehouse manager needs answers fast: which items are at risk, which suppliers can help, and who has the best delivery record.

AI Agents in Oracle APEX give your application the ability to reason through these questions and act on the answers. Instead of navigating multiple reports and forms, a user can open a chat panel and have a guided conversation. The agent understands who the user is, retrieves the right data, compares options, asks for confirmation, and raises a purchase order, all without leaving the application.

This workshop focuses on the inventory and warehouse management aspects of supply chain: identifying stock shortages, evaluating supplier options, and raising purchase orders through a conversational AI Agent.

In this hands-on workshop, you will build an AI Procurement Agent for the APEX Inventory and Warehouse Management application. You will define tools that allow warehouse managers to identify stock shortages, evaluate suppliers, and raise purchase orders, all from within a conversational chat interface in Oracle APEX.

You will define eight tools using the three tool types available in APEX AI Agents: Retrieve Data, Execute Server-side Code, and Execute Client-side Code. You will also learn when to use each one, all configured declaratively within Oracle APEX. Automate key steps like approvals, task assignments, and notifications. Define user roles, trigger workflow actions, and track progress—streamlining HR operations and enhancing the new hire experience. In this hands-on workshop, you'll learn how to build an Employee Onboarding application using APEX Workflows in Oracle APEX 24.2. The app guides HR teams through essential onboarding steps—such as approval requests, task assignments, and provisioning activities like laptop and induction trainings.

Build and Deploy AI Agents on Exadata with Private Agent Factory and Oracle MCP 12123 ExaCS/ExaCC/DBCS leo.alvarado@oracle.com Workshop In Development Build and deploy an AI agent on Oracle Exadata Database Service in this 90-minute hands-on lab. Use Agent Factory to create an agent, connect it to live data through the Oracle MCP server, leverage Select AI for natural language data access, and build a database diagnostics agent that delivers actionable insights for real-world operations. Ready to move beyond AI demos and build agents that actually work against your enterprise data? In this 90-minute hands-on lab, you’ll go from an empty workspace to a working, deployed AI agent running on Oracle Exadata Database Service.

You’ll start by using Private Agent Factory to rapidly scaffold and configure intelligent agents, then connect them to live data through the Oracle MCP (Model Context Protocol) server the bridge that lets agents securely query, reason over, and act on data inside ExaDB. Along the way you’ll put Select AI to work, using natural language to generate SQL and converse with your data directly in the database, no external pipeline required.

To bring it all together, you’ll build a database diagnostics agent: an agent that monitors database health, investigates performance signals, and surfaces actionable insights showing how agentic AI and Oracle’s converged database combine to solve a real operational problem.

You’ll leave with hands-on experience across the full agent lifecycle build, connect, deploy and a reusable pattern you can take back and apply to your own use cases on Exadata Database Service. Build and Enhance a CRM App Through Spec-Driven Development with AI and APEXlang 12126 4459 APEX apoorva.srinivas@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Build a CRM application faster with Oracle APEX using Spec-Driven Development and APEXlang. In this hands-on workshop, you’ll generate a CRM app from functional specifications using Blueprints, then use natural-language prompts to customize features, automate changes, and manage the application without deep APEX expertise using APEXlang skills. Discover how Oracle APEX is transforming application development with Spec-Driven Development and APEXlang. This hands-on workshop is designed for both experienced APEX developers and newcomers who want to accelerate application delivery using AI-assisted development.

You’ll begin by translating a detailed functional specification into a fully functional CRM application, dramatically reducing the time required to start a new project. After generating the application, you’ll explore how APEXlang lets you interact with your app using natural language to make bulk updates, add new functionality, automate common tasks, and perform tenancy-related operations—all without needing to learn complex APEX syntax or terminology.

By the end of the workshop, you’ll have built and enhanced a CRM application while gaining practical experience with modern, AI-powered development workflows in Oracle APEX. Build Collaborative AI Agents Using Wayflow Libraries and the A2A Protocol for Sales Order Automation 12036 Analytics jadd.jennings@oracle.com Workshop Approved Learn how to design and implement a simple yet expandable collaborative AI agent solution for end-to-end sales order automation using Wayflow libraries, the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol, and the AI Data Platform workbench. The primary agent processes the order, delegates an availability check to a second agent through the AI Data Platform, and then sends a friendly email with the resulting report Design and implement a simple yet expandable collaborative AI agent solution that automates the sales order lifecycle end to end using Wayflow libraries, the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol, and the AI Data Platform. In this solution, a primary “Order Agent” serves as the workflow owner. It ingests an incoming sales order (in this example, an object storage bucket but can also be from a chatbot, email, a web form, or an API), extracts key details such as customer, items, quantities, requested dates, and shipping preferences, and validates that the order is complete and well-formed. The Order Agent then uses the A2A protocol to delegate specialized tasks to other agents—starting with an “Inventory Agent” that checks inventory and fulfillment feasibility through the AI Data Platform. The Inventory Agent returns a structured response, enabling the Order Agent to make a clear decision or request additional information if needed.
Once availability is confirmed (or alternatives are identified), the Order Agent compiles a concise order status report and triggers an email notification to the appropriate stakeholders. The message can include key availability results, expected ship dates, backorder details, and any follow-up questions—ensuring fast, consistent communication and reducing manual effort for sales and operations teams.
The architecture is intentionally modular: each agent has a well-defined responsibility and communicates via A2A using standardized message formats. This makes the solution easy to expand beyond the initial MVP. In addition, the order agent runs as a cloud function while the inventory agent operates as a container instance. Wayflow orchestration supports reliable execution, branching, retries, and observability, while the AI Data Platform provides governed access to enterprise data for accurate, compliant decisions. Simulation software has been used for dynamics system design for a long time. It is single machine design and running. Once the simulation finishes, the model is put on the back burner. Our goal is to leverage these models to deploy it into cloud

Detect anomaly based on history data, continuously learn

Build fast pipelines with the Oracle GoldenGate 23ai Microservices WebUI 11656 3980 GoldenGate Docs Team Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Join this workshop to gain an up-close look at the updated end user experience of Oracle GoldenGate 23ai. See how simple it is to create pipelines and get familiar with new features. Learn how to build fast pipelines both ways by setting up a two-way data replication between East and West cloud databases. This LiveLab session provides an in-depth introduction to the Oracle GoldenGate 23ai user interface and guides you through creating a bidirectional replication.

To simulate redundancy and fault tolerance, we use two distinct GoldenGate installations connected to two separate Oracle Database 23ai instances; one located in the "WEST" region and the other in the "EAST" region.

Build Innovative AI driven application using Generative AI Agents and Oracle APEX 11808 AI Services mohanraj.ilangovan@oracle.com Workshop Approved This workshop is about exploring the integration of Oracle's Generative AI Agent Service with Oracle APEX, and learning how to leverage this powerful combination to build innovative AI-driven applications that drive business value and transformation. Oracle APEX is a leading enterprise low-code application platform that allows users to build scalable, secure web and mobile apps with world-class features, deployable anywhere - cloud or on-premises. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI Agents, on the other hand, combines the power of large language models (LLMs) and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with enterprise data, enabling users to query diverse enterprise knowledge bases through a natural language interface and take direct action on the results. 
In this workshop, participants will delve into the capabilities of both Oracle APEX and GenAI Agent Service, and learn how to integrate them to create innovative applications that leverage the power of AI. Through a hands-on, project-based approach, each attendee will gain a firsthand understanding of how to build a simple yet powerful AI application using this integration, by actively following along with the demonstration of a real-world example and exploring its potential. By the end of the workshop, participants will have developed a working prototype of an AI-driven application and will have gained the knowledge and skills required to apply this integration to their own business challenges and use cases. In this workshop, you build a private vector-search stack in from end to end. You verify runtime services, run two embedding paths, and learn when each one fits best: in-database ONNX for SQL-first simplicity, and Oracle Private AI Services Container for flexible model serving. You generate embeddings, store vectors in Oracle AI Database 26ai, and rank semantic matches with cosine similarity in SQL. You then build a image-search app that uses CLIP text and image embeddings to return the top matches from the database. You finish with working notebooks and practical app code for secure, local embedding generation and retrieval. records.searchable:
Build Self-Sovereign Digital Credentials Solution with Decentralized Identities on Oracle Blockchain Platform 11085 Blockchain mark.rakhmilevich@oracle.com Workshop Approved Decentralized identity puts users back in control of their identity. It returns the control and administration of the identity back to the user with the verifiable assurance based on blockchain protocols and enables users to make verifiable assertions about their identity attributes (claims). This lab will guide the user in implementing Decentralized Id (DIDs) using OBP smart contracts. Centralized approaches to managing identity data — common in today’s market — struggle to provide benefits in the three key areas: Privacy, assurance and pseudonymity. A decentralized approach uses blockchain technology to help ensure privacy, enabling individuals to validate information requests by providing the requestor with only the absolute minimum required amount of information. These are important in the emerging web3 world and Metaverse-linked applications, but DIDs are also starting to permeate into web2 enterprise applications, in areas ranging from finance to supply chain, education, healthcare, etc.

This lab will guide the user in implementing Decentralized Id (DIDs) using OBP smart contracts.  It takes a common use case in Higher Ed - a diploma certification for a graduating student and models decentralized identity process and verified claims related to student's degree awarded by a university.  The lab shows the developer how to model the data to be linked to the DIDs and how to generate the chaincodes in Blockchain App Builder for DID lifecycle leveraging some standard libraries. Once deployed, it then allows users to interact with the DIDs using the lifecycle APIs to create, share, verify DIDs and linked DID Documents.  Then a sample UI app modeling user's wallet will be set up. It will show how individual students can manage their own profile and control data sharing. And how other users acting as issuers (e.g., University administrators) will be able to provide verification of credentials. 

Based on the learning from this lab, developers will be able to implement a similar set of capabilities for many other use cases, e.g., self-sovereign health ID for sharing access to electronic health records, truck driver's credentials shared in a freight transportation marketplace, inspector's credentials in food supply chain, machinists credentials in a manufacturing space and many others. Build Trusted Enterprise RAG Applications with Oracle AI Vector Search 12151 AI/ML Database andy.rivenes@oracle.com Workshop Approved Build a real-world RAG pipeline using Oracle AI Vector Search in Oracle AI Database 26ai, SQL, and Private AI Services Container. Large language models are powerful, but they can't answer questions about your organization's enterprise data without relevant context. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with Oracle AI Vector Search addresses this challenge by retrieving the most relevant information from your enterprise data and grounding LLM responses with that context. 
In this lab, you'll build a real-world RAG pipeline using Oracle AI Vector Search in Oracle AI Database 26ai, SQL, and Private AI Services Container. You'll learn how unstructured documents are transformed into vector embeddings, perform semantic similarity searches over enterprise data, and use the retrieved context to generate accurate, context-aware natural language responses. 
To conclude the session, you'll explore a pre-built Oracle APEX chatbot that uses the same SQL-based retrieval pipeline you built, demonstrating how Oracle AI Vector Search can be integrated into enterprise applications to deliver secure, intelligent conversational experiences. Building a Cost Optimized, High-Throughput HL7, EDI, and FHIR Processing Pipeline on OCI 12155 OCI raghu.iyer@oracle.com Workshop In Development Build a scalable, event-driven healthcare data processing pipeline on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) for HL7, EDI, and FHIR workloads using serverless services, streaming, and Kubernetes. Healthcare organizations must process millions of HL7, EDI, and FHIR transactions while maintaining high availability, scalability, security, and cost efficiency. This workshop demonstrates how to build a modern healthcare interoperability pipeline on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) using an event-driven architecture.

Participants will deploy and explore a reference architecture that ingests healthcare transactions from multiple sources, processes them using Oracle Integration for Healthcare, OCI Functions, OCI Streaming, and Oracle Kubernetes Engine (OKE), and stores transaction data in OCI Object Storage for downstream analytics and compliance. The workshop also highlights OCI capabilities that improve performance and optimize infrastructure costs, including flexible compute shapes, Kubernetes autoscaling, serverless orchestration, and intelligent storage lifecycle management.

By the end of this workshop, participants will understand how to design highly scalable, resilient, and cost-effective healthcare integration solutions using OCI native services and industry-standard healthcare messaging formats. records.searchable:
Building a Modular OCI Landing Zone with Modules 11991 OCI kc.flynn@oracle.com Workshop Approved Learn how to assemble a small, non-production OCI Landing Zone using individual Core Landing Zone modules. You’ll discover where to get the modules, select a subset, configure variables via JSON, and read module outputs to supply required inputs for later modules—all from the Terraform/OpenTofu CLI. This intermediate, hands-on lab teaches you how to build a partial, non-production OCI Landing Zone using individual Core Landing Zone modules from the command line. Instead of deploying the monolithic Core Landing Zone or using the Landing Zone Orchestrator, you will work directly with a targeted subset of modules—IAM, Networking, and Tagging—to understand how the building blocks fit together and how to configure them reliably with JSON variable files and version pins. 

You will learn where to obtain the official modules, how to select only those required for a small-scale environment, and how to structure a simple, repeatable workspace for Terraform or OpenTofu. After each module apply, you will read the module’s outputs (for example, compartment OCIDs, VCN and subnet OCIDs, and tag namespace OCIDs) and manually use those values as inputs when configuring subsequent modules. This deliberate, manual handoff is designed to build confidence in interpreting outputs and understanding module boundaries before you progress to orchestration. 

The lab emphasizes practical, day-to-day skills: 

    Discover and pin module versions for reproducibility.
    Author clean, consistent JSON variable files and apply baseline naming/tagging conventions.
    Maintain an “outputs journal” so you can accurately reuse IDs/OCIDs across modules.
    Validate plans/applies, interpret common errors, and verify that resources land in the correct compartments with the expected tags and network reachability.
    Clean up in the right order (networking before IAM/compartments) to avoid dependency issues and stray costs.
     

By the end, you will have a minimal Landing Zone composed of a compartment structure with baseline policies, one VCN with public/private subnets and essential gateways/route tables/NSGs, and a tag namespace with defined tags applied to resources. The result is not production-ready; it is a clear, reproducible demonstration of the modular approach that prepares you to scale up and later adopt the Landing Zone Orchestrator. If you elect to use OpenTofu or other third-party tooling, ensure alignment with Oracle’s internal security and compliance guidelines. Building a weather chatbot with Oracle Digital Assistant 11443 3922 OCI ramona.magadan@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Completed Explore how to use Oracle Digital Assistant to develop a chatbot that provides real-time weather forecast information for any location specified by the user. In this 5-labs workshop, we will explore how to use Oracle Digital Assistant to develop a chatbot that provides real-time weather forecast information for any location specified by the user.

Chatbots have become an essential tool in user interactions, and in this workshop, we will focus on harnessing the capabilities of Oracle Digital Assistant to build an intelligent and personalized chatbot. Oracle Digital Assistant combines artificial intelligence and natural language processing to create effective and contextual conversation experiences.

In this workshop, you will learn how to:
* Oracle Digital Assistant instance provisioning
* Create an Skill and Intents and Entities definition
* Dialog flow implementation
* Consuming a REST API
* Exposing your chatbot in a website

By the end of this workshop, you will have the knowledge to create a chatbot using Oracle Digital Assistant that provides up-to-date weather forecast information for any location. 

We are excited to embark on this journey of creating intelligent and efficient chatbots together! - Intelligent multi-agent collaboration using LangChain

Building AI Applications with OCI Generative AI Service in Visual Studio Code 12087 4427 MySQL lohith.r@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Build an AI-powered eCommerce web application using OCI Generative AI Services, Visual Studio Code, and MySQL HeatWave. In this hands-on workshop, participants will use prompts to integrate OCI AI models into applications and leverage HeatWave’s native AI and vector capabilities to create intelligent, scalable, and data-driven shopping experiences. Discover how to build intelligent, AI-powered applications using Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI Services, Visual Studio Code, and MySQL HeatWave. In this hands-on workshop, participants will develop a modern eCommerce web application enhanced with generative AI capabilities, demonstrating how AI can transform customer experiences and application workflows.

The workshop introduces developers to prompt-driven application development using enterprise-grade OCI AI models directly from Visual Studio Code. Participants will learn how to integrate OCI Generative AI APIs into web applications, design effective prompts, and build interactive AI-powered features such as product recommendations, conversational shopping assistants, content generation, product search, and personalized user experiences.

In addition to OCI Generative AI Services, the workshop highlights the power of MySQL HeatWave and its native AI capabilities, including vector storage, semantic search and AI-driven data processing. Attendees will gain practical experience combining structured application data with AI-enhanced search and recommendation workflows to build scalable, intelligent applications.

Throughout the session, participants will:

* Set up and configure OCI Generative AI Services
* Use Visual Studio Code for AI-assisted development workflows
* Integrate prompts and AI model inference into web applications
* Connect applications with MySQL HeatWave
* Explore HeatWave’s native AI and vector capabilities
* Build and test AI-powered eCommerce features end-to-end

By the end of the workshop, participants will have a functional AI-enabled eCommerce application and a strong understanding of how OCI Generative AI Services and MySQL HeatWave can be used together to accelerate modern AI application development. Building an AI-Powered Banking Insights Application with Oracle 23ai ADB, APEX and VPD 11937 ADB Serverless jibin.panicker@oracle.com Workshop More Info Needed Discover how to create an AI-driven banking insights application using Oracle 23ai ADB and APEX, secured with Virtual Private Database (VPD) policies. Enable two users—one with elevated privileges and one with limited access—to query banking data using natural language and vector-based recommendations, while enforcing strict access controls. In this hands-on workshop, participants will build an "AI-Powered Banking Insights Application" using Oracle 23ai Autonomous Database (ADB) and Oracle Application Express (APEX), secured with Virtual Private Database (VPD) policies to enforce fine-grained access control. The application enables two user types—a privileged user (bank_manager) with full access to sensitive customer and loan data, and a restricted user (bank_staff) limited to public service data—to interact with banking insights via natural language queries (e.g., "Show me customers with credit scores above 700") and AI-driven vector search for personalised recommendations.
Key features include:
Database Setup: Create tables under the admin schema, with vector columns.
AI Integration: Configure AI PROFILE using DBMS_CLOUD_AI for natural language processing and with an in-database ONNX model for vector embeddings, enabling Select AI functionality.
Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Implement secure access
VPD Security: Use VPD policies to enforce row-level security, ensuring unauthorised users cannot access sensitive data.
APEX Application: Develop an APEX application supporting database authentication for manager and staff.
The application includes:
Banking Insights Dashboard (for bank_manager): Query sensitive data with natural language (e.g., credit scores, loan eligibility).
Service Queries Page (for both users): Access service-related data with restricted access for bank_staff.
Recommendations Page (for bank_manager): Provide AI-driven loan recommendations using vector search. Building and Deploying a Spring Boot App with PostgreSQL on OCI using GitHub Actions 11994 4335 OCI maria.danescu@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Learn how to build, containerize, and deploy a real Spring Boot application backed by PostgreSQL on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). This hands-on workshop walks you through setting up OCI services, configuring PostgreSQL, building Docker images, pushing them to OCI Container Registry, and automating your CI/CD pipeline with GitHub Actions for smooth, repeatable deployments. Learn how to build, containerize, and deploy a production-ready Spring Boot application using PostgreSQL on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). In this hands-on workshop, you will go step-by-step through the entire lifecycle of a modern cloud-native application—from code to deployment—using industry-best practices and fully automated pipelines.

You will start by setting up the required OCI services, including networking components, compartments, and access credentials. Then, you will provision and configure a managed PostgreSQL database and connect your Spring Boot application to it using secure environment variables. 

Building on this foundation, you will learn how to use GitHub Actions to automate every stage of your CI/CD pipeline. The workflow will check out your source code, install JDK 17, build your Spring Boot JAR, create and push a Docker image to OCIR, and finally deploy your application on OCI using OCI Container Instances. You will explore how the deployment process dynamically discovers the correct availability domain, generates the necessary JSON payloads for container, VNIC, and compute shape configurations, and launches a fully functional container instance with public network access.

By the end of the workshop, you will have a fully automated pipeline that builds, packages, stores, and deploys your Spring Boot application on Oracle Cloud—with each new push to the main branch triggering a fresh deployment. You will understand how your application connects to PostgreSQL through configurable environment variables, how container port mappings are defined, and how all components work together for smooth and repeatable cloud deployments.

This workshop is ideal for developers, DevOps engineers, and cloud practitioners who want a practical, end-to-end understanding of deploying containerized Java applications on OCI using modern CI/CD automation tools. Building Great APEX Grids 11438 APEX Oracle Partner Workshop Approved Learn how to build feature-rich, custom, consistent user-friendly APEX interactive grids to meet data display and edit requirements across your organization. Learn how to maximize use of APEX Interactive Grids to meet most any data presentation and edit requirement and keep you end users happy across your enterprise.  This workshop will teach you how to leverage interactive grid declarative and customization features to meet all of your business needs, then walk you through steps  to standardize your settings and customization to minimize coding effort, maximize efficiency and ensure consistency across all interactive grids in all your applications.  

You will generate an APEX application that includes an interactive grid. You will enable Edit mode in that grid, and explore various declarative settings to control who is allowed to edit, which rows are editable and which columns are editable. Next you will explore and build alternate views of the data: Group By, Icon, Detail and Chart, and setting default and alternate data views. You will explore various types of charts, and learn how to disable chart types that do not apply to your data set. You will learn to customize column settings, declaratively and by code, to control what users are able to do (or not) with each column. You explore declarative toolbar configuration settings.  You will next define and implement several custom grid view toolbar and action menu configurations.  You will explore the interaction of declarative and custom toolbar configuration settings. Finally you will set up a standard grid customization file to enable easy, declarative implementation of your custom toolbar configurations  across multiple grids on multiple pages in multiple applications.  The principles you learn in this lab are readily adaptable to your own interactive grids. records.searchable: Building Intelligent APEX Apps with OCI Gen AI and Your Oracle Data 11940 4255 APEX karol.stuart@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed This hands-on Oracle LiveLab introduces developers to the future of application development using Oracle APEX and OCI Generative AI. Learn how to create intelligent apps that understand user intent and deliver value from your Oracle data with minimal code. Are you looking to take advantage of your existing Oracle data to create intelligent applications with Generative AI? In this hands-on Oracle LiveLab, you’ll combine the power and ease of Oracle APEX with cutting-edge OCI Generative AI services. Building REST APIs to Insert Data to your Oracle Tables 11013 Developers - Database jeff.d.smith@oracle.com Workshop Approved Create a table, build REST APIs to POST up new records, and GET the data back out - including JSON! This is a comprehensive example showing how to insert and retrieve data from a table - via REST APIs. But our table will use an IDENTITY column for the primary key, and will include a LOB for storing JSON documents alongside your relational data (the power of the Converged Database!). 

Our APIs will know how to: 
 + work with IDENTITY columns
 + grab new column values off POST Request header AND body
 + catching exceptions and avoiding HTTP 500’s
 + acquiring the new primary key value from the inserted row
 + changing the status from 200 to 201 to reflect a successful insert 
 + forwarding the requestor to the new row (item) in the response
 + properly formatting JSON in our responses
 + catching errors in our database code logic and avoiding HTTP 500 responses Individual author Individual Content to review/remove Missing LiveLabs ID in current WMS export; review as a draft or unpublished row 11013 Workshop Approved Developers - Database 2022-05-18 2022-06-02 Individual author Individual No Repository Url 11013 Workshop Approved Developers - Database 2022-05-18 2022-06-02 Individual author Individual No Repository Url No repository URL is present in the current WMS export. jeff.d.smith@oracle.com Create a table, build REST APIs to POST up new records, and GET the data back out - including JSON! Building Your First CICD Project On OCI with ADB 11759 OCI ashu.kumar@oracle.com Workshop Approved Learn to build CICD Project On OCI from the ground up. This hands-on workshop covers project creation, code repository setup, Kubernetes cluster deployment, Autonomous Database configuration, build and deploy pipelines, and accessing your application. Follow step-by-step instructions to set up an OKE cluster, create a build pipeline, and deploy a sample Todo App with live monitoring. Join our in-depth workshop to master creating CICD Project On OCI from scratch. This session will guide you through each essential step:

1. Create a Project: Start by setting up a new OCI project through the OCI console.
   
2. Set Up Code Repository: Configure your code repository and download the Todo App code sample.

3. Deploy Kubernetes Cluster: Use the wizard to create an Oracle Kubernetes Engine (OKE) cluster with default settings.

4. Create an Autonomous Database: Set up an Autonomous Database with default configurations. Download and replace the wallet, upload sample data, and update the configuration file.

5. Build Pipeline Creation: 
   - Name your Build Pipeline.
   - Add stages to create and push Docker images and Kubernetes manifests.
   - Configure artifacts for Docker images and Kubernetes manifests, linking them to build results.

6. Environment Setup: Define an Oracle Kubernetes Engine environment for use in the deploy pipeline.

7. Deploy Pipeline Creation:
   - Name your Deploy Pipeline.
   - Add a stage to apply Kubernetes manifests.
   - Configure the pipeline to use the previously created OKE environment and cluster.

8. Trigger Deployment: Link your Build Pipeline to the Deploy Pipeline to automate deployment triggers.

9. Run and Monitor: Execute the Build Pipeline manually, monitor both the build and deploy processes to ensure successful execution.

10. Access the Application:
    - Retrieve your application’s URL from the OKE cluster details.
    - Use Cloud Shell to access and monitor Kubernetes resources.
    - Copy the LoadBalancer’s External IP, append port 5000, and browse to view your deployed Todo App.

Perfect for those looking to gain practical skills in OCI environments. Join our in-depth workshop to master creating CICD Project On OCI from scratch. This session will guide you through each essential step:

1. Create a Project: Start by setting up a new OCI project through the OCI console.
   
2. Set Up Code Repository: Configure your code repository and download the Todo App code sample.

3. Deploy Kubernetes Cluster: Use the wizard to create an Oracle Kubernetes Engine (OKE) cluster with default settings.

4. Create an Autonomous Database: Set up an Autonomous Database with default configurations. Download and replace the wallet, upload sample data, and update the configuration file.

5. Build Pipeline Creation: 
   - Name your Build Pipeline.
   - Add stages to create and push Docker images and Kubernetes manifests.
   - Configure artifacts for Docker images and Kubernetes manifests, linking them to build results.

6. Environment Setup: Define an Oracle Kubernetes Engine environment for use in the deploy pipeline.

7. Deploy Pipeline Creation:
   - Name your Deploy Pipeline.
   - Add a stage to apply Kubernetes manifests.
   - Configure the pipeline to use the previously created OKE environment and cluster.

8. Trigger Deployment: Link your Build Pipeline to the Deploy Pipeline to automate deployment triggers.

9. Run and Monitor: Execute the Build Pipeline manually, monitor both the build and deploy processes to ensure successful execution.

10. Access the Application:
    - Retrieve your application’s URL from the OKE cluster details.
    - Use Cloud Shell to access and monitor Kubernetes resources.
    - Copy the LoadBalancer’s External IP, append port 5000, and browse to view your deployed Todo App.

This workshop introduces the foundational elements of Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) networking. After you set up the environment, the workshop explores how VMs communicate both within the VCN or with any external network. You will configure route tables, apply security rules, and examine the role of all relevant OCI gateways in enabling or restricting connectivity, whether for outbound internet access or internal communication.

During the workshop, you will create:
- A Virtual Cloud Network (VCN).
- Two Subnets: one public and one private.
- Network Gateways: IGW, NAT, and SGW.
- Two Linux Compute Instances. CD3 Automation Toolkit 11407 3724 OCI dipesh.rathod@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA This workshop will help to deploy OCI resources using CD3 Automation toolkit. It has been developed to help in automating the OCI resource object management. The toolkit also reverse engineers the components in OCI back to the Excel sheet and Terraform configuration. This generated Terraform code can be used by the OCI Resource Manager or leveraged by the organization's CI/CD processes. The Automation toolkit has been developed to help in automating the public cloud resource management. The toolkit reads information from input design document and produces IaaC artifacts. 

The CD3 Automation toolkit is a processor that converts the detailed OCI design spec into executable Terraform code, or takes an export of OCI tenancy objects and resources, and converts it back into a design spec.

It is developed based on enterprise level framework and concepts.
- Dynamic Tenancy Generator
- Cloud Infra Lifecycle Orchestrator
- Declarative Approach - Focus on Secure Design
- Inbuilt Intelligence
- DevOps Oriented

It is also available on GitHub repository if you would like to deploy by yourself in your tenancy.

records.searchable: Centralize Cloud Operations and Automation with OCI Fleet Application Management 11932 4231 OCI bhumika.v.bhagia@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Automate provisioning, patching, and software compliance at scale across your OCI environment — all from a single control plane. As organizations scale their presence on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), managing patching, provisioning, and compliance across a diverse set of resources becomes increasingly complex. OCI Fleet Application Management solves this challenge by providing a centralized platform to automate and govern cloud operations at scale, reducing manual effort while improving consistency and security. Classify X-Ray Images for Pneumonia using Analytics Cloud and Vision AI Services 11301 3576 Community ramona.magadan@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Author: Žiga Vaupot, Oracle ACE Pro - Business Intelligence, Qubix.

Explore organizing image library in object storage for image classification. Author: Žiga Vaupot, Oracle ACE Pro - Business Intelligence, Qubix


Vision is a self-service AI Service within OCI, which applies computer vision to analyze image-based content. It allows developers easily integrate pre-trained models into their applications with APIs or custom training models to meet their specific use cases. In this workshop, we will explore how to use Vision AI service to create a custom-built model to detect pneumonia infected lungs on a fresh dataset of X-ray images. Oracle Analytics is then used as a front-end tool to use the model to classify new images for pneumonia. 

What to expect to see in this workshop? In the first place, we will demonstrate and explore the whole process from “plain” X-ray image to identifying pneumonia infected lungs using OCI services:
• Gathering and storing images to OCI Object Storage.
• Labeling images depending on whether they represent normal or pneumonia infected lungs using Data Labeling service.
• Building and training an image classification model using OCI Vision.
• Registering an OCI Vision model with Oracle Analytics.
• Applying a model in Oracle Analytics’ Data Flows. 
• Visualizing everything at the end by using Oracle Analytics Data Visualization.

Why is this relevant? Firstly, it shows the flexibility and usability of the OCI ecosystem, specifically Data Lakehouse services. Secondly, the whole process (with exception of data labeling which is done programmatically) is code-less, with not too many steps in the process, and the process itself is really very simple to use. This implies possibilities which can be explored by much wider range of users comparing to the situation today, where all depends on skilled developers and data scientists. And the bottom line, this can have very positive impact on business. CloudBank - Modern banking with a 2-Tier microservices architecture 11084 3617 Developers - Converged doug.drechsel@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Completed CloudBank is a financial services sample application implementing parts of a banking and insurance workflow, with the converged Oracle database. It highlights the simplicity of a 2-tier architecture with a mobile front-end and back-end as a service using application services in the database. CloudBank is a financial services sample application implementing parts of a banking and insurance workflow, with the converged Oracle database. It hightlights the simplified 2-tier architecture with a mobile front-end and back-end as a service using application services in the database.
CloudBank is a multcloud sample app that runs where the Oracle database runs, showing microservices implementation with security, data integrity, unified observability, and a rich yet simple user interface. Workflows will showcase samples for retail and corporate core banking platforms. using auto insurance, health insurance, as examples for fraud detection and anti-money laundering services. 
The application will be built in the 2-tier architecture style with a mobile UI in React Native, and a BaaS (with Parse Platform) to work with Oracle SQL and MongoDB APIs. records.searchable: Code Less, Do More: Accelerate App Development with MySQL 11907 4207 MySQL sindhuja.banka@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Learn how to build modern apps faster with MySQL. This workshop covers MySQL REST Services for HTTP data access, JSON, Full-Text Search, Encryption, Compression, and JavaScript Stored Procedures. See how to integrate with Java/Python apps and build low-code solutions using Oracle APEX with MySQL REST endpoints. Discover how MySQL can help you build modern applications faster and with less effort. In this session, you’ll learn how to create and deploy RESTful applications using MySQL REST Services for seamless data access over HTTP. We’ll explore key MySQL features such as JSON support, Full-Text Search, Encryption, and Compression to help you develop secure and flexible solutions. You’ll also learn how to use JavaScript Stored Procedures to add server-side logic and integrate MySQL with full-stack applications using Java and Python connectors. Finally, explore how to rapidly build low-code apps with Oracle APEX using MySQL REST Services endpoints. Configure Hub-and-Spoke Routing for a Standalone Palo Alto NGFW in OCI 12166 OCI iwan.hoogendoorn@oracle.com Workshop In Development Learn how to steer traffic through a standalone Palo Alto Networks VM-Series firewall in an OCI Hub-and-Spoke topology. It covers nine North-South and East-West routing scenarios: public application access with a Load Balancer, central outbound Internet access with NAT, GlobalProtect remote access, Service Gateway placement, intra-VCN and spoke-to-spoke inspection, and hybrid IPSec VPN. In a real Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) environment, a Palo Alto Networks VM-Series firewall rarely sits alone. It is deployed into a Hub-and-Spoke topology where the workloads live in spoke VCNs and the firewall sits in the hub, inspecting every flow that crosses a VCN, subnet, or zone boundary. Getting that design right is a routing problem more than a security one: get the routes right and the firewall sees every packet you want it to see, get them wrong and traffic either bypasses the firewall entirely or never reaches its destination at all.

This workshop is the final part of the Palo Alto Networks in OCI series. The earlier parts focused on deploying and configuring the firewall itself. This part shifts the focus to routing and end-to-end connectivity around a standalone (single instance) firewall deployment.

You will work through nine routing scenarios, each with its own use case, traffic flow, OCI route table configuration, matching PAN-OS virtual router configuration, and a validation step:

North-South scenarios cover a public Application Load Balancer with a WAF policy placed in front of the firewall; the firewall placed in front of a private Application Load Balancer with destination NAT; centralized outbound Internet access for spoke workloads with source NAT; and remote user access through GlobalProtect VPN with split-tunnel routing.

East-West scenarios cover a centralized Service Gateway in the hub with full firewall inspection of Oracle Services Network traffic; distributed Service Gateways in each spoke that bypass inspection; subnet-to-subnet traffic inside a single spoke VCN forced through the firewall; spoke-to-spoke traffic between two VCNs routed through the firewall; and hybrid connectivity over an IPSec VPN between the firewall in one OCI region and an OCI native Dynamic Routing Gateway in another.

Along the way you will apply the Hub-and-Spoke design guidelines that make these topologies predictable and debuggable: a dedicated hub VCN for shared services, one subnet per firewall interface, per-spoke DRG attachments with DRG route tables, DRG import route distributions so the hub learns spoke CIDRs dynamically, and DRG attachment ingress route tables that keep return traffic symmetric instead of short-circuiting back and breaking the connection.

The workshop uses specific routes in the spokes rather than a blanket default route to the hub, so that every flow you build is explicit and traceable. The centralized-egress alternative (0.0.0.0/0 to the hub) is explained where it applies, so you can choose the model that fits your production environment.

Although this workshop targets the standalone deployment, the same routing patterns apply to the Active/Passive and Active/Active deployments covered in the companion workshops. Only the route target changes. records.source: 14 August 2026 WMS and LiveLabs dashboard views; 15 August 2026 GitHub repository census
records.searchable:
Configure Hub-and-Spoke Routing for an Active/Active Palo Alto NGFW Deployment in OCI 12168 OCI iwan.hoogendoorn@oracle.com Workshop In Development Learn how to steer traffic through an Active/Active Palo Alto Networks VM-Series deployment fronted by OCI Network Load Balancers in a Hub-and-Spoke topology. This workshop covers the same nine North-South and East-West routing scenarios as the standalone workshop, with every flow routed to a Trust or Untrust NLB and designed for session symmetry across both firewalls. In an Active/Active Palo Alto Networks VM-Series deployment in Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), both firewalls process traffic at the same time and neither one owns the data path. OCI route rules therefore point at a Network Load Balancer (NLB) rather than at a firewall interface: an Untrust NLB for traffic entering from the Internet side, and a Trust NLB for traffic entering from the workload side. The NLB operates at Layer 4 and preserves the original source and destination addresses, which is what makes stateful inspection on the firewalls possible in the first place.

That design buys horizontal scale, but it introduces the hardest requirement in Hub-and-Spoke firewall routing: session symmetry. A session must land on the same firewall in both directions, because neither firewall holds the other's session state. Every route rule, every NLB listener, and every backend set in this workshop is built with that constraint in mind, and each scenario ends with a validation step that proves the flow is symmetric rather than merely working.

This workshop is the Active/Active variant of the final part of the Palo Alto Networks in OCI series. The earlier parts covered deploying the two firewall instances and the Trust and Untrust NLBs that front them. This part shifts the focus to routing and end-to-end connectivity around that pair.

You will work through nine routing scenarios, each with its own use case, traffic flow, OCI route table configuration, matching PAN-OS virtual router configuration on both firewalls, and a validation step.

North-South scenarios cover a public Application Load Balancer with a WAF policy placed in front of the Untrust NLB; the firewalls placed in front of a private Application Load Balancer with destination NAT; centralized outbound Internet access for spoke workloads with source NAT; and remote user access through GlobalProtect VPN terminated behind a dedicated VPN NLB, with split-tunnel routing.

East-West scenarios cover a centralized Service Gateway in the hub with full firewall inspection of Oracle Services Network traffic; distributed Service Gateways in each spoke that bypass inspection; subnet-to-subnet traffic inside a single spoke VCN forced through the firewalls; spoke-to-spoke traffic between two VCNs routed through the firewalls; and hybrid connectivity over an IPSec VPN between the OCI region hosting the firewalls and an OCI native Dynamic Routing Gateway in another region.

Because an Active/Active deployment has no configuration synchronization, you will also learn where duplicate configuration is required on the second firewall, and how to keep the two members consistent as the topology grows. Finally, you will remove one firewall from service and confirm that the NLB health checks steer new sessions to the surviving member and that the topology continues to inspect every flow you designed it to inspect. Learn how to steer traffic through an Active/Active Palo Alto Networks VM-Series deployment fronted by OCI Network Load Balancers in a Hub-and-Spoke topology. This workshop covers the same nine North-South and East-West routing scenarios as the standalone workshop, with every flow routed to a Trust or Untrust NLB and designed for session symmetry across both firewalls.

In an Active/Active Palo Alto Networks VM-Series deployment in Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), both firewalls process traffic at the same time and neither one owns the data path. OCI route rules therefore point at a Network Load Balancer (NLB) rather than at a firewall interface: an Untrust NLB for traffic entering from the Internet side, and a Trust NLB for traffic entering from the workload side. The NLB operates at Layer 4 and preserves the original source and destination addresses, which is what makes stateful inspection on the firewalls possible in the first place.

That design buys horizontal scale, but it introduces the hardest requirement in Hub-and-Spoke firewall routing: session symmetry. A session must land on the same firewall in both directions, because neither firewall holds the other's session state. Every route rule, every NLB listener, and every backend set in this workshop is built with that constraint in mind, and each scenario ends with a validation step that proves the flow is symmetric rather than merely working.

Configure Hub-and-Spoke Routing for an Active/Passive Palo Alto NGFW HA Pair in OCI 12167 OCI iwan.hoogendoorn@oracle.com Workshop In Development Learn how to steer traffic through an Active/Passive Palo Alto Networks VM-Series HA pair in an OCI Hub-and-Spoke topology. This workshop covers the same nine North-South and East-West routing scenarios as the standalone workshop, but routes every flow to the floating secondary IP addresses so that traffic follows the active firewall automatically after a failover. An Active/Passive Palo Alto Networks VM-Series HA pair changes one thing about Hub-and-Spoke routing in Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), and it changes it everywhere: the route target. OCI route rules cannot point at "whichever firewall is active" — they point at a private IP. In an Active/Passive design that IP is a secondary (floating) IP address on the data VNICs, which PAN-OS moves from the failed member to the surviving member during a failover. Every route rule in the topology must target that floating IP rather than a primary interface IP, or the design will survive a lab test and break during a real failover.

This workshop is the Active/Passive variant of the final part of the Palo Alto Networks in OCI series. The earlier parts covered deploying the HA pair itself, including the HA1 control link, the HA2 data link, the floating secondary IPs, and the IAM policy that allows the firewall to move those IPs between instances. This part shifts the focus to routing and end-to-end connectivity around that pair.

You will work through nine routing scenarios, each with its own use case, traffic flow, OCI route table configuration, matching PAN-OS virtual router configuration, and a validation step.

North-South scenarios cover a public Application Load Balancer with a WAF policy placed in front of the HA pair; the HA pair placed in front of a private Application Load Balancer with destination NAT; centralized outbound Internet access for spoke workloads with source NAT; and remote user access through GlobalProtect VPN with split-tunnel routing.

East-West scenarios cover a centralized Service Gateway in the hub with full firewall inspection of Oracle Services Network traffic; distributed Service Gateways in each spoke that bypass inspection; subnet-to-subnet traffic inside a single spoke VCN forced through the firewall; spoke-to-spoke traffic between two VCNs routed through the firewall; and hybrid connectivity over an IPSec VPN between the HA pair in one OCI region and an OCI native Dynamic Routing Gateway in another.

Each scenario adds a failover validation step. You will confirm that the session survives, or fails and re-establishes as designed, when the active member is taken out of service, and you will inspect the session table on the newly active member to prove that state synchronization over the HA2 link is doing its job.

Along the way you will apply the Hub-and-Spoke design guidelines that make these topologies predictable and debuggable: a dedicated hub VCN for shared services, one subnet per firewall interface including the dedicated HA subnet, per-spoke DRG attachments with DRG route tables, DRG import route distributions so the hub learns spoke CIDRs dynamically, and DRG attachment ingress route tables that keep return traffic symmetric. Configure LDAP on ExaCC Gen2 with Example 5421 ExaCS/ExaCC/DBCS howard.zheng@oracle.com Workshop Approved This purpose of this lab is to provide detailed steps on how to integrate ExaCC with existing LDAP configuration for authentication to ExaCC. The Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) is an open, vendor-neutral, industry standard application protocol for accessing and maintaining distributed directory information services over an Internet Protocol (IP) network. A common use of LDAP is to provide a central place to store usernames and passwords. This allows many different applications and services to connect to the LDAP server to validate users.

ExaCC is able to leverage existing LDAP configuration for user authentication. This document provides the detailed steps on the necessary configurations that will be need to integrate ExaCC with LDAP to allow users to authenticate access using their LDAP credentials. Connect Oracle Agent Factory to Oracle APEX 12072 4397 Other - I don't see it lavkesh.singh@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed This workshop turns a step-by-step implementation blog into a guided LiveLabs flow. You will publish an Oracle AI Database Private Agent Factory agent, inspect the integration endpoint, understand the session-cookie requirement, bridge the private backend with OCI API Gateway, and wire Oracle APEX PL/SQL to start and continue agent conversations without manual cookie handling. This LiveLabs workshop walks learners through the complete end-to-end process of connecting Oracle AI Database Private Agent Factory (PAF) to Oracle APEX using OCI API Gateway, APEX Web Credentials, and PL/SQL. Learners begin by publishing a working agent in Agent Factory, capturing the integration endpoint, and understanding the two core challenges in the integration: the browser-based session cookie required by PAF and the private-network, self-signed SSL setup that prevents a straightforward direct call from APEX. The workshop then shows how OCI API Gateway can be configured as the bridge between APEX and the private backend, including the required login and agent routes and the SSL verification settings needed for this pattern to work.

After the gateway is in place, learners move into Oracle APEX and implement the full server-side integration flow. They create secure Web Credentials for storing login information, build PL/SQL logic to fetch a fresh agent_factory_session cookie automatically, initialize a room for the conversation, and send user messages to the published agent through the gateway. They also learn how to parse NDJSON responses returned by the service and return those responses cleanly back into the APEX application. By the end of the workshop, participants will have a practical, production-oriented blueprint for integrating Oracle Agent Factory with Oracle APEX without relying on manual cookie copy-paste steps, while also understanding the architectural decisions, security considerations, and operational flow behind the solution. The workshop concludes with a knowledge-check lab to reinforce the concepts and implementation details. Connecting to Oracle NoSQL Database 11945 4309 NoSQL purnima.subramanian@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed This workshop is designed to help you quickly get started with developing applications using Oracle NoSQL Database. It shows the different methods by which your application can connect to the database and perform simple operations on it. This workshop is designed to help you quickly get started with developing applications using Oracle NoSQL Database. It shows the different methods by which your application can connect to the database and perform simple operations on it.
Oracle NoSQL Database offers various methods by which your application can access the database:
•	Using Integrated Development Environments (IDEs):
You can use integrated development environments to connect to the Oracle NoSQL database and develop your applications efficiently. Oracle NoSQL Database plugins are available for Microsoft Visual Studio Code and IntelliJ IDEs.

•	Using Software Development Kits (SDKs):
You can use the SDKs available in different programming languages to develop your applications. These SDKs enable applications to connect to the database using HTTP/HTTPS protocol via the Oracle NoSQL proxy.

•	Using SQL Command Line Interface (CLI):
You can use the SQL language in your applications to interact with the Oracle NoSQL Database.

In this workshop, you will be using  Microsoft Visual Studio Code to demonstrate the three methods. 
Also, you will be using a simplified version of the Oracle NoSQL Database called KVLite. KVLite provides a single storage node, single shard store, that is not replicated. A converged database is a multi-model, multitenant, multi-workload database. It supports the data model and access method each development team wants, without unneeded functionality getting in the way. It provides both the consolidation and isolation these different teams want but don’t want to think about. And it excels in all the workloads (like OLTP, analytics, and IoT) these teams require.  Oracle Database 19c is the world’s first converged database. Create a Base Database on Oracle AI Database@Google Cloud 12088 4436 DB Multicloud devinder.p.singh@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed In this workshop, you will learn how to create a Base Database on Oracle AI Database@Google Cloud Oracle Base Database Service on Oracle AI Database@Google Cloud brings the simplicity and automation of Oracle-managed databases directly into Google Cloud regions. It enables customers to run Oracle Database workloads with low latency to Google Cloud services like Vertex AI, BigQuery, and Gemini, while maintaining Oracle Database compatibility, performance, and security. The service provides automated lifecycle management, independently scalable compute and storage, built-in Oracle APEX low-code development, monitoring, backups, and patching — all managed through the familiar Google Cloud console and APIs. 
Unlike Exadata-based deployments that target the highest-end enterprise workloads, Base Database Service is designed for organizations that want a cost-effective, fully managed Oracle Database platform for transactional applications, modernization initiatives, and AI-enabled workloads. It supports Oracle AI Database capabilities, including integration with Oracle’s AI features and Google Cloud AI services, helping enterprises build intelligent applications without moving data across clouds. 
A key differentiator is the multicloud architecture: Oracle database infrastructure physically runs inside Google Cloud data centers while remaining connected to OCI control and management services. This gives customers a secure, high-performance path between Oracle databases and Google Cloud-native services, simplifying hybrid and multicloud strategies while reducing operational complexity. Create a MongoDB-Compatible App with Autonomous JSON Database 11977 4288 AI/ML Database luke.farley@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Build a full-stack To-Do app using Node.js, Express, and the MongoDB driver, connecting to Oracle Autonomous JSON Database via its MongoDB API. Experience drop-in MongoDB compatibility with Oracle’s autonomous scaling, security, and performance—no code changes required. This lab demonstrates how to build a CRUD To-Do List application using Node.js, Express, and the official MongoDB driver. Instead of connecting to a traditional MongoDB backend, you’ll point the app to Oracle Autonomous JSON Database (AJD) using its MongoDB API endpoint.

You’ll see how Oracle AJD can act as a seamless, drop-in backend for MongoDB workloads—with no changes to drivers, APIs, or development workflow. The only change required is updating your connection string. The lab also highlights Oracle AJD’s built-in benefits, such as autonomous scaling, security, and high availability.

By the end of this lab, you’ll have a working web application that looks and feels like a classic MongoDB stack, but runs on Oracle Cloud. This makes it easy to migrate, modernize, or develop new apps using familiar tools—while gaining the advantages of Oracle’s Autonomous Database. Create a non-container database in ExaDB-D 11137 3321 Database leona.dsouza@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Complete Learn how to create a non-container database in Exadata Database Service on Dedicated Infrastructure (ExaDB-D) using dbaascli utility. This hands-on workshop provides step-by-step instructions on creating a non-container database in Exadata Database Service on Dedicated Infrastructure using the dbaascli utility.

By default, the database system you create using the OCI console in ExaDB-D creates an Oracle Database 12.1, 12.2, 18c, or 19c using the multitenant architecture with a container database (CDB) with one pluggable database (PDB). If you want to create a non-container database in ExaDB-D in OCI, this can be done using the dbaascli utility. records.searchable: Create a Web Application in Oracle Visual Builder Studio 7061 920 OCI Docs Team Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Explore how to develop and deploy a modern web application within minutes in an agile environment. records.searchable: Create a web application with a microservices architecture to submit SLURM jobs on your HPC cluster. 11433 HPC bruno.garbaccio@oracle.com Workshop Approved This workshop intends to demonstrate the various capabilities of Oracle Cloud for High Performance Computing. In addition to the underlying IaaS, it is possible to deploy a microservices based architecture in order to interact with a web application under Visual Builder. Oracle has a strong IaaS offer when it comes to HPC. However, Oracle Cloud is a bigger platform than just IaaS and HPC can benefit from different available services. The goal of this workshop is to take the current HPC Stack available on the OCI marketplace as a basis (https://cloudmarketplace.oracle.com/marketplace/en_US/listing/67628143) and see how easy it is to build an entire application on top of it. Once the infrastructure is in place after the HPC stack deployment, the user will create a vault with a secret and serverless functions to interact with the vault and the underlying infrastructure. Then, the user will create an API gateway to call those functions outside of OCI. Finally, the user will create a web application in Visual Builder and build the front-end that will make API calls to launch HPC jobs on the compute nodes.  In the end, the user will have a graphical interface to submit Slurm jobs and will no longer have to use a terminal window which can be only for expert users. Create an Image Classification Model 11473 3807 AI Services samuel.cacela@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA In this LiveLab, you will train your own image classification model on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) using OCI AI Vision. You will experience the themes of automating, accelerating, and enhancing a biomedical research process where time is critical. You will learn how to implement a highly transferrable, multi-industry OCI solution pattern. In this LiveLab, you will train your own image classification model on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) using OCI AI Vision. You will experience the themes of automating, accelerating, and enhancing a biomedical research process where time is critical. You will learn how to implement a highly transferrable, multi-industry OCI solution pattern. The LiveLab is divided into two Labs: loading and labeling a provided dataset, followed by model training and serving.

An image classification model will be able to tell you what your image represents, based on all of the shapes and colors present in the image. This experiment will require our image classifier to serve as a cell classifier. As a cell classifier, your machine learning model will be able to discern images of cells from non-cells in the provided dataset, where the images were captured using a technique called coherent diffraction imaging.

The concept of the cell classification story and the dataset used in this LiveLab has been provided by Dr. Xin-hua Hu, from his machine learning experiment in the Physics department at East Carolina University. The cell classifier is a practical option for medical professionals during their research process, who would traditionally distinguish images of cells from non-cells by their own visual observation, and record their findings manually.

With large datasets, this process can be incredibly time-consuming and impractical. However, by offloading this important busywork to the cell classifier, and focus on tasks where their broad and deep range of knowledge and skills can be much more economically applied - and derive their analyses much faster where time is of the essence.

This solution pattern will be especially interesting if you can identify processes in your business and industry where automated and accurate visual analysis will render valuable time and cost savings.
