Create an Oracle Autonomous AI Database on Dedicated Exadata Infrastructure on Oracle AI Database@AWS 12077 4405 DB Multicloud devinder.p.singh@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed In this workshop, you will learn how to create an Oracle Autonomous AI Database on Dedicated Exadata Infrastructure on Oracle AI Database@AWS Oracle Autonomous AI Database on Dedicated Exadata Infrastructure on Oracle AI Database@AWS combines Oracle’s fully autonomous database platform with the performance and isolation of dedicated Exadata infrastructure, deployed natively within AWS environments. The service allows enterprises to run Oracle Autonomous AI Database workloads on OCI infrastructure colocated inside AWS data centers, delivering low-latency integration with AWS services while maintaining full Oracle Database compatibility and Exadata performance. The platform provides a private, single-tenant database cloud with dedicated compute, storage, networking, and Exadata resources for enhanced security, governance, and predictable performance. Oracle automates critical database lifecycle operations—including provisioning, patching, tuning, scaling, backups, and security—reducing administrative overhead while supporting mission-critical OLTP, analytics, AI, and mixed workloads. Through Oracle AI Database@AWS, organizations can modernize Oracle RAC and Exadata workloads with minimal application changes, while leveraging AWS-native services such as Amazon Bedrock, Redshift, Glue, Athena, and EC2. The offering also supports Oracle Database 23ai and AI Vector Search capabilities for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), semantic search, and enterprise AI applications. 
Key benefits include:
•	Dedicated Exadata performance with RDMA networking and high availability 
•	Autonomous operations that eliminate routine DBA tasks 
•	Integrated AI and vector search capabilities 
•	Native AWS console and marketplace integration

Create and Modify Tables in Oracle NoSQL Database Cloud Service using Terraform 11649 4077 NoSQL ramya.umesh@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Create and modify NoSQL tables in Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) using Terraform. The Oracle NoSQL Database Cloud Service is a serverless, fully managed data store that delivers predictable single-digit response times and allows applications to scale on demand via provisioning API calls.
Terraform is an infrastructure as code (IaC) software tool that allows DevOps teams to automate infrastructure provisioning using reusable, shareable, human-readable configuration files. Terraform uses providers to interface between the Terraform engine and the supported cloud platform. The Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Terraform provider is a component that connects Terraform to the OCI services that you want to manage.
In this workshop, you will create a singleton NoSQL table and a Global Active table using Terraform. Create custom models using OCI Document Understanding and Label Studio 11936 4246 AI Services cristina.granes@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed This workshop guides you through the process of configuring and using Label Studio for key-value extraction custom models in OCI Document Understanding. Label Studio is an open source software that provides an interface to annotate images for training custom models. Document Understanding (DU) is a service offered by Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) that uses AI-powered tools to help businesses extract insights, manage, and process documents at scale. DU provides pre-trained AI models for document classification, key value extraction, table extraction, and the extraction of other key elements for document processing. It also offers an option to create custom models to meet specific customer needs. These custom models can be trained to recognize unique document types, industry-specific terms, or specific data fields, ensuring that the solution adapts seamlessly to the company’s processes and requirements.

This workshop guides you through the process of configuring and using Label Studio to train your own key-value extraction model in OCI Document Understanding. We will focus with an example of using it to extract key values from invoices which the pre-trained DU model does not extract. The workshop will be comprehensive, covering everything from setting up the Label Studio environment to creating and training the custom model, and testing. Some synthetic examples will be offered to help understand the process end-to-end. Creating a COVID-19 Mask Detection Model on OCI with YOLOv5: Augmenting Data, Training and Real-Time Inference 11414 Machine Learning ignacio.m.martinez@oracle.com Workshop Completed In the last workshop, we created a Computer Vision model able to recognize whether someone was wearing their COVID-19 mask correctly, incorrectly, or simply didn't wear any mask.

Now, as a continuation of this topic, I will show you how you can train, augment and improve the model using OCI. This applies to any object detection model created using the YOLO standard and format. In the last workshop, we created a Computer Vision model able to recognize whether someone was wearing their COVID-19 mask correctly, incorrectly, or simply didn't wear any mask.

We used RoboFlow as the platform to help us during the creation of the model. It was especially useful to accelerate our data labeling process, as well as gathering data from other Computer Vision folks using RoboFlow Universe.

Now, as a natural continuation of this topic, I will show you how you can train and improve the model using Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). This applies to any object detection model created using the YOLO (You Only Look Once) standard and format - we will still use this framework to operate.

At the end of this workshop, you'll be able to perform real-time inference. Additionally, you will learn how to create your own model versions, which parameters are good or bad, and how to automatically augment your dataset before/during training. I dreamt of knowing how a Tesla autopilot worked on the inside, and whether I could make my own AI system at some point in my life.
Today, we're going to create a computer vision model, which will be able to tell us if you, or anyone else, is properly wearing a COVID-19 mask or not.

Join me and learn how to achieve this! I've always been curious about using Vision ML in some projects of mine. I dreamt of knowing how a Tesla autopilot worked on the inside, and whether I could make my own AI system at some point in my life. I was tired of dreaming, so I decided to learn by example (hands-on).

I set my focus on re-learning everything I knew about Vision ML (which is what I call image/video processing concerning Machine Learning in one way or another).

There are some topics, like Computer Vision, that are considered "too hard". Through this workshop, I aim to show you that it's not that hard to do this yourself (and not expensive either!).

Computer Vision has been a growing industry since its conception, and vision ML is one of the many components of Computer Vision. If you're interested in content like this, make sure to follow me, and stay tuned for part 2 (more info at the end).

Today, we're going to create a computer vision model, which will detect different mask-wearing states. So, it will be able to tell you if you, or anyone else that you want, is properly wearing a COVID-19 mask or not. The three different states we will consider are:
- A person with a mask.
- A person with a mask, but incorrectly worn.
- A person with no mask at all. Creating an Autonomous AI Database using Azure Infrastructure-as-Code tools 11953 Database matthew.mcdaniel@oracle.com Workshop More Info Needed This workshop will cover the steps required to provision an Autonomous AI Database@Azure using infrastructure as code tools. The goal is for users to understand the different methods in which we can provision databases in a repeatable fashion. There are many ways to provision an Autonomous AI Database@Azure: you can use the console for a seamless, new user friendly experience. For more experienced or those who are more DevOps inclined, you can use IaC (Infrastructure-as-code) tools to provision infrastructure through programming tools, such as the API, CLI, or Terraform. Additionally, Azure offers a user-friendly language called Bicep, which acts as an alternative to ARM templates or Terraform, which can often be challenging to read.

This workshop will cover how to create an Autonomous AI Database@Azure using 3 different infrastructure as code methods: Bicep, Azure Resource Manager, and Terraform. records.searchable: Customer Delinquency Workshop 8741 Machine Learning aaron.whitman@oracle.com Workshop Self QA Explore predict employee attrition to understand the key variables that influence turnover. In this workshop, an employee attrition dataset is used. You start by doing an exploratory data analysis (EDA) to understand the data. Then a model is trained using AutoML. The model is used to make predictions and evaluate the model to determine how well it generalizes to new data. Then you use machine learning explainability (MLX) to understand the global and local model behavior. You do all of this using the Oracle Accelerated Data Science (ADS) library. records.searchable: Customize AI Agents and Workflows with LLMs and OCI AI Agent Platform—Finance Edition 11959 4264 AI Services anthony.g.marino@oracle.com Workshop Published Event Completed Unlock the power of OCI AI Agent Platform in this immersive LiveLab! Build a smart AI agent that helps compliance officers and risk managers review loan applications, monitor workloads, and check policy adherence—seamlessly accessing both your Oracle AI Database and lending policy documents using natural language. If you’ve been curious how intelligent AI agents actually work behind the scenes, this hands-on workshop is your next step. You’ll build and customize a finance-focused AI agent using the OCI AI Agent Platform and large language models (LLMs) to help compliance officers and risk managers make smarter loan decisions. You will configure tools that allow the agent to query live data from Oracle AI Database and retrieve insights from policy manuals stored in Object Storage—combining structured and unstructured sources. You will learn how to connect these tools to an AI Agent, test multi-step reasoning with real compliance scenarios, and deliver policy-cited answers that explain the “why” behind each decision. Along the way, you’ll experiment with agent workflows, prompts, and configurations, and see how easily the OCI AI Agent Platform can bring context-aware intelligence to your enterprise use cases. By the end, you’ll have a fully functioning financial compliance AI agent—built, tested, and ready to adapt for your own organization’s workflows. If you’ve been curious how intelligent AI agents actually work behind the scenes, this hands-on workshop is your next step. You’ll build and customize a finance-focused AI agent using the OCI AI Agent Platform and large language models (LLMs) to help compliance officers and risk managers make smarter loan decisions. You will configure tools that allow the agent to query live data from Oracle AI Database and retrieve insights from policy manuals stored in Object Storage—combining structured and unstructured sources. You will learn how to connect these tools to an AI Agent, test multi-step reasoning with real compliance scenarios, and deliver policy-cited answers that explain the “why” behind each decision. Along the way, you’ll experiment with agent workflows, prompts, and configurations, and see how easily the OCI AI Agent Platform can bring context-aware intelligence to your enterprise use cases. By the end, you’ll have a fully functioning financial compliance AI agent—built, tested, and ready to adapt for your own organization’s workflows. Data Engineering: Build a Data Platform with Autonomous AI Database 11866 4146 Database DB Product Management Workshop Published Public Completed In this workshop, you will use Oracle’s Autonomous AI Database to simplify data access, management, and sharing, and to build AI-powered applications that give companies a competitive edge by automating time-consuming tasks—enabling a true Data Platform. This hands-on workshop guides finance data engineers through building a modern data platform using Oracle Autonomous AI Database. You’ll learn how to discover, connect, load, link, and share data across databases and cloud object storage to create trusted, ready-to-use financial data products. The lab scenarios follow SeersEquities, a financial services company, as it builds a data foundation to power smarter loan decisions and real-time risk analysis.

records.searchable: Data Mesh - App Modernization 11140 Developers - On Premises matthew.mcdaniel@oracle.com Workshop In Development This workshop will show users how to apply data mesh to their application modernization efforts. Application modernization is a large concern for many organizations. In a recent survey by vFunction, 92% of respondents stated that their organizations are currently undergoing this initiative. Undoubtedly, many of these organizations are attempting to decompose a monolithic application into microservices. While this is a challenging process, we would like to give a brief example of how it can be done. This workshop features a monolithic WebLogic application, MedRec, and we would like to add new functionality surrounding COVID-19 data tracking. Specifically, we would like to determine if certain patients are at risk of having a severe reaction to COVID-19. To accomplish this, we will use Golden Gate Stream Analytics to provide integration between our application and our Autonomous Database, which itself will contain the ML model for determining COVID-19 risk. Furthermore, we will expose our "transformed" data as a REST API using Helidon. Finally, we need a way for our internal teams to analyze this data and turn it into information. To this end, we will implement a streamlined analytical view using Oracle Analytics Server. Data Mesh - Data Integration Workshop 11017 Developers - On Premises brian.r.elliott@oracle.com Workshop Approved This workshop is to educate users on a Data Integration Data Mesh scenario for Transportation. This workshop is to educate users on a Data Integration Data Mesh scenario for Transportation and Logistics.
Use case: A logistics and supply chain business use case. A package delivery company (think FedEx) which has a centralized warehouse in Dallas. We have 10 trucks that each deliver a truckload of packages to 10 different destinations (1 truck per destination). Our live stream data monitors the trucks on their route, things like engine temperature, speed, which route they are on, etc. We are also using weather data from a service like the national weather station to enhance and do predictive analysis using oracle machine learning to predict which deliveries will be late based on certain weather conditions. For example, a high wind and high rain will cause a package delay. We also monitor truck health and maintenance which is sent to a Kafka topic which the auto shop team uses to keep the trucks at the ideal maintenance level. records.searchable: Data Mesh - Event Sourcing 11138 Developers - On Premises matthew.mcdaniel@oracle.com Workshop In Development This workshop will show users how to apply data mesh to an event sourcing use case about real-time credit card fraud detection. Event sourcing is a common practice for use cases that require storing changes to domain objects. For instance, in a package shipping application, one might store changes to an object in transit i.e item has shipped, item is in delivery, item has been delivered, etc. With this, we can guarantee that changes to the domain object's state are caused by these events. This gives us traceability as we can trace the state of an object by the events associated with it. When we introduce data mesh to this architecture, we can treat these events as data products, that is, we realize the potential business value of these events and publish them to analytics tools and APIs. In this workshop, we will cover one such use case in the form of real-time transaction fraud detection. The user will be responsible for configuring a Golden Gate Stream Analytics (GGSA) pipeline and a Oracle Machine Learning (OML) (IDK if this is the extent, please advise) model to accurately transform credit card transaction events into a data product, which will then be published to Oracle Analytics Server and exposed to a lightweight microservice. OAS will be used to support analysis on decisions.

records.searchable: Data Refactoring Advisor 11291 Developers - Converged DB Product Management Workshop Delete Requested Automatic discovery of bounded contexts for strangling microservices out of monolith applications. Helps convert legacy applications to modern app dev with Oracle Database. Data refactoring advisor takes an approach to collect and evaluate data access patterns, and then model it as a graph to find clusters of connected components that might look like a bounded context. This data-driven bottom-up approach is driven by data access patterns  observed by collecting SQL tuning sets data and creating an affinity matrix. This affinity matrix is translated into a graph for community detection, and to find clusters. These clusters are then presented to the application expert to evaluate their mapping to distinct and disjoint domains. records.searchable: Data Refactoring Advisor for Migrating a Monolith to Microservices 11016 3484 Developers - Database sanjay.goil@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Complete Developers of existing enterprise applications refactor their monoliths into microservices. Developers are often faced with refactoring their monolith applications into microservices. Won't it be great to have a tool that automates the data collection of access affinity to the tables and objects in the database schema? By analyzing the affinity closely, and applying graph clustering techniques using the Oracle Graph Database, advise for schema refactoring is provided. It is an iterative process to arrive at a meaningful cluster that the development team can take advantage of by defining bounded contexts in coding the applications. Splitting the schema and bounding access of a cluster of tables and objects to microservices results in the use of APIs or messaging to communicate between microservices. The Hybrid Partition Tables feature extends Oracle Partitioning by enabling partitions to reside in both Oracle Database segments and in external files and sources. Use hybrid partitioned tables in an Oracle 19c database to move non-active partitions to external files. This workshop also covers Oracle AI Vector Search, JSON collections, and JSON Relational Duality, providing a hands-on introduction to the latest capabilities. Explore the groundbreaking features in Oracle Database 23ai - a long-term support release packed with innovations. You will step through a range of key enhancements in Oracle Database 23ai, including new features for application development, availability, performance, and security. 

Create a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) application using Oracle AI Vector Search and a Generative AI model. The application serves as a flexible template that can be adapted to diverse business scenarios. Oracle Database 23ai acts as the vector storage, where critical context is stored to support accurate, up-to-date generative AI responses tailored to specific needs.

A JSON collection stores JSON documents alongside some metadata like the time of creation or update. Collections offer operations like inserts, deletes, index creation or queries. 

 JSON Relational Duality offers unmatched flexibility by enabling developers to access the same data as relational tables or JSON documents without duplication. Whether you’re a relational or document database developer, this feature streamlines application development and bridges the gap between the two models. This workshop explores how Oracle Transparent Data Encryption and Advanced Compression can be used together to protect sensitive data while optimizing storage.

Transparent Data Encryption is widely adopted to secure data at rest. However, many organizations have found that once data is encrypted, traditional storage-level compression becomes ineffective. Oracle’s integrated approach addresses this by enabling compression of encrypted data within the database, enhancing security while reducing storage costs. DB Security - Key Vault (SSH Key Management) 11645 3937 Database  - Security peter.wahl@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Centralize and protect SSH key pairs with Oracle Key Vault. Securing SSH key access is a critical part of safeguarding servers and preventing unauthorized logins. This workshop dives into Oracle Key Vault’s advanced SSH key management capabilities, demonstrating how to centralize SSH keys within a robust, policy-driven environment and minimize the risk of credential theft or misconfiguration. Learn to store, control, and rotate SSH key pairs directly in Key Vault—where private keys can be set to non-extractable, so even if a server is compromised, the keys remain protected.

During the 35-minute lab, explore hands-on tasks like registering remote servers as endpoints, uploading and distributing SSH keys through Key Vault, and revoking or rotating access with a few simple clicks. DB Security - Label Security 1644 676 Database  - Security roger.wigenstam@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Control user access to sensitive data rows using data labels. Label Security uses row-level data classifications to enforce access controls, restricting users to only the data they are allowed to access. It enables organizations to control operational and storage costs by enabling data with different sensitivity levels to co-mingle within the same database. Oracle Label Security provides controlled access to data rows based on the classification label of the data row.  Users will only be able to see and update data records they are authorized to access.

Oracle Label Security mediates access based on data sensitivity labels and user label authorizations. Oracle Label Security has consistently been evaluated as part of the Oracle Database to the Common Criteria for Information Technology Security Evaluation (ISO15408). Oracle Label Security is easily managed using API calls or Oracle Enterprise Manager. Oracle Label Security is an option available with Oracle Database Enterprise Edition, and it is included with the High Performance and Extreme Performance Editions of Oracle Database Cloud Service, on the Autonomous Cloud Databases, and on the Oracle Exadata Cloud Service. details: Control user access to sensitive data rows using data labels.

Label Security uses row-level data classifications to enforce access controls, restricting users to only the data they are allowed to access. It enables organizations to control operational and storage costs by enabling data with different sensitivity levels to co-mingle within the same database. Oracle Label Security provides controlled access to data rows based on the classification label of the data row.  Users will only be able to see and update data records they are authorized to access.

Oracle Label Security mediates access based on data sensitivity labels and user label authorizations. Oracle Label Security has consistently been evaluated as part of the Oracle Database to the Common Criteria for Information Technology Security Evaluation (ISO15408). Oracle Label Security is easily managed using API calls or Oracle Enterprise Manager. DB Security - Oracle Audit Vault and Database Firewall (AVDF) 3460 4227 Database  - Security najiah.abide@oracle.com Workshop Published Private Quarterly QA Monitor and safeguard databases with real-time activity tracking, advanced threat detection, and Database Security Posture Management (DSPM). Ensure continuous protection of sensitive data, detect risks early, enforce access controls, and help organizations stay compliant and secure against evolving threats. In the era of digital transformation and heightened regulatory expectations, data security is no longer optional—it is a vital necessity. Oracle Audit Vault and Database Firewall (AVDF) is a robust solution that empowers organizations to safeguard their most valuable digital assets from both internal and external threats. With AVDF, your databases are protected through advanced auditing, real-time monitoring, and proactive defense mechanisms, all managed from a unified, streamlined interface.

Why Attend this LiveLab?

Do you worry about meeting complex compliance mandates such as PCI DSS, SOX, or GDPR? Are you tasked with defending your organization against sophisticated cyber threats while enabling business agility? This hands-on LiveLab is the perfect environment for data professionals, security administrators, and auditors to experience first-hand how AVDF helps organizations secure sensitive information, streamline compliance, and respond rapidly to suspicious activity—before damage is done. 

What Problem Does AVDF Solve?

Modern database environments are highly dynamic and increasingly targeted by cyber attackers. Insiders with privileged access often represent the greatest risk, whether through error or deliberate misuse. Traditional logging and monitoring solutions frequently fall short—missing subtle policy violations or producing overwhelming volumes of raw data that are hard to interpret and act upon. Furthermore, regulatory auditors demand immediate, centralized, and immutable proof of how sensitive data is accessed and who is responsible. 

AVDF bridges these gaps by:

 - Centralizing and automating the collection, consolidation, and analysis of audit data from Oracle and non-Oracle databases.
    - Delivering real-time monitoring and alerts to detect unusual or unauthorized SQL activity—down to the individual statement.
    - Enforcing fine-grained controls at the network edge with the Database Firewall, blocking unwanted or suspicious commands before they can cause harm.
    - Offering a rich suite of compliance-ready reports and dashboards for continuous assurance.
     
What You’ll Experience in this LiveLab

In this interactive session, you'll step into the shoes of a security analyst or compliance officer as you: 

    - Deploy and configure AVDF for both Oracle and non-Oracle database environments
    - Set up real-time auditing policies and analyze collected data through intuitive dashboards
    - Use the Database Firewall to enforce strong security controls, detect policy violations, and block malicious SQL traffic
    - Respond to simulated threats, generate compliance reports, and implement best practices for the separation of duties
     
With guided exercises and real-world scenarios, you’ll gain practical skills you can immediately apply to your organization’s security and compliance strategy. No prior AVDF experience is required—just a willingness to learn and a desire to witness the power of Oracle’s database security solutions. 

Who Should Attend?

    - Database Administrators
    - Security Engineers
    - Auditors and Compliance Officers
    - IT Managers and Risk Professionals
     
Whether you are wrestling with stricter compliance mandates, tightening your security posture, or just curious about next-generation database protection, this LiveLab will inspire you to rethink what’s possible with AVDF. 

Take the next step in your data security journey—join us for the AVDF LiveLab and unlock the tools to secure your enterprise database estates, meet compliance demands with confidence, and fend off the threats of tomorrow. Your path to resilient database defense starts here. DB Security - Oracle Audit Vault and Database Firewall (AVDF) 3460 711 Database  - Security najiah.abide@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Monitor and safeguard databases with real-time activity tracking, advanced threat detection, and Database Security Posture Management (DSPM). Ensure continuous protection of sensitive data, detect risks early, enforce access controls, and help organizations stay compliant and secure against evolving threats. In the era of digital transformation and heightened regulatory expectations, data security is no longer optional—it is a vital necessity. Oracle Audit Vault and Database Firewall (AVDF) is a robust solution that empowers organizations to safeguard their most valuable digital assets from both internal and external threats. With AVDF, your databases are protected through advanced auditing, real-time monitoring, and proactive defense mechanisms, all managed from a unified, streamlined interface.

Why Attend this LiveLab?

Do you worry about meeting complex compliance mandates such as PCI DSS, SOX, or GDPR? Are you tasked with defending your organization against sophisticated cyber threats while enabling business agility? This hands-on LiveLab is the perfect environment for data professionals, security administrators, and auditors to experience first-hand how AVDF helps organizations secure sensitive information, streamline compliance, and respond rapidly to suspicious activity—before damage is done. 

What Problem Does AVDF Solve?

Modern database environments are highly dynamic and increasingly targeted by cyber attackers. Insiders with privileged access often represent the greatest risk, whether through error or deliberate misuse. Traditional logging and monitoring solutions frequently fall short—missing subtle policy violations or producing overwhelming volumes of raw data that are hard to interpret and act upon. Furthermore, regulatory auditors demand immediate, centralized, and immutable proof of how sensitive data is accessed and who is responsible. 

AVDF bridges these gaps by:

 - Centralizing and automating the collection, consolidation, and analysis of audit data from Oracle and non-Oracle databases.
    - Delivering real-time monitoring and alerts to detect unusual or unauthorized SQL activity—down to the individual statement.
    - Enforcing fine-grained controls at the network edge with the Database Firewall, blocking unwanted or suspicious commands before they can cause harm.
    - Offering a rich suite of compliance-ready reports and dashboards for continuous assurance.
     
What You’ll Experience in this LiveLab

In this interactive session, you'll step into the shoes of a security analyst or compliance officer as you: 

    - Deploy and configure AVDF for both Oracle and non-Oracle database environments
    - Set up real-time auditing policies and analyze collected data through intuitive dashboards
    - Use the Database Firewall to enforce strong security controls, detect policy violations, and block malicious SQL traffic
    - Respond to simulated threats, generate compliance reports, and implement best practices for the separation of duties
     
With guided exercises and real-world scenarios, you’ll gain practical skills you can immediately apply to your organization’s security and compliance strategy. No prior AVDF experience is required—just a willingness to learn and a desire to witness the power of Oracle’s database security solutions. 

Who Should Attend?

    - Database Administrators
    - Security Engineers
    - Auditors and Compliance Officers
    - IT Managers and Risk Professionals
     
Whether you are wrestling with stricter compliance mandates, tightening your security posture, or just curious about next-generation database protection, this LiveLab will inspire you to rethink what’s possible with AVDF. 

Take the next step in your data security journey—join us for the AVDF LiveLab and unlock the tools to secure your enterprise database estates, meet compliance demands with confidence, and fend off the threats of tomorrow. Your path to resilient database defense starts here. This lab introduces the latest enhancements to Oracle Data Redaction in Oracle Database 23ai, running on Oracle Autonomous Database. DB Security - Oracle Database Vault on Autonomous Database 7641 3071 Database  - Security richard.c.evans@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Enforce advanced access controls on Autonomous DB with Database Vault with no code changes needed. This workshop demonstrates how to implement advanced access controls using Oracle Database Vault on Oracle Autonomous Database. Key focus areas include enforcing separation of duties, restricting privileged user operations, and applying contextual controls based on SYS_CONTEXT attributes such as IP address, hostname, and OS user.

These capabilities are essential for reducing the risk of common attack vectors, including credential compromise and privilege escalation. By leveraging Database Vault, organizations can adopt a zero trust model at the data layer and enforce strong governance without altering application code. Database Vault is included with most Oracle Cloud Database offerings, including Autonomous Database, Base Database Service High and Extreme Performance editions, and Exadata Cloud@Customer. DB Security - Privilege Analysis 3260 4092 Database  - Security vasishtha.kumar.n.nalla@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Uncover and fix excessive Oracle DB privileges to reduce risk and strengthen security posture. In this lab, you'll explore Privilege Analysis, a powerful Oracle Database Enterprise Edition feature introduced in 12c. It helps identify and eliminate unused privileges, reducing risk and tightening security.

Excessive privileges are a common attack vector. Privilege Analysis goes beyond traditional audits by showing which privileges are actually used, helping you cut unnecessary access and shrink your attack surface.

Through hands-on exercises, you'll learn to generate actionable reports, refine privilege assignments, and strengthen your database security posture. DB Security - Protect sensitive data in REST calls using Oracle Data Redaction 11318 3564 Database richard.c.evans@oracle.com Workshop Published Private Quarterly QA Complete With Oracle Data Redaction,  protect your REST API calls by dynamically masking data in the payload. Redacting sensitive data in REST calls is essential for protecting user privacy, meeting compliance requirements, and minimizing the risk of data exposure. records.searchable: DB Security - TDE key management with Oracle Key Vault 5322 4179 Database  - Security peter.wahl@oracle.com Workshop Published Private Quarterly QA Migrate an encrypted Oracle database 19c to centralized key management with Oracle Key Vault. In this hands-on lab, you’ll migrate an Oracle Database 19c encrypted with TDE from a local wallet to centralized key management with Oracle Key Vault (OKV). You’ll upload pre-migration TDE master keys to OKV, then remove them from the encrypting server to align with PCI DSS requirements. You’ll also use tagged keys to associate TDE master keys more easily with PDBs, reducing manual steps and configuration errors. By the end, you’ll have a repeatable workflow for centralizing database encryption keys with auditing and rotation readiness. DB Security – TLS Network Encryption & Authentication 11108 Database  - Security gian.sartor@oracle.com Workshop Approved Learn how to configure TLS for network encryption as well as authentication in the Oracle Database Encrypting your database is a vital security control to protect against out-of-band access and satisfy regulatory requirements. Failing to encrypt your data leaves a security gap that other controls cannot close. 

There are two ways to encrypt data in motion within the Oracle Database – Native Network Encryption and Transport Layer Security (TLS). Native Network Encryption is covered in a different lab. If you are interested in Native Network Encryption, please review the DB Security – Native Network lab. This lab focuses on Transport Layer Security, and includes both encryption and authentication. DB Security - Unified Auditing 3261 702 Database  - Security angeline.dhanarani@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete A simple and practical approach to start with Unified Auditing. Unified Auditing is critical for ensuring the security and compliance of your Oracle databases. This workshop will guide you through the essentials of getting started with unified auditing, covering key scenarios like privileged user monitoring, sensitive data access, and direct database access. Whether you're looking to strengthen your security posture or ensure compliance with industry standards, this hands-on experience will equip you with the skills to implement robust auditing within Oracle Database.
Whether you're getting started with Unified Auditing or need help transitioning from legacy audit, this workshop will guide you through the process.
You may also want to explore Audit Vault and DB Firewall, and Data Safe LiveLabs to learn how you can enhance database auditing with activity monitoring capabilities. DBA Essentials - Administer Oracle Database 23ai with Oracle Enterprise Manager 11768 4058 OCI O&M suresh.r.rajan@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Explore container details from the SQL prompt. Manage target Oracle Databases and Listeners in a web browser, access target home pages, and view target details in Oracle Enterprise Manager. This workshop gets you started with basic database administration. You will connect to the SQL prompt and view details of your Container Database.
Next, you will log into Oracle Enterprise Manager (EM) in a web browser. You will use the guided discovery to add Oracle Databases and Listeners as manageable targets in EM. The workshop also shows how to remove these targets from EM.
You will then access the home page of the database instance, Container Database (CDB), and Pluggable Database (PDB), view target details, and perform some basic navigation. DBA Essentials - Administer user accounts and security for Oracle Database 23ai 11775 4065 OCI O&M suresh.r.rajan@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Learn how to administer user accounts, roles, and system privileges for Oracle Database 23ai using Oracle Enterprise Manager. This workshop aims at explaining user administration and security management for your Oracle Database 23ai so you can access your database with appropriate rights.
You will learn how to view existing roles in the database, create and modify roles, and manage system privileges. You will also manage the user accounts in your database, such as view existing users, create new users, and grant roles to users. You will learn how to unlock user accounts and allow them to log into the database. Additionally, this workshop will guide you to log into your Oracle Database a new user. You will perform all these tasks on your Oracle Database in a web browser using Oracle Enterprise Manager. DBA Essentials - Manage PDBs in Oracle Database 23ai using Oracle Enterprise Manager 11782 4071 OCI O&M suresh.r.rajan@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Discover and learn how to manage and administer the PDBs in Oracle Database 23ai using Oracle Enterprise Manager. Understand how to scale and automate the management of multiple Oracle Databases across your enterprise. 
This workshop will guide you not only to provision Pluggable Databases (PDBs) in your database instance but also perform administrative tasks on the PDBs. It will take you through different options for creating new PDBs in your Container Database (CDB), for example, using the Seed and by cloning another PDB. The workshop also provides detailed steps for removing PDBs from the database instance, such as deleting PDBs and unplugging PDBs from the root container. Moreover, you will learn how to plug in an unplugged PDB into a root container and create a new PDB. You will then perform additional tasks on the PDBs, such as closing and opening the PDBs. 
You will perform all these tasks on your Oracle Database in a web browser using Oracle Enterprise Manager. Deliver Exadata Database Performance and Scale with Oracle Cloud Master Class 11419 3830 ExaCS/ExaCC/DBCS eddie.ambler@oracle.com Workshop Published Event Completed In this hands-on class, you’ll deploy and configure Oracle databases using the Exadata Database Service leveraging OCI console, API, & Terraform. You will use cloud automation functions to create database environments leveraging VM Cluster Node Subsetting consolidation feature.  You will also configure Data Guard & automated backups to deliver the desired Maximum Availability Architecture SLAs. In this hands-on class, you’ll deploy and configure Oracle databases using the Exadata Database Service in our lab environment, leveraging the user interface web console and Terraform. 
 
In one of the most real-world classes you’ll ever attend, you’ll learn the latest techniques designed to simplify operational tasks and automate standards-based deployments of the database for your applications. You will use cloud automation functions to create database environments leveraging VM Cluster Node Subsetting consolidation feature.  . You’ll learn how the Exadata platform embraces cloud economics to control costs with the ability to scale CPUs up and down and to scale out compute and storage nodes. 
 
To meet your desired SLA levels, you’ll configure Maximum Availability constructs for your databases by enabling high availability and disaster recovery with Data Guard and Active Data Guard and cloud-based automatic backup and recovery. 

Don’t miss your chance to learn how to use cloud automation functions to standardize your database cloud environments, all while realizing the performance and scale of the Oracle Database on the Exadata Cloud Platform that is available to all types of workloads. Deploy a healthcare integration engine on OCI 12170 OCI sean.ru@oracle.com Workshop Self QA Complete This workshop walks through the steps of creating necessary OCI resources and deploying a popular open-source healthcare integration engine. Healthcare interoperability has evolved far beyond connecting systems within a single hospital. While interface engines continue to route HL7 messages between electronic health records (EHRs), laboratories, pharmacies, and imaging systems, today's healthcare organizations face a much broader challenge. They must deliver a seamless digital experience across multiple hospitals and clinics, support care coordination, expose FHIR APIs, integrate AI into clinical workflows, and securely exchange data with partners, payers, and public health agencies—all while continuing to rely on mission-critical on-premises clinical systems that remain essential to patient care.

Replacing these existing systems is rarely practical. Instead, healthcare organizations are extending their interoperability investments by adopting a hybrid architecture that combines proven on-premises solutions with cloud-native services. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) provides a secure, scalable, and high-performance platform for building this next generation of healthcare integration.

In this Oracle LiveLabs workshop, you will provision the minimum OCI infrastructure required to host an integration engine and then deploy the open-source edition of Mirth Connect on OCI. Along the way, you'll learn how to create the essential OCI resources, configure the environment, and prepare a cloud-based interoperability platform that can serve as the foundation for modern healthcare integration solutions. records.searchable: Deploy a Private Open WebUI Chatbot on OCI with Generative AI 12024 4418 OCI dario.mandic@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Deploy Open WebUI on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure integrated with Oracle Generative AI Service. Leverage automated infrastructure (OpenTofu), configuration (Ansible), and secure OpenAI-compatible API access to LLMs in your OCI region, all with SSL and modern DevOps tooling. This LiveLab provides a step-by-step guide to deploy Open WebUI, a lightweight, user-friendly interface for LLM chat on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), fully integrated with Oracle Generative AI Service . The solution uses automated infrastructure provisioning with OpenTofu and configuration management with Ansible to streamline deployment. The Open WebUI application runs on OCI Compute and communicates securely with Oracle-hosted LLMs via a Python API service gateway exposing an OpenAI-compatible API, ensuring all data and model inference remains within your OCI tenancy and region. SSL is automatically configured with Let’s Encrypt, and DevOps workflows are powered by Podman. Detailed instructions cover prerequisites, networking, DNS, identity/policy setup, host provisioning, and model registration. Ideal for users wanting to rapidly enable secure, enterprise-grade, OpenAI-compatible LLM inference and chat interfaces on OCI using open-source tools and Oracle's native GenAI capabilities. In this workshop, we will explore how to deploy Spring Boot applications to an Oracle Kubernetes Engine (OKE) cluster using Verrazzano.

Oracle Kubernetes Engine (OKE) provides a managed Kubernetes service that simplifies the deployment and management of containerized applications on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI).

Spring Boot is a popular Java-based framework used to build web applications and microservices. It offers a streamlined development experience with a convention-over-configuration approach, making it an excellent choice for building and deploying containerized applications on Kubernetes.

Verrazzano is an open-source, Kubernetes-native platform that provides a complete end-to-end solution for deploying and managing cloud-native applications. It simplifies the deployment of complex, multi-component applications by providing a unified view of the application topology, as well as a set of integrated tools for deployment, monitoring, and management. Deploy a Tomcat application to OKE using Verrazzano 11367 3621 Weblogic adrian.padilla@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Delete Requested This lab shows you how to install the Verrazzano platform on a single Kubernetes cluster and deploy a sample tomcat application docker image using Verrazzano concepts. Deploying a Tomcat application on a Kubernetes cluster can be a complex process that involves managing multiple containers, configuring networking, and ensuring high availability and scalability. 

To simplify this process, many organizations are turning to containerization technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes. Docker allows for the creation of portable container images that can be deployed on any platform, while Kubernetes provides a powerful orchestration engine that can manage the deployment and scaling of containers.

Oracle Verrazzano is a cloud-native platform that provides a unified management experience for deploying and operating containerized applications on Kubernetes clusters. It simplifies the deployment of complex applications by providing a consistent set of tools and APIs that can be used to manage and monitor applications across multiple clusters.

In this workshop, we will explore the process of deploying a Tomcat application Docker image to an Oracle Kubernetes cluster using Verrazzano.
We will cover the steps involved in creating a Docker image, configuring Verrazzano, deploying the application, and monitoring its performance. By the end of this article, you will have a clear understanding of how to deploy containerized applications on an Oracle Kubernetes cluster using Verrazzano. details: This lab shows you how to install the Verrazzano platform on a single Kubernetes cluster and deploy a sample tomcat application docker image using Verrazzano concepts.

Deploying a Tomcat application on a Kubernetes cluster can be a complex process that involves managing multiple containers, configuring networking, and ensuring high availability and scalability. 

To simplify this process, many organizations are turning to containerization technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes. Docker allows for the creation of portable container images that can be deployed on any platform, while Kubernetes provides a powerful orchestration engine that can manage the deployment and scaling of containers.

Oracle Verrazzano is a cloud-native platform that provides a unified management experience for deploying and operating containerized applications on Kubernetes clusters. It simplifies the deployment of complex applications by providing a consistent set of tools and APIs that can be used to manage and monitor applications across multiple clusters.

In this workshop, we will explore the process of deploying a Tomcat application Docker image to an Oracle Kubernetes cluster using Verrazzano.
We will cover the steps involved in creating a Docker image, configuring Verrazzano, deploying the application, and monitoring its performance. By the end of this article, you will have a clear understanding of how to deploy containerized applications on an Oracle Kubernetes cluster using Verrazzano.

This solution enables developers to perform GenAI RAG on custom PDF documents (stored in OCI Object Storage) using the OCI Generative AI Agent Service. Connect from a client VM. Create and apply custom PostgreSQL configurations. Create backups and restore a PostgreSQL DB system from a backup. In the lab, you'll learn how to create and connect to an OCI Database with PostgreSQL DB system. First, we'll work through some simple prerequisites like creating groups, policies, VCNs/subnets, and create a vault.

Then, we'll create a Database with PostgreSQL DB system through the console. You'll create a client VM and connect to it, followed by installing PSQL on the client VM.

Next, you'll connect the PostgreSQL DB system to the client VM, create and apply some simple custom PostgreSQL configurations, create backups, and restore a Database with PostgreSQL DB system from a backup. records.searchable: Deploy and Scale Redis using Master-Slave Mode 1541 OCI larry.beausoleil@oracle.com Workshop Self QA Redis (REmote DIctionary Server) is a popular open-source, in-memory data store that supports a wide array of data structures in addition to simple key-value pairs. It is a key-value database where values can contain more complex data types, such as strings, hashes, lists, sets, sorted sets, bitmaps, and hyperloglogs, with atomic operations defined on those data types. Redis combines in-memory caching with built-in replication, persistence, sharding, and the master-slave architecture of a traditional database. Given the rich features offered by Redis out of the box, a wide variety of deployment options are available. In this lab we will deploy Redis in Master-Slave mode (similar to below) though we will not deploy a NAT instance (Bastion host). Deploy APEX Apps In The Time It Takes To Make Your Morning Coffee 11474 3793 Developers - Database zachary.talke@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Learn how you can automatically deploy APEX applications, REST APIs, and database objects to new databases in a matter of minutes using SQLcl's enhanced Liquibase feature. Learn how you can automatically deploy APEX applications, REST APIs, and database objects to new databases in a matter of minutes using SQLcl's enhanced Liquibase feature.

Deploy & Execute HPC AI Inference Application ESMFold on OCI Autoscaling GPU Cluster 11319 OCI xinghong.he@oracle.com Workshop Approved Explore the hottest scientific AI-oriented AlphaFold on a GPU cluster that autoscales its size to match the demand of large scale workload for protein structure prediction. If you are a researcher who wants to quickly deploy a GPU cluster in the cloud to run ESMFold, one of the newest and hottest machine learning (ML) applications, this is the workshop for you.

ESMFold has drawn tremendous attention since its release in July 2022 because its break-through ML model can accurately predict protein structure orders of magnitude faster than other applications.   This workshop will guide you to deploy a GPU cluster in the cloud. Then, you will move on to install and run ESMFold to predict protein structures for a dozen synthetic protein sequences.  As a bonus benefit, you will experiment with cluster autoscaling, seeing how the cluster dynamically launched and terminated nodes to meet the need of ESMFold analysis workload. 

Step-by-step instructions will be provided so you do not need previous cloud computing experience. Neither you need previous experience in ESMFold or machine learning.

Objective
In this workshop you will learn the basics of a GPU cluster architecture with Slurm managed autoscaling capability.  Then, you will work on the 4 labs in the workshop
•	Lab 1: Creating a GPU cluster to run ESMFold 
•	Lab 2: Downloading and install ESMFold software packages 
•	Lab 3: Downloading example data sets and OCI utility scripts
•	Lab 4: Executing ESMFold 

Prerequisites
•	A customer account, Oracle Paid or LiveLabs Cloud Account with service limit approved for at least 8 gpu4-count.

records.searchable: Deploy Falco on Oracle Kubernetes Engine (OKE) 11964 4281 OCI adina.nicolescu@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed This LiveLab describes how to install Falco on OKE using a Terraform automation code using ORM, test the installation, access the UI, generate some events and view them in the UI. This LiveLab provides a step-by-step guide to deploying Falco, an open-source runtime security tool, on Oracle Kubernetes Engine (OKE) using Terraform automation in Oracle Resource Manager (ORM). This session is designed for developers and MLOps engineers who want to operationalize NVIDIA AI models using Kubernetes-native workflows on OCI. In this workshop, you will learn how to deploy and manage NVIDIA NIM containers on Oracle Container Engine for Kubernetes (OKE)  to run scalable, high-performance AI inference workloads. This session is designed for developers and MLOps engineers who want to operationalize NVIDIA AI models using Kubernetes-native workflows on OCI.

This workshop is ideal for developers, data scientists, and DevOps practitioners interested in:

- Deploying NIM on Kubernetes: Learn how to orchestrate and scale NVIDIA NIM containers using OKE for efficient AI inference in production.
- Harnessing NVIDIA GPUs for optimal performance: Experience how OKE integrates with NVIDIA GPU nodes to accelerate inference with TensorRT-optimized NIMs.
- Streamlining MLOps: Automate deployment, scaling, and lifecycle management of AI models using Helm, kubectl, and OCI DevOps tools within a unified cloud environment.

- Creating an NVIDIA API Key and pulling NIM containers

- Deploying NVIDIA NIM using Helm or kubectl
- Exposing NIM services securely for inference

Deploy ODA Multi-API Orchestration Chatbot powered by GenAI Tools and ADB Select AI 11855 4137 OCI jadd.jennings@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Deploy an ODA chatbot integrated with SELECT AI,  live APEX app and OIC. Deploy OpenKruise on Oracle Kubernetes Engine (OKE) 11950 4275 OCI dragos.nicu@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Learn how to deploy OpenKruise on Oracle Container Engine for Kubernetes (OKE) and explore advanced workload management with real-world use cases: sidecar injection, in-place updates with CloneSet, and enhanced StatefulSets. This LiveLab takes you through deploying OpenKruise, a CNCF project that extends Kubernetes workload management, on Oracle Container Engine for Kubernetes (OKE). OpenKruise enhances the standard Kubernetes controllers by introducing powerful capabilities such as automated sidecar injection, seamless in-place updates, and more advanced StatefulSet behaviors for improved scalability and reliability.

Throughout the workshop, you will provision an OKE cluster using a pre-built automation repository, install OpenKruise, and then explore how it can be used to simplify and optimize application lifecycle management. You will experiment with real-world scenarios that demonstrate how sidecar containers can be automatically injected into workloads, how applications can be updated in place without requiring pod recreation, and how stateful applications can benefit from safer and more flexible update strategies. Finally, you will clean up all deployed resources to avoid unnecessary costs.

By the end of this lab, you will have practical, hands-on experience running OpenKruise in a production-grade Kubernetes environment on OKE and a deeper understanding of how it can streamline and strengthen workload deployments. Deploy Rook-Ceph Storage on Oracle Kubernetes Engine (OKE) 12018 4334 OCI dragos.nicu@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Deploy Rook-Ceph distributed storage on Oracle Kubernetes Engine (OKE) using Terraform. Learn to configure block, file system, and S3-compatible object storage for your containerized applications with automated deployment via OCI Resource Manager. In this hands-on workshop, you will deploy Rook-Ceph, a cloud-native storage orchestrator, on Oracle Kubernetes Engine (OKE). Rook transforms Ceph distributed storage into self-managing, self-scaling, and self-healing storage services that integrate seamlessly with Kubernetes.
You will learn how to:
- Deploy an OKE cluster with attached OCI Block Volumes using Terraform or one-click OCI Resource Manager deployment
- Install and configure the Rook operator using Helm charts
- Create three types of Ceph storage classes:
  - Block Storage (RBD) for databases and stateful applications
  - Shared File System (CephFS) for multi-pod access with ReadWriteMany
  - Object Storage (S3-compatible) using RADOS Gateway
- Deploy real-world applications including WordPress with MySQL using persistent Ceph storage
- Monitor cluster health and storage usage with Ceph tools and dashboard Individual author Individual 4334 12018 Workshop Published Public Completed Intermediate OCI 2026-07-29 2026-02-02 Individual author Individual oci Mapped From Current Wms 2 52 31 52 59 160 172 4334 12018 Workshop Published Public Completed Intermediate OCI 2026-07-29 2026-02-02 Individual author Individual oci Mapped From Current Wms 2 https://livelabs.oracle.com/ords/dbpm/r/livelabs/view-workshop?wid=4334 https://oracle-livelabs.github.io/oci/rook-on-oke/workshops/tenancy/index.html github_pages dragos.nicu@oracle.com Deploy Rook-Ceph distributed storage on Oracle Kubernetes Engine (OKE) using Terraform. Deploying a Highly Available Wordpress Site utilizing Oracle Kubernetes Engine (OKE) and MySQL Managed Database Service (MDS) 11544 OCI poorvardh.patel@oracle.com Workshop Approved Set up your own Cloud-Native Wordpress website using Oracle Kubernetes Engine (OKE) and MySQL Managed Database Service (MDS). In this workshop, you will learn how to set up a highly-available Wordpress website running on Oracle Kubernetes Engine (OKE). This lab also includes optional steps to use Cloudflare for DNS management and SSL/TLS Certificates for increased security. 

You will be introduced to some of Oracle Cloud Infrastructure's (OCI) cloud-native services such as OKE and the MySQL Managed Database Service (MDS), along with some core services such as Virtual Cloud Networks (VCN), Block Volumes for persistent storage, and Load Balancers. 

You will also be introduced to the Cloud Shell and Code Editor on the Cloud Console. The lab will walk through creating a Dockerfile, utilizing the Docker CLI tool to build and push images to the Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Registry (OCIR), creating Kubernetes deployment files, utilizing the kubectl CLI tool, and basic linux commands. Design Different Topologies with Oracle GoldenGate 23ai 11755 4121 GoldenGate preeti.s.shukla@oracle.com Workshop Published Private Completed This livelab is designed to allow you to set up data replication in different Oracle GoldenGate topologies such as unidirectional, bidirectional, cascading among others. In this tutorial, you will be provided steps to run automated scripts for configuring a sample data replication environment and use it to generate standard business reports for a unidirectional topology. 
The scripts allow you to use two approaches for configuring Oracle GoldenGate data replication:
-	Using cURL scripts
-	Using OBEY commands run from the Admin Client
The tutorial provides the steps to run the scripts for both these methods.
The following diagram shows a standard unidirectional replication in Oracle GoldenGate. In the standard Oracle GoldenGate configuration, an Extract sends captured data using the Distribution Service over TCP/IP to a trail on the target system, where it is received by the Receiver Service and stored until processed by the Replicat. records.searchable: Develop AI RAG Apps with Autonomous AI Database Select AI 11833 4114 ADB Serverless lauran.serhal@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Retrieval Augmented Generation - OR RAG - is a way of improving a large language model’s ability to accurately answer natural language questions or queries - especially when those answers require information that is held privately within an organization. Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) is a way of improving a large language model’s ability to accurately answer questions - especially when those answers require information that is held privately within an organization. In this workshop, you will learn how Autonomous AI Database makes it easier to create RAG-based apps. Every organization has knowledge basis to support different part of the business. Oracle moviestream is no different. It has an internal web site that is used by the support teams to answer technical questions from customers. The moviestream has recently deployed a Chatbot to help its customers get relevant answers instantly based on the information in the internal knowledge base. The moviestream database was indexed capturing the semantics behind the content.  This application uses a new Oracle Database 26ai called AI Vector. When a question is asked, Vector search finds the relevant content based on a similarity ranking. It's not a simple text comparison search; instead, it is a semantic search, a much more powerful way of finding relevant information. Here's a summary of the full process. Your question is encoded as a Vector and sent to AI Vector search.  AI Vector search then finds relevant documents and those documents are then sent to GenAI along with your question. In other words, your question has been augmented with content from the customer support knowledge base. GenAI then uses that relevant support information to provide an informed answer to your question. This may sound complex, but it turns out that select AI simplifies the entire process. details: Retrieval Augmented Generation - OR RAG - is a way of improving a large language model’s ability to accurately answer natural language questions or queries - especially when those answers require information that is held privately within an organization.

Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) is a way of improving a large language model’s ability to accurately answer questions - especially when those answers require information that is held privately within an organization. In this workshop, you will learn how Autonomous AI Database makes it easier to create RAG-based apps. Every organization has knowledge basis to support different part of the business. Oracle moviestream is no different. It has an internal web site that is used by the support teams to answer technical questions from customers. The moviestream has recently deployed a Chatbot to help its customers get relevant answers instantly based on the information in the internal knowledge base. The moviestream database was indexed capturing the semantics behind the content.  This application uses a new Oracle Database 26ai called AI Vector. When a question is asked, Vector search finds the relevant content based on a similarity ranking. It's not a simple text comparison search; instead, it is a semantic search, a much more powerful way of finding relevant information. Here's a summary of the full process. Your question is encoded as a Vector and sent to AI Vector search.  AI Vector search then finds relevant documents and those documents are then sent to GenAI along with your question. In other words, your question has been augmented with content from the customer support knowledge base. GenAI then uses that relevant support information to provide an informed answer to your question. This may sound complex, but it turns out that select AI simplifies the entire process.

Develop with Oracle AI and Database Services: Healthcare (Open Source Version) 11485 3876 Database paul.parkinson@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed This is the open source version of the original AI for Healthcare workshop written in Ape.
AI tools are changing modern healthcare. In this workshop we show how Oracle AI is helping identify  cancer by using the Oracle Database, OCI, and AI Services and popular full-stack languages and frameworks including Flutter, Java (SpringBoot), JavaScript (React, Express, Node), Python, Rust, etc. Authors: Paul Parkinson, Nicholas Cusato, and Divit Gupta

ML and AI tools are unprecedentedly changing Modern Healthcare. Given the speed of innovation and global outreach, it can be challenging for patients and healthcare providers to stay abreast of the latest technological advances and how they will impact the future.

In this LiveLabs AI for Healthcare, Learn about the latest innovations in Healthcare, Detect Breast Cancer using OCI Vision at an early stage. Detect Cardiovascular disease with Electrocardiogram (ECG) Reports and OCI Anomaly Detection. Use the power of OCI Document Understanding to submit medical expenses, or using OCI Speech, ask a doctor about specific medical symptoms and get a response from a virtual Doctor (not a replacement for actual medical advise of course) leveraging the power of Oracle Gen AI. Chat with a virtual doctor through Oracle Digital Assistant, asking questions related to Breast cancer or Lung cancer or Covid and how to diagnose them. Analyze complex clinical data or genome sequences with Oracle Analytics Cloud or locate the nearest Hospital with Oracle Spatial and Maps and contact them. And much more.

records.searchable: Develop your first truly distributed transactional Microservices in Kubernetes 11067 Developers - Database mark.rakhmilevich@oracle.com Workshop Approved Learn how to build transactional Microservices that ensure data consistency across polyglot services using transaction coordination services provided by Oracle Transaction Manager for Microservices. Microservices architecture based apps are distributed by nature, however ensuring consistency across services is another thing.  At best, apps deal with it in business logic to compensate for an already committed transaction, which usually results in increased development effort and delays in release to production. In this hands-on lab, we will walk you through steps to build a microservices based app consisting of Java, Typescript and Database APEX/ORDS services participating in a global distributed transaction using two-phase commit/XA and coordinated by Oracle Transaction Manager for Microservices. Developing your application for 99.999% availability 11553 Developers - Database paul.parkinson@oracle.com Workshop Approved Achieving 99.999% availability for an application requires rigorous planning, sophisticated architecture, and strict operational management. This workshop delves into the particulars of a comprehensive range of considerations essential for developers and illustrates how Oracle provides one-of-a-kind solutions across the entire spectrum of concerns. Achieving 99.999% availability for an application requires rigorous planning, sophisticated architecture, and strict operational management. This workshop delves into the comprehensive range of considerations essential for developers and illustrates how Oracle provides one-of-a-kind solutions across the entire spectrum of concerns.
The use case focus involves particular aspects, including Oracle integrations and features, of the most popular full stack software languages and platforms like Spring Boot, .NET, and JavaScript. It explores application tier architectures, highlighting the roles of Kubernetes and microservices, and examines data and message-driven applications (including details on Kafka, TxEventQ, data models, workloads, etc.).
The workshop emphasizes the importance of idempotence and eventual consistency and maintaining transactional data integrity, exploring various protocols such as XA and sagas/LRA (including MicroTx , Oracle Sagas, reservation less locking, auto-compensating data types, etc.). 
It also addresses the significance of caching and application continuity features for enhancing performance and reliability.
The course covers the use of globally distributed databases and sharding techniques to ensure scalability and availability. It outlines the critical need for compliance with regulations and underscores the details of robust security measures.
Additionally, the workshop delves into lower-level aspects like cross site recovery, Oracle DataGuard, GoldenGate, etc. providing a holistic view of the technologies and practices necessary to build highly reliable systems. 
Finally, observability, and Oracle’s end-to-end unified observability approach across all products is discussed in detail providing the ability to monitor application for failures and performance.
This comprehensive approach is designed to equip developers with the knowledge and skills required to design and operate applications that meet the demanding uptime goal of 99.999% availability, ensuring minimal downtime and maximum reliability in a variety of operating environments. records.searchable: Discover the Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Security Available on Your Tenancy 11121 3584 OCI sonia.yuste.lledo@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete The purpose of the workshop is to provide you with an introduction and overview about all the security services available in Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) by using automation with our Unique Security Experience (USE) tool. The USE tool is created to provide you the best cloud security experience in the market through the automation of OCI security assessments and security enablement. In order to do that, this Live Lab will drive you through the required steps to perform a “Security Services Assessment” of your OCI tenant. The goal of this assessment is to determine, for each OCI Security Service, whether you have activated it and you are using it, or not yet. In case you are not leveraging it yet, the USE tool will provide you with all the details on the service, direct links to the right dashboard and/or the documentation, as well as to Terraform Scripts, to help you activate the service in a few clicks if applicable. We will provide you the USE tool in this workshop so that you can experience the OCI security services capabilities and get a good knowledge about it. Easily Build Powerful Analytic Applications using APEX and Analytic Views 11395 3726 ADB Serverless mike.matthews@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Building a powerful, interactive analytic reporting application using Oracle Application Express (APEX) is easier than you would ever think possible when that application uses Oracle Analytic Views as the foundation. Learn how to use Analytic View to supercharge your APEX application with aggregation and calculations, and simplify SQL generation at the same time! Oracle Application Express (APEX) is a low-code application development environment that creates database-centric applications.   Analytic views are a dimensionally oriented semantic layer in the Oracle Database that can serve as a foundation for business intelligence applications.  Analytic views mask the underlying complexity of tables and views, define aggregation rules, include analytical expressions to create calculated measures and provide rich descriptive metadata.

This Live Lab will teach you how to use both to build a powerful, interactive analytic application.  You will learn how analytic views enhance the capabilities of APEX applications with aggregations and rich calculations while simplifying SQL generation at the same time.  More power, less work.  What could be better? This workshop introduces you to the Data Transforms tool in Data Studio. You will learn how to create a data pipeline for data analysis, data science or for any ad-hoc data preparation need. Autonomous Database is bundled with Data Studio for loading, integrating, preparing, analyzing and sharing data. 

This workshop introduces you to the Data Transforms tool in Data Studio. You will learn how to create a data pipeline for data analysis, data science or for any ad-hoc data preparation need. Data can be loaded from a wide selection of heterogenous sources (databases and applications) and can go through complex transformations. You will learn how to define the data load and transforms process and schedule them for periodic execution.

Deployment:
- Data Transforms is part of Data Studio tools and is available in every Autonomous Database Serverless. You can simply create an Autonomous Database and go through this workshop.

- If you are not an Autonomous Database user, then you can use the Data Transforms deployed through OCI Golden Gate service. After deploying the service, you can use the remainder of this workshop to learn how to use Data Transforms. records.searchable: Easy Text Search over Multiple Tables and Views with DBMS_SEARCH in Oracle Database 26ai 11437 3721 Database oscar.tepepan-aviles@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Completed DBMS_SEARCH in Oracle Database 26ai makes it easy to create a single text index over multiple tables and views. With a single call you can add a table or view to your text index, and make it available to your users for full-text search. Oracle Text provides text content searching over text data types such as VARCHAR2, JSON, CLOB and BLOB. But what if you want a single index that covers many columns and many tables? DBMS_SEARCH makes this easy for you by adding a table or view to an index with a single, simple PL/SQL call. You can then search all of your tables, or just specific table using the CONTAINS and JSON_TEXTCONTAINS operators. EBS Analytics with ADW/OAC 2800 794 OCI ionel.panaitescu@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Load and optimize data from sources like EBS into a centralized Oracle Autonomous Data Warehouse using Oracle Data Integrator and then use Oracle Analytics Cloud to analyze the data and obtain actionable insights. Departmental Analytics (with EBS Integration)

Lines of business, typically, don't have timely or efficient access to data and information. Analysts gather the data manually, work with it on an individual basis, and then share files through emails or file servers. With Oracle Autonomous Data Warehouse (ADW) and Oracle Analytics Cloud (OAC), you can load and optimize data from Oracle E-Business Suite (EBS) and other sources into a centralized data warehouse for analysis, so departments can gain actionable insights.

These lab guides provide directions on how one can set up departmental EBS analytics in Oracle Analytics Cloud. We will use Oracle Data Integrator (ODI) to load data from an EBS instance and a database into an ADW. Thereafter, we will connect the ADW to OAC, create data sets and import a prebuilt sample analysis with refined data. EBS Asserter - Integrating Oracle E-Business Suite with IDCS for SSO 11112 OCI NA Cloud SE Workshop Approved E-Business Suite Asserter is a lightweight Java application provided by Oracle Identity Cloud Service, using which we can able to integrate Oracle E-Business Suite with Oracle Identity Cloud Service as authentication mechanism. This integration allows Oracle E-Business Suite to participate in the single sign-on (SSO) provided by Oracle Identity Cloud Service. Oracle Identity Cloud Service provides a lightweight Java application, called Identity Cloud Service Asserter for E-Business Suite (EBS Asserter). With the E-Business Suite Asserter, you can implement SSO for Oracle e-Business Suite and other applications.

EBS Asserter main features:

Non-intrusive solution that doesn't require configuration changes in your Oracle e-Business Suite environment.
Need to be deployed in WebLogic Server 12c using secure communications (SSL/TLS)
Multiple access modes for SSO with Oracle e-Business Suite:
Access Oracle e-Business Suite using the EBS Asserter’s direct URL link (bookmark)
Access Oracle e-Business Suite using Oracle Identity Cloud Service's My Apps page
Access Oracle e-Business Suite using the EBS Asserter's login using a redirect parameter
Access Oracle e-Business Suite using previously bookmarked Oracle EBS URLs
Supports Oracle e-Business Suite, EBS Asserter, and Oracle Identity Cloud Service Single logout. Efficient Resource Management for Kubified Java Apps 11186 3436 Community sharat.chander@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Authors: Elder Moraes, Developer Advocate, Red Hat & Ana-Maria Mihalceanu, Sr. Developer Advocate, Oracle.
Explore best practices and user settings to manage the application’s resources in a Kubernetes cluster. Authors: Elder Moraes, Developer Advocate, Red Hat & Ana-Maria Mihalceanu, Sr. Developer Advocate, Oracle.

In this session, we'll explore best practices and user settings to manage the application’s resources in a Kubernetes cluster. Since a load of cluster usage may increase rapidly due to traffic load and the number of applications deployed, it's better to set up resource quotas to keep the workloads running smoothly.

We’ll start by setting up a Quarkus application, increasing its complexity, and tailoring appropriate resource quotas for CPU and RAM. Moreover, we will look into using integration tests to validate Kubernetes/OpenShift resources prior to their actual deployment.

We will see how to monitor those workloads and finally, we'll cover performance and tuning aspects for production clusters. EM - Automation with Enterprise Manager Job System 6981 841 OCI O&M anand.p.prabhu@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA In this lab you will learn how to use the Enterprise Manager Job System to automate routine administrative tasks such as backup, SQL scripts and OS jobs etc., in your environment so you can manage them more efficiently. A job is a unit of work that you define to automate commonly-run tasks. Scheduling flexibility is one of the advantages of jobs. You can schedule a job to start immediately or start at a later date and time. You can also run the job once or at a specific interval, such as three times every month. The Enterprise Manager Job System serves these purposes:

Automates many administrative tasks; for example: backup, cloning, and patching
