Enhance your Oracle APEX App with Document-Aware Generative AI Agents 11917 4190 APEX shailu.srivastava@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed This workshop demonstrates how to integrate Oracle APEX with OCI Generative AI Agents, showcasing how enterprises can enhance their applications with intelligent, context-aware capabilities. You will explore the power of Large Language Models (LLMs) combined with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to transform raw enterprise documents into actionable insights. This workshop demonstrates how to integrate Oracle APEX with OCI Generative AI Agents, showcasing how enterprises can enhance their applications with intelligent, context-aware capabilities. You will explore the power of Large Language Models (LLMs) combined with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to transform raw enterprise documents into actionable insights.

As part of this workshop, you will begin by uploading various documents to OCI Object Storage, which serves as a secure, scalable repository for your enterprise data. These documents are then processed through an ingestion job, which parses, indexes, and prepares the data for interaction using the OCI Generative AI service.

You will integrate a chat interface within your Oracle APEX application, allowing end users to interact with the Generative AI Agent in real time. The AI agent uses the previously ingested content to provide intelligent, personalized, and context-rich responses, enhancing user experience and driving operational efficiency. The sample process used as an example in this workshop relates to the selection of a uniform by an employee and the subsequent approval step by the procurement manager prior to an email confirmation sent to the uniform distributor. In this comprehensive workshop, we delve into the intricacies of configuring the native Process Automation task type within the Journeys feature of Oracle HCM Cloud. The workshop aims to provide a detailed and practical understanding of how to streamline and automate a specific business process, and it employs a sample process as an illustrative example. This process revolves around the crucial task of an employee selecting a uniform and the subsequent approval step undertaken by the procurement manager before a confirmation email is dispatched to the uniform distributor. The workshop offers an invaluable opportunity to gain hands-on experience in setting up this process, thereby enhancing your proficiency in harnessing Oracle HCM Cloud's capabilities to optimize and automate essential HR and procurement workflows. Participants will leave this workshop equipped with the knowledge and skills needed to adapt these techniques to their unique organizational needs, ushering in a new era of efficiency and productivity in their HR and procurement operations. Ensure data consistency in distributed transactions across ORDS applications using MicroTx 11512 3886 Developers - Database brijesh.deo@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Complete Use Oracle Transaction Manager for Microservices (MicroTx) to maintain data consistency across multiple ORDS applications (microservices in Oracle Database). With microservice based architectures, each microservice typically uses its own database.  When a request spans multiple microservices, there’s a good chance it will run into a problem where two or more updates must succeed, or none do. Like if I send you money from my bank, but your account isn’t updated for some reason. Unfortunately, in the microservices world, local database transactions can’t span microservices. So how do you overcome the dual write problem?  
 
With Oracle Transaction Manager for Microservices, or MicroTx you don’t have to worry about making sure all updates happen. It’s a workflow engine to ensure data consistency across microservices.   
 
It takes on the burden of error handling and recovery so that the microservices and developers can focus on business logic and not on underlying technical issues. It keeps microservices consistent with each other, reducing complexity.

In this workshop, you will learn how to use MicroTx to maintain data consistency across multiple ORDS applications by deploying and running a Bank Transfer application. The Bank Transfer application is created in PL/SQL and deployed using ORDS in Oracle Database. MicroTx provides a transaction coordination microservice to maintain consistency in the state of various databases participating in a transaction. Enterprise Data Quality 2400 612 Developers - On Premises srivishnu.gullapalli@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA This lab introduces you to the Enterprise Data Quality (EDQ). You will connect to sample data, understand how to profile the data and know how to correct the data in EDQ. Enterprise Data Quality brings the necessary functionality for delivering Data Fit for Use and that satisfy an organization’s current and emerging Data Governance requirements for your Data Warehouse / Data Mart / Data Lake initiatives. EDQ offers an integrated suite of data quality tools that provide an end-to-end solution to measure, improve and manage the quality of data from any domain. EDQ also combines powerful data profiling, cleansing, matching and monitoring capabilities while offering unparalleled ease of use. Features of EDQ include:

    Advanced data profiling to identify and measure poor quality data and identify rule requirements to resolve your Project and/or Enterprise data quality issues
    Semantic and pattern-based recognition to accurately parse and standardize data that is poorly structured
    An innovative Open Reference Data Architecture enabling easy creation, customization and maintenance of business rules that adapt and learn from your data to enable and expedite automated solutions to jumpstart, continually improve and socialize your data quality over time

Take an educational journey that leverages your domain knowledge and extends your data skills to evolve from an Oracle Data Professionals to an Oracle Data Scientist in just 6 weeks! Oracle makes machine learning simple. By implementing an architecture that “moves the algorithms; not the data”, Oracle embeds 30+ ML algorithms in the SQL kernel of Oracle Databases (EE, ADW/ATP and DBCS) for in-database ML processing. Oracle Data Professionals can now use Oracle Machine Learning (OML) SQL and PL/SQL functions to build, apply and deploy OML models inside Oracle Databases. Data professionals today already perform many of the supporting data preparation tasks for data scientists, typically 80% of the work. records.searchable: Exploring RAFT Replication in Oracle Database 23ai 11542 Database ethan.shmargad@oracle.com Workshop Approved Discover RAFT replication in Oracle database 23ai, focusing on its integration for high availability and automatic failover with zero data loss in distributed database environments. This workshop delves into the RAFT replication feature, a consensus algorithm for replicated state machines, integrated into the Oracle database engine. Participants will learn how RAFT lets you automatically distribute and replicate data across a pool of Oracle databases that share no hardware or software. RAFT's implementation for Oracle sharding ensures its role in high availability, simplified replication, and zero data loss in distributed databases. Oracle Database developers can easily turbocharge their productivity by taking advantage of AI Assist technologies. This lab will show how you can easily use OCI's Code Assist platform to work directly against your Oracle Database using our MCP server (Oracle SQLcl).

Imagine being able to have a conversation with the database, gain insight on your data, get help optimizing your SQL code, easily adding new columns to your tables, all from your favorite AI chatbot or AI enabled IDE. This is now possible for any Oracle Database with our MCP server provided by SQLcl.

Combine this with OCI's Code Assist platform, which has already been trained and optimized for Java, PL/SQL, and application development on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure - and you have everything you need to be a cloud native database developer on OCI. 

This lab will show you how to setup your development environment for an Oracle Database using AI Code Assist via Oracle SQLcl's MCP server. From there we will guide you along the complete application development lifecycle, ending with a working web application. records.searchable: Extend EBS with Logging Analytics 4661 803 EBS nicholas.cusato@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Explore the use of enabling OCI Logging Analytics to extend your EBS environment. This 5 Lab workshop will walk you through the process of first onboarding Logging Analytics in your tenancy and region. Then ingesting OCI Network and Audit Logs as well as the process to ingest logs from your servers. Then you will be introduced to Entities Sources and the Logging Analytics Service on OCI. You will set up your Logging Analytics service to understand the data being ingested and finally build visualizations and dashboards to understand your log data. This lab is an extension to the EBS on OCI lab. Map app roles to database data roles and enforce row- and column-level policies per user—no code, no proxies. Same query, different results, automatically enforced by the database. Oracle AI Database 26ai Deep Data Security solves AI agent security within the kernel of the database. records.rawTitle: Feature types for data exploration and validation
records.source: 14 August 2026 WMS and LiveLabs dashboard views; 15 August 2026 GitHub repository census
records.searchable:
Feature types for data exploration and validation 11059 3193 OCI Data Science john.peach@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA There is a distinction between the data type of a feature and the nature of data that it represents. The data type represents the form of the data that the computer understands. ADS uses the term "feature type" to refer to the nature of the data. For example, a medical record id could be represented as an integer, its data type, but the feature type would be "medical record id". The feature type system allows data scientists to separate the concept of how data is represented physically from what the data actually measures. That is, the data can have feature types that classify the data based on what it represents and not how the data is stored in memory. Each set of data can have multiple feature types through a system of multiple inheritances. As a concrete example, an organization that sells cars might have a set of data that represents the purchase price of a car, that is the wholesale price. You could have a feature set of wholesale_price, car_price, USD, and continuous. 

All default feature types have methods for creating summary statistics and a plot to represent the data. This allows you to have summary information for each feature of your dataset while only using a single command. However, the default feature types may not provide the exact details needed in your specific use case. Therefore, feature types have been designed with expandability in mind. When creating a new feature type, the summary statistics and plots that are specific to your feature type can be customized.

The feature type system works at the Pandas dataframe and series levels. This allows you to create summary information across all of your data and at the same time dig into the specifics of one feature.

The feature type framework comes with some common feature types. However, the power of using feature types is that you can easily create your own and apply them to your specific data. You don't need to try to represent your data in a synthetic way that does not match the nature of your data. This framework allows you to create methods that validate whether the data fits the specifications of your organization. For example, for a medical record type, you could create methods to validate that the data is properly formatted. You can also have the system generate warnings to sure the data is valid as a whole or create graphs for summary plots.

The framework allows you to create and assign multiple feature types. For example, a medical record id could also have a feature type id and the integer feature type. It also allows you to customize summary statistics, plots and correlations. Select columns based on feature types.

Feature type warnings are used for rapid validation of the data. For example, the wholesale_price might have a method that ensures that the value is a positive number because you can't purchase a car with negative money. The car_price feature type may have a check to ensure that it is within a reasonable price range. USD can check the value to make sure that it represents a valid US dollar amount. It can't have values below one cent. The continuous feature type is the default feature type and it represents the way the data is stored internally.

The feature type validators are a set of is_* methods, where * is generally the name of the feature type. For example, the method .is_wholesale_price() can create a boolean Pandas series that indicates what values meet the validation criteria. It allows you to quickly identify which values need to be filtered or require future examination into problems in the data pipeline. The feature type validators can be as complex as they need to be. For example, they might take a client ID and call an API to validate that each client ID is active. records.searchable: Find Roles Hidden in Your Skills using Graphs 12157 4498 Database - Spatial and Graph ramu.murakami.gutierrez@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Submitted Explore a career skills graph to uncover roles that match your experience. Use multi-hop queries, vector similarity, and an LLM to find related skills, identify gaps, and understand why a role fits. Leave with a visualized career graph and practical insights for your next move. You have more career options than your job title suggests, and a graph can prove it. This hands-on workshop uses a career skills graph to answer the question: what roles could I move into based on what I already know how to do? Participants will explore a dataset connecting skills, job roles, and open positions, then personalize it with their own experience. Graphs are great at multi-hop traversal, revealing roles two or three connections away. We’ll enhance this with vector similarity to uncover semantically related skills, and an LLM layer to explain why a role fits and highlight skill gaps. You’ll leave with a visualized career graph and real queries to guide your next move. Who knows? You might discover an unexpected path. Found In Space, Just In Time: Oracle Database 23ai’s Spatio-Temporal Features 11703 Database ramona.magadan@oracle.com Workshop Approved Oracle database technology makes it simple to identify exactly where a point on the surface of the earth is and even the geospatial boundary it’s within. But starting in Oracle Database 23ai, it’s now possible to track positions within spatiotemporal dimensions, so it’s now possible to build sophisticated logistics and position tracking applications on a grand scale. Oracle 23ai’s advanced spatio-temporal features offer the ability to not only identify exactly where a point on the surface of the earth is and what geography it lies within, but now also when a particular object has entered, remained within, and finally left the confines of a specific geospatial boundary. 
We’ll show how these new abilities make it possible to build sophisticated logistics and tracking geospatial applications at scale using a real-world example: identifying which electric vehicles (EVs) are approaching, currently using, just leaving, or circling a large-scale EV charging station.
This session will:
- Explain Oracle Database 23ai spatio-temporal features
- Explore the potential logistics and tracking capabilities now made possible through this feature set
- Demonstrate how these features can be leveraged within a sample APEX application Individual author Individual Content to review/remove Missing LiveLabs ID in current WMS export; review as a draft or unpublished row 11703 Workshop Approved Database 2025-09-09 2024-07-31 Individual author Individual No Repository Url 11703 Workshop Approved Database 2025-09-09 2024-07-31 Individual author Individual No Repository Url No repository URL is present in the current WMS export. ramona.magadan@oracle.com DB Product Management Oracle database technology makes it simple to identify exactly where a point on the surface of the earth is and even the geospatial boundary it’s within. 2. Test replication of data between and across regions
3. Test replication of guest VMs in host VMs deployed in OCI. From Security Events to Attack Paths: Graph-Powered Cyber Threat Hunting 12172 Community karin.patenge@oracle.com Workshop Approved Contributor: Léo Nicolle, Visualization Engineer, Nuix (formerly Linkurious)

Discover how graph technology turns security data into attack maps. Using Oracle Graph and Linkurious Ogma, security teams can connect logs, users, devices, and events to uncover hidden relationships, trace attack paths, spot suspicious patterns, and accelerate threat hunting and incident response. Modern cyberattacks rarely consist of a single suspicious event. Instead, they unfold through a sequence of interconnected actions involving users, systems, devices, network connections, and applications. Understanding these relationships is essential for detecting threats, investigating incidents, and responding effectively. In this session, we demonstrate how graph technology can transform complex security data—such as network logs, authentication records, and security events—into an intuitive graph model that reveals attack paths, hidden relationships, and suspicious patterns. By representing entities as nodes and interactions as edges, investigators can move beyond isolated alerts and gain a complete view of an attack's progression. Using Oracle Graph for in-database graph queries, pattern matching, and graph analytics, together with Linkurious' high-performance Ogma visualization technology, we show how security teams can explore large-scale attack scenarios, identify critical connections, and accelerate threat investigations. Through practical demonstrations, attendees will learn how graph analytics and visualization work together to support cyber threat hunting and incident response.

Learn more:
Getting started with the integration of Ogma with Oracle AI Database 26ai: https://linkurious.github.io/ogma-oracle-parser/getting-started.html

Fusion AI Agentic solutions for Oracle Cloud EPM 12042 4368 Other - I don't see it ramona.magadan@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed The workshop will provide a step-by-step guide to enable connection and basic EPM tasks from Fusion AI Agent Studio. Currently, there are no business objects available for Oracle EPM. The workshop will show how to use External REST API to create meaninful EPM use cases. Author: Vatsal Gaonkar, Director - Oracle Cloud & Digital, PwC

records.searchable: Gain a competitive edge with Generative AI, use AI to generate the Edge and Vertices that make Property Graph data structures 11883 4174 Database - Spatial and Graph jadd.jennings@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed This workshop will show users how to extract relational data from a vectorized text file and use the data to create property graph data structures for exploration. Also we use the graph as RAG for generative AI. Have you heard of Sherlock Holmes? If not, he's one of the greatest detectives in the world of fictional novels. This workshop will take you thru the compelling journey of “The Adventure of the Blue Carbuncle”, its a Sherlock Holmes story written by Arthur Conan Doyal and is now in the public domain. We will walk thru loading the text of the story into an Autonomous database as unstructured data and then embedding it into many chunks. You will sequentially send each chunk to Generative AI services within a prompt and ask the model to extract relationships in JSON form. The results of the response will then be transformed with pl/sql to produce a property graph. We will then use Graph Studio to explore the story based on the edges and vertices of the property graph. And finally, we will use property graph queries for retrieval augmented generation to generate new content based on the property graph relationships. Galactic Exploration with OCI Vision 11181 3448 AI Services OCI - Data Science Product Management Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Explore the universe to recognize galaxies, nebulas, and planets in space telescope images with the help of OCI Vision. By experiencing this hands-on lab, you’ll learn how to train and use a custom image object-detection model to process and explore space images—no data science experience required and no code required. OCI Vision is an AI service that includes a feature to detect objects in images. The object detection feature is pre-trained to detect many types of common objects. However users can also retrain the service with their own data to detect objects not recognized by the pre-trained model. This workshop will take the user through the steps needed to prepare images and retrain object detection in OCI Vision. The image data used is from space telescopes and OCI Vision will be trained to detect and identify planetary and galactic images. No data science experience or machine learning experience is required.
	• Discover how to use OCI Vision and OCI Data Labeling.
	• Create a custom object detection model without machine learning experience.
	• Practice applying a re-trained model to real-world data. Generate regulatory documents for compliance submissions with OCI Generative AI 11685 4028 AI Services rajib.g.ghosh@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Completed In this hands-on lab, we will show how to auto-generate and fill documents for compliance submissions to regulatory authorities. This lab uses OCI Generative AI toolsets to generate custom content from the organizational dataset. Learn more about the automation steps that can be adopted to scale it across the enterprise knowledge base. Organizations today are challenged with analyzing large amounts of structured and unstructured data such as tables, invoices, reports for compliance reporting to regulatory authorities accurately. This requires analyzing, filtering and summarizing large volume of textual and tabular data that are typically resident in an enterprise lakehouse, on-premise servers and cloud. Producing outputs accurately and timely that conforms to a form template is a big time and effort consuming task and hence enterprises are looking to Artificial Intelligence to solve this issue.
    So, in this hands-on lab, we will show how you can auto-generate and fill up compliance forms summarizing information from a pool of  PDF documents to submit to regulatory authorities. This lab uses OCI Generative AI tool sets to generate custom content from a healthcare organization clinical trial dataset. 
To maintain generic nature of the lab and data compliance, all source clinical trial data is auto-generated by OCI Generative AI model such as Cohere Command R+.
Learn more about the architecture, methodology and the key automation steps that can be adopted to scale compliance document generation across your enterprise knowledge base. Generative Data-Centric Application Development 11929 4250 Database kishy.kumar@oracle.com Workshop Publish Requested Public In Development Join this workshop to discover how AI can accelerate the creation of data-centric applications. Learn to use Oracle Database GenDev AI to automatically generate data access APIs, database objects, and data privacy policies by breaking down an application into modules. We will use Oracle APEX AI Assistant to create UI on these APIs and also showcase how you can leverage MCP to connect with GenDev. In this hands-on workshop, you'll learn how artificial intelligence is transforming the way data-centric applications are built. We'll demonstrate how you can leverage Oracle Database GenDev AI to automatically and reliably generate robust data access APIs and database objects by modularizing your application design. Using a real-world scenario—a sample conference management system—you’ll see how application modules are decomposed and the corresponding APIs are created.

Next, we'll show how Oracle Application Express (APEX) AI Assistant can rapidly generate the user interface for your app, sitting seamlessly on top of the generated APIs. The workshop will dive deep into defining, iterating, and enforcing data privacy and role-based access control rules within the application.

Finally, you’ll discover how next-generation multi-modal clients, such as Claude Desktop, can interact with Oracle GenDev MCP Server. We'll demonstrate generating APIs and application code simply by describing your requirements using a large language model (LLM), making application development more accessible and efficient. This session is ideal for developers, architects, and tech leaders seeking to make the most of AI in enterprise application development. records.searchable: Get faster data insights using serverless spark on OCI Data Flow 11205 OCI sujoy.chowdhury@oracle.com Workshop Approved In this workshop, you will create a spark application iteratively on OCI Data Flow using standard developer and data science tools. OCI Data Flow is a fully managed Apache Spark service that unlocks big data analysis without the overheads of infrastructure provisioning and management. Data Flow is server less, so it handles the cluster provisioning, network setup and teardown when Spark jobs are complete. Storage and security are also managed in a cloud native way, which means less work is required for creating and managing Spark applications. Data Flow has deep integrations with OCI Shell Code Editor and Data Science notebooks, so developers can build their Spark apps iteratively. That includes Spark Streaming apps to perform cloud ETL on their continuously produced streaming data. In this tutorial, you will learn how Data Flow enables developers to do rapid application delivery because they can focus on app development, not infrastructure management. Similarly, data engineers can spend more time on their data pipelines, and data scientists can iterate faster on their machine learning models. Using the DBMS_CLOUD_AI_AGENT package, learn how to use this simple framework to build, deploy, and manage AI agents. Build custom tools using PL/SQL. Invoke external tools using REST. Analytic Views provide a dimensional model and calculations that provide a higher level of abstraction over the underlying data, allowing users to access and analyze the data in a more meaningful way. An Analytic View is a type of view in the Oracle Database that allows users to perform complex queries and calculations on data stored in one or more tables. These views provide a higher level of abstraction over the underlying data, allowing users to access and analyze the data in a more meaningful way. They are typically used in business intelligence and data warehousing applications, and can be based on a single table or multiple tables joined together.

The Data Studio Analysis application, included with Autonomous Database, includes everything you need to get started with designing Analytic Views.  In this workshop you will create an Analytic View, complete with multiple hierarchies, fact measures and calculated measures. You will also query the Analytic Views using the Analysis applications data viewer.

This Live Lab is designed to be short and approachable.  The Analytic View that you will design is simple and easy to understand. It introduces the business model and key features. You will also use the Analysis tool to view your Analytic View and verify the design. Get Started With MySQL Enterprise Edition 11856 4130 MySQL perside.foster@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed This hands-on workshop is designed to help you get started with MySQL Enterprise Edition, a powerful database management system. You'll learn the fundamentals of installing, configuring, and using MySQL Enterprise Edition, with a focus on its JavaScript Stored Procedure and Function feature. This hands-on workshop is designed to help you get started with MySQL Enterprise Edition, a powerful database management system. You'll learn the fundamentals of installing, configuring, and using MySQL Enterprise Edition, with a focus on its JavaScript Stored Procedure and Function feature.

In this workshop, you'll work through a series of guided tasks and exercises that will help you understand the basics of MySQL Enterprise Edition, including:

Installing and configuring the server
Creating and managing databases
Using JavaScript to create stored procedures and functions
Implementing a LAMP (Linux, Apache, MySQL, and PHP) stack—or a LAMP stack with Python/Flask instead of Apache/PHP—for web development
Deploying a sample web application, the "Sakila Film Time Converter", which demonstrates the use of MySQL JavaScript functions
By the end of this workshop, you'll have a solid foundation in MySQL Enterprise Edition and be able to start building your own databases and applications. Our goal is to provide you with a comprehensive and practical introduction to MySQL Enterprise Edition. In this workshop, you will learn how to use Oracle Cloud APM to analyze application data, identify symptoms, and trace issues down to their root causes in monitored GenAI and cloud-native applications.

You will begin by using the Inferencing App dashboard to analyze GenAI application data and drill down into trace details. You will also examine data captured for cloud-native service applications, including performance alarms, synthetic monitor activities, and server-side insights using the APM Trace Explorer. Get started with OKE Virtual Nodes and deploying the MuShop App (eCommerce demo app) 11416 3755 OCI orlando.gentil@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA In this workshop, you will learn how to provision Oracle Container Engine for Kubernetes (OKE) with Virtual Nodes and Deploy the MuShop e-Commerce demo app with few commands. In this workshop, you will learn how to provision Oracle Container Engine for Kubernetes (OKE) with Virtual Nodes and Deploy the MuShop e-Commerce demo app with few commands.

OKE virtual nodes deliver a complete serverless Kubernetes experience. With virtual nodes, you can ensure reliable operations of Kubernetes at scale without needing to manage any worker node infrastructure. This cluster option provides granular pod-level elasticity and pay-per-pod pricing, while eliminating the operational overhead of managing, scaling, upgrading, and troubleshooting worker nodes’ infrastructure. Kubernetes clusters become fully managed. Oracle manages clusters’ control plane and data plane for you. You’re responsible only for the applications deployed through the cluster’s Kubernetes API. Get started with Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Anomaly Detection 5683 819 OCI prasanna.anupindi@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Explore the Anomaly Detection service within the Oracle Cloud AI service group to build your ML model to detect anomalies in production with a few simple steps. Anomaly Detection is the identification of rare items, events, or observations in data that differ significantly from the expectation. This can be used for several scenarios like asset monitoring, maintenance and prognostic surveillance in industries such as utility, aviation and manufacturing.

The core algorithm of our Anomaly Detection service is an Oracle-patented multivariate time-series anomaly detection algorithm originally developed by Oracle Labs and had been successfully used in several industries for prognosis analysis.

The Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Anomaly Detection will create customized Machine Learning models by taking the data uploaded by users, using the core algorithm to train the model, and hosted in the cloud to be ready for detection. Users can then send new data to the detection endpoints to get detected anomaly results.

In this workshop, we want to help users achieve the following objectives:

Understand a high level overview of the OCI Anomaly Detection Service
Understand the full cycle/workflow of univariate anomaly detection service provided in the OCI Anomaly Detection
Understand the full cycle/workflow of multivariate anomaly detection service provided in the OCI Anomaly Detection
Hand-on activities to experience the whole pipeline of machine learning model development from training to detecting
(In Advanced Sessions) Learn to use REST API to interact with Anomaly Detection service

The labs in this workshop cover an introduction to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Core Services, including virtual cloud networks (VCN), compute and storage services. These labs also provide some of the foundational skills and knowledge you'll need to attempt the [Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Certification](https://www.oracle.com/cloud/iaas/training/foundations.html) offered by Oracle University.

The Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Certification provides candidates with foundational knowledge of core cloud computing concepts and an understanding of those services in Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. The certification is intended for candidates with technical and non-technical backgrounds who want to validate their understanding of Oracle Cloud infrastructure.

Get started with Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Data Catalog 6882 919 OCI rashmi.badan@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Introduction to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Data Catalog, learn the basics! This workshop introduces you to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Data Catalog and will give you a full tour of the service in a hands-on manner. Data Analysts, Data engineers and Data Stewards are some of the data professionals who can use Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Data Catalog and would benefit from this Live Lab.

In this Live Lab, you will create a catalog, connect to data sources like Autonomous Data Warehouse and Object Storage, harvest metadata from them and enrich the technical metadata with business context. Finally, you will see how the catalog can be used to search, discover and understand data available in the data sources. Get started with Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Forecasting 8561 927 OCI OCI Product Management Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Complete Get started with Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Forecasting Forecasting is a common data science problem that aids companies with effective and efficient planning, goal setting and to forecast future business outcomes like demand etc. OCI TSF service uses data science and machine learning to deliver high quality and reliable forecasts. It is fully managed, serverless and multi-tenant service, accessible over REST APIs. Forecasting methods can be simple statistical models or highly complex, such as machine learning models using neural networks etc.

Users can then send new data to the endpoints to get the forecast results of desired horizon. In this workshop, we want to help users achieve the following objective:
The users will be able submit historical data as inline data via end-points and get forecast

In addition to providing forecasts, this service also focuses on explaining predictions from the model by leveraging state-of-the-art Model Explainability techniques. Get started with Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Language 6181 887 OCI sahil.kalra@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Explore the OCI Language within the AI Service group to perform NLP tasks like detecting languages, extracting key elements, classifying intent, detecting the sentiment, etc., in the text with a few simple steps. Enterprise textual data has significant value related to core business activities and their customers. To gain business and customer insights effectively and at scale from this text data, natural language processing capabilities are needed. For example, identifying key requirements in RFPs to respond effectively or understand customer perception of their products to address gaps.  Some core language processing capabilities include detecting languages, translating content, extracting key elements, classifying intent and detecting the sentiment expressed in the text. These capabilities are typically machine learning algorithms custom built, tuned by Data Scientists and productized for use in applications. Doing this is a time consuming and expensive proposition. 

OCI Language service reduces this time and effort, by providing key language processing capabilities via production ready REST APIs. The service enables applications to automate sophisticated text analysis at scale without needing ML expertise. The service functionality is implemented with pre-trained ML models which are often useful. They may also be further customized to understand the language patterns of the customer’s context by providing additional data.These capabilities are expected of and provided by all hyperscale public clouds. Get Started with Oracle Data Science Agent 12049 4468 AI/ML Database moitreyee.hazarika@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Learn how to use the Data Science Agent component available through the Oracle Machine Learning user interface on Autonomous AI Database Serverless. The Oracle Data Science Agent is a new Oracle Machine Learning (OML) feature in Oracle Autonomous AI Database that brings a modern, chat-based experience to the full data science lifecycle, running entirely in-database. It lowers the barrier to analytics and machine learning for every skill level, accelerates expert workflows by automating repeatable steps, and preserves governance by operating fully within the database. Whether you are a business analyst, a data scientist, or an application developer, the agent provides a secure, explainable, and efficient way to work with data directly where it lives.

Red Bull Racing Honda and Oracle bring data-driven insight to octane-powered races with machine learning.

Join this hands-on-class to learn how to use the new Exadata Database Service on Exascale to take advantage of advanced snapshot and cloning capabilities to reduce storage costs and enhance platform flexibility to increase the benefit of running production, disaster recovery and development databases on Exadata. 

Oracle Exadata Database Service on Exascale Infrastructure is a cutting-edge solution designed to address critical challenges in enterprise database management. Organizations face multiple pain points today, including inefficient storage utilization, complex database provisioning processes, performance bottlenecks, escalating costs, and limited scalability. The Exadata Database Service on Exascale Infrastructure offers a comprehensive approach to these challenges through innovative redirect-on-write storage technology, space-efficient snapshots and clones, simplified provisioning workflows, and elastic scalability capabilities.

Learn how Oracle Exadata Database Service on Exascale Infrastructure enables organizations to optimize their database operations, enhance resource utilization, improve application performance, and achieve greater business agility through dynamic resource allocation. Ultimately, look to the future to support strategic business initiatives while reducing the total cost of ownership. Exascale is a multitenant, hyper-elastic intelligent data architecture that delivers all the advantages of Exadata with all the benefits of modern clouds. Join this hands-on class to learn how to use Oracle Exadata Database Service on Exascale Infrastructure on Oracle Database@Azure.  Exascale on Oracle Database@Azure Delivers Power and Flexibility. With Oracle Exadata Database Service on Exascale Infrastructure on Oracle Database@Azure, users can provision and manage smaller database workloads and scale as needed while leveraging the power of Exadata. Exascale is a multitenant, hyper-elastic intelligent data architecture that delivers all the advantages of Exadata with all the benefits of modern clouds. The Exascale intelligent storage cloud and a pool of Exascale database-optimized compute provide scalable shared resources in the cloud while still meeting even the most demanding workload requirements. You can start with a small VM cluster and a small amount of storage and easily scale as needs grow. With the introduction of Exascale infrastructure, the benefits of Oracle Exadata Database Service are now available for workloads at any scale.

Learn how Oracle Exadata Database Service on Exascale Infrastructure enables organizations to optimize their database operations, enhance resource utilization, improve application performance, and achieve greater business agility through dynamic resource allocation. Get Started with Oracle Globally Distributed Exadata Database on Exascale Infrastructure 12003 ExaCS/ExaCC/DBCS leo.alvarado@oracle.com Workshop Completed Join this hands-on workshop to get started with Oracle Globally Distributed Exadata Database on Exascale Infrastructure. Learn how to build and manage a globally distributed database using Exascale’s cloud-native architecture, which delivers Exadata performance with elastic scaling, high availability, and simplified operations. Join this hands-on workshop to explore how to build and operate a globally distributed database using Oracle Globally Distributed Exadata Database on Exascale Infrastructure. This next-generation platform combines the power of sharding, built-in Raft replication, and Exascale architecture to deliver a fully managed, cloud-native database service designed for mission-critical applications.

Modern applications require global scalability, continuous availability, and low-latency access to data across regions. Traditional database architectures often struggle to meet these demands without added complexity. In this workshop, you will learn how Oracle addresses these challenges by enabling seamless data distribution across geographically dispersed environments while maintaining strong consistency and zero data loss.

Through a series of guided, hands-on labs, you will actively build, configure, and manage a distributed database environment on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). You will provision Exadata resources on Exascale Infrastructure, configure networking and security, and deploy a globally distributed database architecture. You will also work with core components such as shards and catalog databases, and perform key lifecycle operations including scaling and resource management.

This workshop highlights the advantages of Exascale Infrastructure, which decouples compute and storage to provide independent scaling, on-demand resource allocation, and consumption-based efficiency. You will experience how this architecture simplifies operations while delivering the performance, reliability, and automation expected from Exadata.

By the end of this workshop, you will have a solid understanding of how to:

- Deploy and manage a globally distributed database architecture
- Scale databases horizontally by adding and managing shards
- Configure high availability using Raft-based replication
- Monitor and manage performance across distributed environments
- Leverage OCI capabilities for secure, resilient, and scalable deployments

Whether you are a database administrator, cloud architect, or developer, this workshop will equip you with the knowledge and practical experience needed to design and operate globally distributed, enterprise-scale database systems with confidence. Get started with Oracle GoldenGate for Big Data 1780 692 Developers - On Premises brian.r.elliott@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Create Realtime Changed Data to Big Data Targets with GoldenGate for BigData and Microservices This hands-on lab is designed to demonstrate how Oracle GoldenGate Classic and GoldenGate 21.1 Microservices can be used to setup a replication environment by using a mix of web interface, shell scripts and Rest API interfaces. All labs will use shell scripts to facilitate the building of the environment, at the same time provide insight into how to use the web pages and the GoldenGate AdminClient to manage GoldenGate from both Windows and Linux.

The labs will walk the end-user through how to add all components of Oracle GoldenGate replication. To do the instantiation of the target database, the end-user will be performing a data pump export and import. All replication process will be started as they are built. Our source data changes are generated by Classic GoldenGate and trail file changes will be received into the GoldenGate Microservices Target. records.searchable:
Get Started with Oracle Query Service 12014 OCI lauran.serhal@oracle.com Workshop Approved Oracle Query Service makes it easy to run secure Oracle SQL queries across sources like OCI Object Storage and Delta Sharing tables. There’s no database setup or maintenance required—just start querying. Pay only for the compute you use. Access the service through the OCI Console, APIs, or Oracle client tools. Oracle Query Service is an OCI native, serverless platform for running Oracle SQL across multiple data sources—no database provisioning or management required. 

Projects, the service's core organizational unit, group related tables, views, worksheets, and queries. Each project can access various sources: 

 

OCI Object Storage (with direct querying) 

Delta Sharing providers (for interoperable data sharing and synchronization) 

Pre-defined public datasets 

You can also create tables from query results or ingest data from public HTTP/HTTPS endpoints. 

 

Submit queries using three main interfaces: 

 

OCI Console UI (with graphical query builder and worksheets) 

REST and SDK APIs 

Direct SQL client connections (JDBC, SQL Developer, SQL*Net) 

 

Worksheets help manage multiple queries but are UI-only—they can't be accessed via APIs. All queries are billed per Enterprise Compute (ECPU) resources used, with compute provisioned on demand. No persistent database is linked to any project. 

 

Query results land in a staging area and are kept for three days by default. You can export results to your OCI Object Storage or materialize them as new project tables. Pagination for results is available through all interfaces. Security relies on OCI Identity and Access Management (IAM), with permissions at project and query execution levels, plus network access controls for direct connections. 

 

Delta Sharing lets you list, update, and delete providers, browse shared tables, and synchronize data either on demand or by schedule. Synchronized tables become native within the project, available for queries and views. 

 

Oracle Query Service supports full Oracle SQL syntax and semantics, working seamlessly with Oracle Database tools and APIs. It fits teams needing flexible, secure analytics across diverse data sources. Typical uses: 

 

Exploring large datasets in object storage 

Federated querying via Delta Sharing 

Prototyping and experimentation 

Operational analytics without the cost of dedicated databases 

 

With Oracle Query Service, organizations can simplify data exploration, processing, and delivery—while preserving security, governance, and cost efficiency. Get Started with Select AI for Java 12076 AI/ML Database sarika.surampudi@oracle.com Workshop Approved In this workshop, learn how to use the Java API for NL2SQL, RAG, and AI Agents, among other Select AI features. Then, use the Ask Oracle chatbot for no-code interaction. Select AI for Java enables you to ask questions about your database data using natural language (NL2SQL), receive generative AI responses using your trusted content (retrieval-augmented generation), generate synthetic data using large language models, and more – all from Java.  With Select AI for Java, you can leverage the broader Java ecosystem in combination with Oracle’s database functionality and generative AI capabilities – bridging the gap between the Select AI’s DBMS_CLOUD_AI PL/SQL package and Java’s rich ecosystem. It provides objects and methods for AI model interaction.

Get Started with Select AI for Python 12048 AI/ML Database sarika.surampudi@oracle.com Workshop Approved In this workshop, learn how to use the Python API for NL2SQL, feedback, chat, summarization, translation, and synthetic data generation. You will also use the Ask Oracle Select AI chatbot for no-code interaction. Select AI for Python enables you to ask questions about your database data using natural language (NL2SQL), generate synthetic data using large language models, and text summarization and translation – all from Python.  With Select AI for Python, you can leverage the broader Python ecosystem in combination with Oracle’s database functionality and generative AI capabilities – bridging the gap between the Select AI’s DBMS_CLOUD_AI PL/SQL package and Python’s rich ecosystem. With Lakehouse, you can query hundreds of terabytes of data in Object Storage and optionally combine it with transactional data in MySQL databases without copying the data from the Object Storage into the MySQL database. In this workshop, get hands-on experience and learn how to use HeatWave Lakehouse on AWS. With Lakehouse, you can query hundreds of terabytes of data in Object Storage and optionally combine it with transactional data in MySQL databases without copying the data from the object store into the MySQL database. You can also perform machine learning (ML) tasks, like training, predictions, and explanations on this data. Querying data in the object store is as fast as querying the data in the database. HeatWave Lakehouse scales out to 512 nodes and allows customers to query up to half a petabyte of data on a single HeatWave cluster. records.searchable: Getting started with OCI Data Science 1860 673 OCI Data Science wendy.yip@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Explore concepts used in the Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Data Science service to speed up your workflow and make you more productive. The Oracle Data Science Service is a fully managed, self-service platform for data science teams to build, train, and manage machine learning (ML) models in Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. This lab will introduce the Accelerated Data Science SDK, showing you how it can speed up your workflow and make you more productive. In this module, we will build a binary classification model in an effort to predict employee attrition. Using the Accelerated Data Science (ADS) SDK we will do an exploratory data analysis (EDA) to understand the nature and distribution of the data. We will visualize the data and assess the correlation between predictors. The Oracle AutoML tools will be used to perform and automatically tune Light Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), XG Boost, Random Forest and Logistic Regression classifiers. These models will be evaluated and compared using ADS' model evaluation tools. Once the best model is selected, we will use the machine learning explainability (MLX) tools to explain the global and local behavior of the model. That is, we will see what features are important in the model using feature permutation importance, partial dependence plots (PDP), individual conditional expectation (ICE) and several other methods used to determine why the model made the prediction that it did. Getting Started with OCI Internet of Things Platform 12177 OCI pete.st.pierre@oracle.com Workshop Submitted Learn how to use OCI IoT Platform digital twins to model, connect, and monitor physical devices. Create an asset hierarchy, build reusable equipment and component models, configure adapters, create twin instances, send telemetry through HTTP, and verify data in the OCI CLI and Console. Organizations across manufacturing, energy, utilities, transportation, logistics, retail, healthcare, and smart buildings depend on physical assets that must operate reliably. Pumps, motors, compressors, refrigeration units, conveyors, generators, vehicles, and other equipment produce valuable operational data, but that data often remains isolated in vendor systems or arrives in inconsistent formats.
This hands-on workshop introduces OCI Internet of Things Platform and its digital twin capabilities through a practical equipment-monitoring scenario that applies across industries. You will learn how to represent physical assets and their relationships in a shared digital model, connect telemetry from different sources, and use incoming data to understand equipment condition and performance.
You begin by setting up the OCI resources needed for the workshop and reviewing a realistic operational use case. The scenario uses a hierarchy of sites, operational areas, and equipment, but the same approach can represent a factory with production lines, a utility network with pumping stations, a fleet with vehicles, a hospital with critical systems, or a building portfolio with HVAC equipment.
Next, you create a digital representation of the asset environment. You model a parent facility and define related operating areas without requiring each entity to connect directly to a device. This captures the business and physical context around connected equipment. For example, a pump can belong to a production line, a compressor can serve a refrigeration zone, or a vehicle can operate within a fleet and depot structure.
You then build reusable digital twin models for equipment and its components. The workshop uses a water-pump model that includes a motor component, demonstrating how to compose a complete asset from smaller reusable models. You define telemetry properties such as flow rate, pressure, motor temperature, vibration, and power consumption. These properties use quantitative data types, validation rules, and history so teams can capture measurements consistently, reject invalid values, and review changes over time.
The workshop also covers digital twin adapters. Real devices and control systems rarely publish telemetry in the same structure, even when they report the same measurement. You create a default adapter and a flat telemetry adapter to map different payload formats to the shared digital twin model. This pattern helps organizations normalize telemetry from equipment supplied by different vendors, deployed at different sites, or connected through different gateways.
After defining the models and adapters, you create digital twin instances for individual assets and establish relationships between facilities, operating areas, equipment, and components. In the final lab, you send telemetry through HTTP, verify data ingestion with the OCI CLI, and view asset data in the OCI Console.

Getting Started With Oracle Access Governance 11496 3855 OCI anuj.t.tripathi@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA This workshop walks you through the steps to get started using Oracle Access Governance with use cases including access controls implementation, user access reviews, and enterprise-wide visibility for systems managed using Access Governance. This workshop walks you through the steps to get started using Oracle Access Governance to understand use cases such as access controls implementation, user access reviews, and enterprise-wide visibility for systems managed using Access Governance. 

Oracle Access Governance is a cloud-native identity governance and administration (IGA) service that provides enterprise-wide visibility to govern access to cloud and on-premises environments. With an intuitive user experience, dynamic access control, and a prescriptive analytics–driven access review process, it helps customers automate access provisioning, get insights into access permission and cloud infrastructure policy reviews, identify anomalies, and remediate security risks. Oracle Access Governance allows:
    Administrator to perform various system, service, and access control administrative tasks
    Campaign administrator to run intelligent access review campaigns for access governance and compliance
    Cloud Access Reviewers to review policy access insights and take informed decisions based on prescriptive analytics
    Users and user managers to validate access assigned to self and their direct reports, respectively.
    Access Control Administrator to automate access through Access Bundles, Roles, Identity Collections, Policies, and Approval Workflows.
    Users to request access provisioned various target systems

This lab walks you through the steps to get started using Oracle Access Governance with several use cases - access controls, access reviews, and enterprise-wide access browsing. In this workshop, a fictitious corporation is using Oracle Access Governance to manage and govern the application access of its employees and contractors. This lab shows how the database is connected to AG as a target system and implement access control by creating identity collections, approval workflows, roles, access bundles, and centralized policies. It also shows how to perform access review campaigns, and associated review tasks. Getting Started With Oracle Database Transactional Event Queues (TxEventQ) 8021 1016 Developers - Converged anders.swanson@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete This lab will provide you with a basic understanding of Oracle Database Transactional Event Queues, enabling you to leverage its powerful features for building robust, event-driven messaging systems. Oracle Transactional Event Queues (TxEventQ) is a messaging platform built into Oracle Database that combines the best features of messaging and pub/sub systems. TxEventQ was introduced as a rebranding of AQ Sharded Queues in Oracle Database 21c, evolving from the Advanced Queuing (AQ) technology that has been part of Oracle Database since version 8.0. TxEventQ continues to evolve in Oracle Database 23ai, with Kafka Java APIs, Oracle REST Data Services (ORDS) integration, and many more features and integrations.

TxEventQ is designed for high-throughput, reliable messaging in event-driven microservices and workflow applications. It supports multiple publishers and consumers, exactly-once message delivery, and robust event streaming capabilities. On an 8-node Oracle Real Application Clusters (RAC) database, TxEventQ can handle approximately 1 million messages per second, demonstrating its scalability. records.searchable:
Gimme a Vector, Victor: Deploying Oracle Database 23ai VECTOR Datatype for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) 11702 4124 AI/ML Database ramona.magadan@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Completed The new VECTOR datatype in Oracle Database 23ai enables vector embedding—a key requirement for Generative AI applications—as well as vector indexing to enable an LLM to speedily search a corpus through chatbots and other applications using Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) to answer business questions. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), when enabled through Oracle Database 23ai’s new VECTOR datatype, makes it simple to build APEX and analytic applications that leverage Large Language Models (LLMs) to solve complex business problems, even when the end user doesn’t even know what specific questions to ask. 
This lab demonstrates:
- The basics of VECTORs and how they’re useful for LLMs and RAG

GoldenGate for Distributed Applications and Analytics 23ai 11740 GoldenGate deniz.sendil@oracle.com Workshop In Development GoldenGate for Distributed Applications and Analytics 23ai has a new UI and supports news source and target technologies. This lab is going to help customers and fields. This lab can be used for on-boarding activities, enablement sessions and demonstrations. This lab will support various use cases including Delta Lakes, Message Streaming and MongoDB to Oracle migrations. This hands-on lab is designed to demonstrate how Oracle GoldenGate Microservices Architecture and Oracle GoldenGate (MA) for Big Data can be used to set up a replication environment by a mix of web pages, shell scripts, and Rest API interfaces. All labs will use shell scripts to facilitate the building of the environment while providing insight into how to use the web pages and AdminClient. The labs will walk the end-user through how to add all components of Oracle GoldenGate replication. This hands-on lab focuses on GoldenGate Real-Time Data Replication demonstrating five scenarios that you can use (both on-premise and in the cloud) to capture real-time data changes from your sources.

All labs will use shell scripts to facilitate the building of the environment while providing insight into how to use the web pages and AdminClient. The labs will walk the end-user through how to add all components of Oracle GoldenGate replication. This hands-on lab focuses on GoldenGate Real-Time Data Replication demonstrating five scenarios that you can use (both on-premise and in the cloud) to capture real-time data changes from your sources.

HOL2810-Build an AI Agent for GoldenGate Data streams and JSON-relational duality view 11911 4220 GoldenGate denis.gray@oracle.com Workshop Published Event Completed In this hands-on lab, you'll learn how to build an AI-powered agent that interacts with real-time data from OCI GoldenGate using Data Streams and JSON-relational duality views. You'll configure GoldenGate to stream database changes as JSON payloads, then run an AI agent that consumes this stream, interprets the data in real-time, and responds to natural language queries. In this hands-on lab, you will build an intelligent AI agent that integrates with OCI GoldenGate Data Streams and leverages the power of JSON-relational duality views to deliver real-time insights and recommendations. The lab focuses on a practical, event-driven use case using live cart order data, where the AI agent performs semantic search across other orders to dynamically suggest items that a customer might want to add to their cart—enabling an intelligent, personalized shopping experience powered by streaming data.
As part of the lab, you will:
	•	Configure OCI GoldenGate to stream real-time transactional data as JSON payloads using Data Streams.
	•	Create and work with Oracle Database 23ai JSON-relational duality views to bridge structured and semi-structured data, enabling flexible access to both traditional relational schemas and modern JSON formats.
	•	Build an AI agent capable of understanding user queries in natural language and translating them into meaningful actions, such as recommending products or retrieving operational metrics.
	•	Implement real-time semantic search logic to analyze current cart contents and suggest complementary products based on patterns in past orders.
	•	Integrate a conversational interface that allows users to query GoldenGate operational metrics (e.g., lag, status, throughput) via chat, using natural language.
This lab demonstrates how you can combine Oracle's cutting-edge data streaming technology with AI to build context-aware, real-time, and highly responsive applications. It's ideal for developers, architects, and data engineers looking to explore the future of event-driven AI systems powered by Oracle technologies. Host a Highly Available MySQL-Backed WordPress Website with OCI Core Services 11412 3702 OCI bernardo.castro.chalate@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Learn how to set up your own website using OCI Core Services such as VCN, Compute Instances, Load Balancers, DNS, and MySQL Database. Additionally, find out how you can develop it for your needs using OS Management. In this workshop, you will learn how to set up a highly-available website architecture and get introduced to some of Oracle Cloud Infrastructure's (OCI) services. 

You will be walked through step-by-step in provisioning a Virtual Cloud Network to contain your instances, a compute instance that will run WordPress for a website you can easily customize, and a MySQL database to store your data. Additionally, we will take a look at some useful networking features such as load balancers for high availability and DNS to create a web page address. Lastly, you will learn to use OS Management continuously develop your website's design as it grows.

This lab will walk users with little to no experience with cloud infrastructure services. How Generative AI helps you build smarter applications 11655 4016 AI Services anshuman.p.panda@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Completed Learn how to embed OCI Generative AI in your applications and solve real business challenges – like document summarization, natural language conversations grounded in documents, website content, transcriptions from videos and more. Leverage OCI and open frameworks to improve productivity and efficiency of your applications. In this lab, you will explore the power of OCI Generative AI and its potential to revolutionize your applications. Through hands-on exercises, you'll learn how to integrate Generative AI into your solutions to tackle real-world business challenges, such as document summarization, natural language conversations grounded in documents, content generation for websites, video transcriptions, and more.

We'll begin with an overview of the services and frameworks utilized in this lab, followed by a series of practical exercises. These exercises will guide you through setting up your environment, building and testing a Gen AI chat application, interacting with PDF documents, comparing files, summarizing content, and more. By the end of this lab, you'll have the skills to leverage OCI Generative AI to enhance the productivity and efficiency of your applications.

Agenda:

Introduction
Get an overview of the lab objectives and the impact of Generative AI on modern applications.

Demo of Applications
Preview the applications you'll be building during the lab.

Review of Services and Frameworks
Explore the OCI services and open frameworks that you'll use to implement AI-driven solutions.

Lab 1: Setting Up and Testing the Environment
Prepare your environment and ensure that all necessary tools and services are correctly configured.

Lab 2: Gen AI Chat App
Build a chat application powered by Generative AI, enabling natural language interactions.

Lab 3: Chat With PDF Documents
Implement a feature allowing users to chat and extract information from PDF documents.

Lab 4: Compare PDF Files
Learn how to compare and contrast content across multiple PDF files using Generative AI.

Lab 5: Document Summarization
Automatically generate concise summaries of documents to save time and enhance productivity.

Lab 6: Chat and Summarize Web Pages
Extend your application's capabilities to interact with and summarize web pages.

Lab 7: Chat and Summarize YouTube Videos
Integrate AI to transcribe and summarize content from YouTube videos, making information more accessible.

Outcome:
By completing this lab, you will gain hands-on experience in embedding OCI Generative AI into various applications, empowering you to create smarter, more efficient solutions for real-world challenges. In this lab, you will explore the power of OCI Generative AI and its potential to revolutionize your applications. Through hands-on exercises, you'll learn how to integrate Generative AI into your solutions to tackle real-world business challenges, such as document summarization, natural language conversations grounded in documents, content generation for websites, video transcriptions, and more.

We'll begin with an overview of the services and frameworks utilized in this lab, followed by a series of practical exercises. These exercises will guide you through setting up your environment, building and testing a Gen AI chat application, interacting with PDF documents, comparing files, summarizing content, and more. By the end of this lab, you'll have the skills to leverage OCI Generative AI to enhance the productivity and efficiency of your applications.

Implement a feature allowing users to chat and extract information from PDF documents.

Lab 4: Compare PDF Files
Learn how to compare and contrast content across multiple PDF files using Generative AI.

Lab 5: Document Summarization
Automatically generate concise summaries of documents to save time and enhance productivity.

Lab 6: Chat and Summarize Web Pages
Extend your application's capabilities to interact with and summarize web pages.

Lab 7: Chat and Summarize YouTube Videos
Integrate AI to transcribe and summarize content from YouTube videos, making information more accessible.

Outcome:

How to securely integrate Private Endpoint Large Language Models (LLMs) with Oracle Autonomous Database Select AI 11948 AI/ML Database chandrakanth.putha@oracle.com Workshop Approved Learn how to securely integrate large language models (LLMs) with Oracle Autonomous Database Select AI using private endpoints. This hands-on lab walks you through configuring network isolation, setting up a private LLM host, and enabling Select AI to safely query data. By the end, you’ll know how to combine LLM power with Oracle’s enterprise-grade security. In this hands-on workshop, you will learn how to securely integrate large language models (LLMs) with Oracle Autonomous Database Select AI by leveraging private endpoints. Private endpoints provide network isolation and ensure that communication between your Autonomous Database and AI models does not traverse the public internet, meeting strict enterprise security and compliance requirements.

The lab guides you step-by-step through creating a Virtual Cloud Network (VCN), configuring private endpoints, and deploying a jump server and private LLM host. You will then provision an Autonomous Database instance with Private Endpoint access, install and configure an Ollama AI model, and use it with Select AI for secure natural language prompting.

By the end of this workshop, you will understand how to combine the power of LLMs with Oracle Autonomous Database Select AI. You will be able to build secure, enterprise-ready AI solutions that integrate structured business data and unstructured data with external LLM capabilities — all while maintaining privacy, compliance, and control. Hybrid Search with OCI PostgreSQL 11670 4036 AI Services marc.gueury@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Completed Search Documents using PostgreSQL vector store.
The documents are uploaded to Object Storage, parsed and indexed inside PostgreSQL.
The installation is automated with Terraform.

Using OCI PostgreSQL, OCI Generative AI, OCI Document Understanding, OCI Speech, OCI Vision, and custom binary parser. In today’s modern business world, people want access to information fast, but when it comes to document scans, it can be difficult to access the text from those documents. In this lab, we’ll walk you through automating this process. You’ll upload documents to object storage, extract text and insights using AI Services, and add this information to an OCI PostgreSQL database. The result is that users can more quickly find the content they need and they will be able to compare results of word and semantic search, Generative AI, and RAG. Hybrid Vector Search and Vector Indexes on Iceberg for next-gen AI apps 12152 AI/ML Database andy.rivenes@oracle.com Workshop Approved Build AI applications that deliver more accurate and relevant results across all types of data using advanced vector techniques such as hybrid vector search indexes and vector indexes on iceberg tables. Build AI applications that deliver more accurate and relevant results across all types of data using advanced vector techniques such as hybrid vector search indexes and vector indexes on iceberg tables. In this hands-on lab, you'll learn how to combine semantic vector search with deterministic keyword search to improve retrieval quality for RAG applications, AI agents, and enterprise search and be able to easily run semantic searches against high volume iceberg data in object store.  

You'll create a hybrid index, a vector index on iceberg, execute hybrid queries, and compare the results against traditional vector-only and keyword-only search. Along the way, you'll learn how Hybrid Vector Search improves recall and precision by combining semantic similarity with exact keyword matching—making it easier to retrieve documents containing required entities such as names, products, or locations while still capturing semantic meaning. 

Using Oracle Database, you'll build and optimize hybrid retrieval pipelines through a unified indexing and query interface, leaving with practical techniques for developing production-ready AI applications with more accurate and trustworthy search results. Implement custom authentication in APEX 11049 3315 APEX ana.beyer@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete How to allow end users to create and manage their own account info without access to APEX Workspace. In this workshop you will learn how to create a custom authentication scheme in APEX 
that allows end users to create their own account and manage their own login credentials/information without ever seeing the application’s backend.

In order to achieve this, you will first implement a password hashing function and a user credentials table in the underlying database. You will then create an authentication function that will be called at login. Next you will learn how to put all the pieces together to create your own custom authentication scheme. Finally, you will make use of this new authentication scheme by creating a page in your APEX application that allows end users to create their own account. Additional "bonus" labs are provided to implement additional, related functionality involving account activation and password resetting capabilities. records.searchable: Implement Row-Level Security with Semantic Modeler in OAC 11761 4177 Analytics chenai.jarimani@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed The workshop explains the steps for setting up data filters or row-level security in the semantic modeler to determine what data can be queried by an individual user based on their role. Data-level security defines what a user in an analytics application can access inside a report. When run by two different users, the same report can bring up different data. The structure of the view is the same for all users, unless a user does not have access to the subject area, in which case the report displays an error. Ensuring that only authorized people can access specific data is important to prevent sensitive information from being queried or run. The solution involves using a security table in the database with session variables. The session variable is set when a user logs into  Oracle Analytics to set filters and permissions for the session. Implementing Image and Text Semantic Search in Oracle APEX 11884 4208 APEX sahaana.manavalan@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed In this workshop, you’ll learn how to implement image and text semantic search in Oracle APEX using ONNX models and Oracle Database 23ai’s AI Vector Search. Enhance the Social Media app to search images by meaning using both image and text queries - unlocking smarter, more intuitive search experiences beyond keywords. In today's digital landscape, visual content is everywhere. From product photos and social media posts to scanned documents and user-generated media. The ability to search and understand images meaningfully, not just by filenames or tags, has become a powerful differentiator for modern applications. Traditional search methods often miss the context or content of images, limiting their effectiveness in image-rich environments.

In this workshop, you will learn how to implement image and text semantic search in Oracle APEX using ONNX models and Oracle Database 23ai’s built-in AI Vector Search. You will enhance a Social Media APEX application to intelligently interpret and search image using both text and image queries. By combining deep learning models with APEX, you’ll unlock next-generation search experiences that go beyond keywords - empowering your apps to truly understand what users are looking for. records.rawTitle: Improve application performance with True Cache
records.source: 14 August 2026 WMS and LiveLabs dashboard views; 15 August 2026 GitHub repository census
records.searchable:
Improve application performance with True Cache 11454 3933 Database - MAA sambit.p.panda@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Many large scale Web applications faces performance issues when a a database becomes the bottleneck.

Run this hands-on workshop to learn how to use True Cache to improve scalability by offloading queries and reducing the number of requests and connections to the primary database. Why use True Cache?
True Cache can be used to scale a read-mostly application even without partitioning data. When primary database becomes the bottleneck , True Cache can be used to offload the primary and scale the workload. Also the data is always consistent and recent within a single query, this is important when there are joins across multiple rows.


This usage model of true cache through the JDBC requires minimal application change to use the functionality. Applications connect to only one service. Application uses setReadOnly(true) and setReadOnly(false) calls to mark some sections of code as "read only". If True Cache instances are configured, the JDBC driver will internally maintain, for each logical connection, 2 physical connections, one to a primary instance and one to an True Cache instance. The JDBC driver automatically sends SQL statements in "read-only" blocks to the True Cache instance.

What's in the workshop
This workshop is based on a compute instance (a demo application) connected to a Primary database configured with True Cache. The demo application is a Java program using the 23c JDBC driver. Its simulates a high number of transactions for the primary database and how off loading the read only queries to true cache helps in application performance.

It demonstrates:

How to set up True Cache.
Schema creation and initial data load to the primary database
The demo application shows the transactions running against the primary database and how switching to true cache helps in performance improvement .
