Run this hands-on workshop to learn how to use True Cache to improve scalability by offloading queries and reducing the number of requests and connections to the primary database.

Why use True Cache?
True Cache can be used to scale a read-mostly application even without partitioning data. When primary database becomes the bottleneck , True Cache can be used to offload the primary and scale the workload. Also the data is always consistent and recent within a single query, this is important when there are joins across multiple rows.


This usage model of true cache through the JDBC requires minimal application change to use the functionality. Applications connect to only one service. Application uses setReadOnly(true) and setReadOnly(false) calls to mark some sections of code as "read only". If True Cache instances are configured, the JDBC driver will internally maintain, for each logical connection, 2 physical connections, one to a primary instance and one to an True Cache instance. The JDBC driver automatically sends SQL statements in "read-only" blocks to the True Cache instance.

What's in the workshop
This workshop is based on a compute instance (a demo application) connected to a Primary database configured with True Cache. The demo application is a Java program using the 23c JDBC driver. Its simulates a high number of transactions for the primary database and how off loading the read only queries to true cache helps in application performance.

It demonstrates:

How to set up True Cache.
Schema creation and initial data load to the primary database
The demo application shows the transactions running against the primary database and how switching to true cache helps in performance improvement .

Increase DB security with Connection Manager over SSL Protocol 11173 Database  - Security christopher.guray@oracle.com Workshop Approved 12.2.0.1 and later versions provides a more secure access to the server by supporting SSL protocol. With this support, the database client can communicate to the server through Oracle Connection Manager over TCPS protocol.
The workshop will guide users to create SSL Wallet and to setup TCPS protocal using Connection Manager as an added security. Oracle Connection Manager is a proxy server that forwards connection requests to databases or other proxy servers. It operates on the session level. It usually resides on a computer separate from the database server and client computers.
SSL / TLS is used for encrypting data over network, 
Together with CMAN and TLS,   Oracle 12.2 onwards provides added security in masking the actual DB server details and also have encryption enabled over TCPS at the network level. 
This lab helps customer to setup CMAN for an OCI database and also have traffic sent over using TLS, with an option to encrypt data from client to DB server or between  Client and CMAN layer. records.searchable: Innovate with Autonomous AI Database's built-in Select AI, Graph, ML and Spatial analytics 8081 3156 Developers - Converged michelle.a.malcher@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Learn how to get the most out of your data! Connect to the data lake turn unstructured data into actionable information. Use generative AI with your data to enable natural language queries. Predict customers at risk of churning. Make those customers personalized offers based on geographic location and movie viewing habits. All hands on. All in 90 minutes! This workshop uses Oracle Cloud's modern data platform for analytics to enable MovieStream to better understand their customers, predict churn and provide targeted recommendations and promotions.  We'll start with two key components of MovieSteam's architecture. MovieStream is storing its data across Oracle Object Storage and Autonomous Database. Data is captured from various sources into a landing zone in object storage. That data is enhanced and loaded into an Autonomous Database where it is analyzed by many (and varied) members of the user community - from data analysts to data scientists. These users will take advantage of a variety of Autonomous AI Database capabilities: Select AI to perform natural language queries and analytics, advanced Oracle SQL to glean customer insights, Oracle Machine Learning to predict churn, and Oracle Spatial and Graph to provide targeted promotions. Integrate Oracle Analytics Cloud with Java Management Service 12005 4333 OCI maria.merino.perez@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed This workshop will guide you on the integration of Oracle Analytics with Java Management Service (JMS) on OCI. In this hands-on workshop, will walk you through the process to build a real-time dashboard in Oracle Analytics Cloud (OAC) that allows you observe the use of Java in your enterprise using Java Management Service (JMS).
The session begins with setting up the environment, followed by creating a Fleet and configuring a managed instance within JMS. Participants will then set up an Autonomous AI Database and configure JMS to export relevant instance data—specifically managed instances, java runtimes and applications.
With the export in place, the workshop guides participants through creating an OAC instance, importing a JMS OAC template, and securely connecting OAC to Autonomous AI Database. Finally, attendees will configure periodic data imports in OAC to ensure the dashboard reflects the latest managed instance information.
By the end of the workshop, participants will have a functional OAC dashboard displaying up-to-date IP addresses and host names from JMS, supporting improved visibility of Java resources. records.searchable: Integrate Oracle Data Safe with Applications and Services 11337 3596 Database  - Security jody.glover@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete In this workshop, you learn how to use the Oracle Data Safe REST API and CLI, and use the Event service in Oracle Cloud Infrastructure with Oracle Data Safe. records.searchable: Integrating GoldenGate Microservices and ODI Marketplace 8501 OCI gurudixit.chepuri@oracle.com Workshop Approved The purpose of this LiveLab is to Provide hands-on experience to perform near real-time replication using ODI Marketplace in conjunction with GoldenGate Microservices. Oracle Data Integrator is Oracle’s strategic product for data integration. Using the E-LT (Extract, Load, Transform) methodology to gather data from the source, load it into a staging area, and then perform transformations while loading the final target, ODI uses the power of the database to perform the work, rather than an additional ETL engine. ODI also has its own form of change data capture, which is implemented using a Journalized Knowledge Module. The JKM generates the infrastructure for the CDC, creating journal tables that store the change rows and views that provide access to the change rows for use in ODI Interfaces. ODI CDC can be implemented using various capture processes, such as triggers on source tables, timestamps on rows, or mining of the database logs via Oracle Streams or, in our case, Oracle GoldenGate. Generative AI agents are powerful for reasoning and decision-making, but to be truly useful in enterprise scenarios, they need access to real-world tools and data. This is where the Model Context Protocol (MCP) comes in. MCP allows developers to expose services—such as APIs or business logic—as tools that an agent can call in real time.
In this workshop, we’ll show how to integrate an MCP server with OCI Generative AI Agents, using a simple weather server as an example. By the end, you’ll understand how to extend your OCI agents with domain-specific tools, accelerating automation and enhancing business outcomes. Introduction To Data Science 2060 788 OCI Data Science jeroen.kloosterman@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete If you're a technical professional and you would like to broaden your skillset with Data Science and Machine Learning, then this is the workshop for you! 
In this workshop we will first cover the required theory on Data Science and Machine Learning. After that you will work on several products, such as OCI Data Science, Oracle Machine Learning (in-database), Oracle Analytics Cloud and Graph. Without a doubt, you've heard about the potential of this new field. There are many proven applications throughout industries and business functions, and many new cases are still waiting to be discovered. For the professional, this means that there's an enormous opportunity to ride this wave of innovation.

In this workshop, we will start with the necessary theory on Data Science and Machine Learning. Therefore, no previous knowledge is required. After the theory, we'll move to a product overview and you will get the chance to practice with various products in Oracle Cloud, for example, OCI Data Science, Oracle Machine Learning (in-database), Oracle Analytics Cloud and Graph.

The target audience is people without previous Data Science experience that would like to get started with this new field, for example:
- Application developers that would like to add ML to their applications or business flows.
- Advanced users of analytics that would like to add predictions to their dashboards.
- Database experts that would like to create ML models for data that are stored in databases.
- Other (IT) professionals with technical affinity.

- Learn the required DS/ML theory
- Get a high level overview on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and the architecture for DS/ML
- Learn how to train ML models for a variety of cases (e.g. predict house prices, assess credit rating, predict which customers will be interested in a product)
- Learn to use OCI Data Science
- Learn to use Oracle Machine Learning (in-database)
- Learn to use Oracle Analytics Cloud (specifically ML features)
- Learn how Graph database is related to ML

Introduction to OCI Document Understanding 11295 3585 AI Services guy.michaeli@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Complete This workshop provides an introduction to OCI Document Understanding for both business users and developers. Business users can setup an OCI tenancy to use Document Understanding (Lab 1) and then try out features on different documents (Lab 2). Developers can exercise the REST API using Postman (Lab 3) and execute a Python script that extracts key-value pairs from an invoice (Lab 4). Enterprise document data has significant value related to core business activities and their customers. To gain business and customer insights effectively and at scale from this data, document analysis capabilities are needed. Some core capabilities include classifying documents, extracting text, extracting table information, and extracting key-value pairs from documents. Building these machine learning algorithms from scratch requires extensive time, data, and data science expertise, but OCI Document Understanding gives organizations ready access to these models and capabilities. 

OCI Document Understanding is an AI service that enables developers to extract text, tables, and other valuable data from document files through APIs and command line interface tools. With OCI Document Understanding, you can automate tedious business processing tasks with prebuilt AI models and customize document extraction to fit your industry-specific needs. Introduction to Oracle Machine Learning for R on Oracle Database 6942 3204 AI/ML Database milton.wan@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Learn OML4R for Oracle Database Machine Learning in R with Oracle Database. The lab exercises use different machine learning algorithms to predict outcomes for a customer insurance data set. Oracle Machine Learning for R (OML4R), a component of Oracle Machine Learning on Oracle Database and Oracle Autonomous Database, makes the open-source R scripting language and environment ready for enterprise data. OML4R provides a database-centric environment for end-to-end analytical processes using R. Users invoke overloaded R functions on database-resident data for data exploration and preparation, which leverages the database as a high-performance computing environment. Further, R users can invoke powerful in-database machine learning algorithms from a native R API and deploy user-defined R functions in database-spawned and controlled R engines - all in support of R-based solution development.

OML4R is for those looking to process data in place without moving the data out of the database. This allows you to leverage the high-performance database to process data for data science and machine learning solutions. This workshop guides you through using various OML4R features for data exploration and preparation, and machine learning modeling using in-database algorithms. Java and the Promise of Quantum Computing 11185 3443 Community sharat.chander@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Authors: Johan Vos, Co-Founder of Gluon HQ & Barry Burd, Professor at Drew University.

Explore how to run Java code using Johan Vos's Strange platform and use the code to learn about quantum computing's revolutionary approach to problem-solving. Authors: Johan Vos, Co-Founder of Gluon HQ & Barry Burd, Professor at Drew University.

We've all heard the hype: Quantum computers will leave our current machines wallowing in the dust. Quantum algorithms will crack our existing encryption schemes in seconds. Will it really happen? The answer depends on engineering problems that have yet to be solved. But for those who write code, many insights are already available. In this lab, we'll run Java code using Johan Vos's Strange platform. We'll use the code to learn about quantum computing's revolutionary approach to problem-solving. records.searchable: JavaScript for APEX Developers 11517 3863 APEX yuan.yuan.deng@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Explore the basics of JavaScript, learn how to add JavaScript to APEX apps, and use jQuery to work with the DOM. Welcome to the Introduction to JavaScript for APEX Developers hands-on lab. For developers that know SQL and PL/SQL, no other framework is as empowering as Oracle Application Express (APEX). OCI Database Management provides database performance and management capability for all flavors of Oracle Databases, which significantly reduce the burden on DBA and DevOps staff by providing a lifecycle solution encompassing monitoring, performance management, tuning, and database administration. OCI Database Management is part of the Oracle Cloud Observability and Management platform.

This workshop lists the steps to configure an on-premises Oracle Database (external database) in the Oracle Cloud and use the OCI Database Management to manage that database. records.searchable: [Korean] OCI Configuring File System Storage 11078 OCI sangsu.lee@oracle.com Workshop In Development Create and mount File Storage System to a compute instance. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure File Storage Service provides a durable, scalable, distributed, enterprise-grade network file system. You can connect to a File Storage Service file system from any bare metal, virtual machine, or container instance in your Virtual Cloud Network (VCN). You can also access a file system from outside the VCN using Oracle Cloud Infrastructure FastConnect and Internet Protocol security (IPSec) virtual private network (VPN). records.searchable: Lab - OIC Integration, Process and Insight (Instructor-led version) 9601 OIC - Integration wallence.wong@oracle.com Workshop Approved Use of OIC Integration and Process features to help new hires to learn basics of OIC via labs. The purpose of this lab is to help Oracle new hires understand the features and functionality of Oracle Integration (OIC) so you can represent the product in customer sessions, deliver demonstrations and develop skills to build proof-of-concept (POC) projects for customers. You will use THREE key capabilities of Oracle Integration (Integration, Process Automation & Insight Analytics capabilities) to address the use case challenge by developing an integration and a process automation application. In this training, you will complete three labs. In Lab 1, you will use the Integration component of Oracle Integration (OIC) to build an application integration that will be used in Lab 2 to interact with an Autonomous Transaction Processing (ATP) database to create a new order based upon an approved order request. Finally, in Lab 3, you will use OIC Insight capability to create an Insight model that will enable business users to collect and monitor metrics for the above business process and integration flow. Learn Analytics and Machine Learning with Red Bull Racing 8421 909 Analytics jeroen.kloosterman@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Learn Analytics and Machine Learning with Red Bull Racing - Find the BEST race of all time! Learn Analytics and Machine Learning with Red Bull Racing - Find the BEST race of all time!

We're sure you know the feeling—sometimes a race is so exciting that you can't look away for a second, while other times the result is clear from the beginning.

What is the intangible factor that makes a race exciting? Is it the amount of overtaking? The battle for the number 1 position? The weather conditions? Or are we missing some other element that we don’t quite understand yet?

The answer to these questions lies hidden in data: 70 years of racing data, to be precise.

In this two-hour workshop, you’ll have the opportunity to experiment with racing data using a combination of techniques to look for the answer.

You’ll extract critical pieces of information that define the essence of each race, and visualize races and seasons using advanced techniques to determine how great each race is based on established criteria.

Experience firsthand what challenges data scientists. You’ll learn the basics of analytics and machine learning and become familiar with the entire process, from data preparation and visualization to model building, prediction, and evaluation.

So come join us in this fun workshop and help solve the challenge!

No previous analytics or data science experience is required. We’ll provide you with the instructions you’ll need to get your Oracle Cloud Free Tier account for use during the workshop. details: Learn Analytics and Machine Learning with Red Bull Racing - Find the BEST race of all time!

Learn Analytics and Machine Learning with Red Bull Racing - Find the BEST race of all time!

We're sure you know the feeling—sometimes a race is so exciting that you can't look away for a second, while other times the result is clear from the beginning.

What is the intangible factor that makes a race exciting? Is it the amount of overtaking? The battle for the number 1 position? The weather conditions? Or are we missing some other element that we don’t quite understand yet?

The answer to these questions lies hidden in data: 70 years of racing data, to be precise.

In this two-hour workshop, you’ll have the opportunity to experiment with racing data using a combination of techniques to look for the answer.

You’ll extract critical pieces of information that define the essence of each race, and visualize races and seasons using advanced techniques to determine how great each race is based on established criteria.

Experience firsthand what challenges data scientists. You’ll learn the basics of analytics and machine learning and become familiar with the entire process, from data preparation and visualization to model building, prediction, and evaluation.

So come join us in this fun workshop and help solve the challenge!

No previous analytics or data science experience is required. We’ll provide you with the instructions you’ll need to get your Oracle Cloud Free Tier account for use during the workshop.

Learn how to add Generative AI as a Skill in Oracle Digital Assistant 11654 4023 AI Services Workshop Published Private Completed Oracle Digital Assistant (ODA) can be integrated with Large Language Models (LLMs) to enhance its capabilities. OCI Gen AI Service offers LLMs trained on vast amounts of text data, enabling them to perform tasks like text summarization and sentiment analysis. By connecting ODA with OCI Gen AI, you can make it more versatile in handling user input and generate human-like responses. Learn how to integrate generative AI into the Oracle Digital Assistant by connecting it to a large language model, or LLM, hosted in OCI Gen AI Service. An LLM is an AI system that has been trained on vast amounts of text data. These models can be trained on various domains to perform a variety of tasks, including audience-specific text summarization and sentiment analysis of chat histories.

By integrating your ODA skill with an LLM, you enable it to not only field a range of user input, but also to respond with context-appropriate answers in a human-like tone. To help the LLM predict the most likely words or phrases for its responses, you send it the appropriate context and instructions in a block of text known as a prompt. In response, the LLM generates a completion, a sequence of words or phrases that it believes are the most probable continuation of the prompt. details: Oracle Database Sharding enables globally distributed, linearly scalable, multi-model databases.

Oracle Sharding distributes segments of a data set across many databases (shards) on different computers, on-premises or in cloud. It enables globally distributed, linearly scalable, multimodel databases. It requires no specialized hardware or software.

Oracle Sharding does all this while rendering the strong consistency, full power of SQL, support for structured and unstructured data and the Oracle Database ecosystem. It allows you to support applications that require low latency, high availability, and meet data sovereignty requirements.

LiveLabs FastLab: Cross-table Data Grants with Oracle Deep Data Security 12063 4474 Database  - Security richard.c.evans@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed This FastLab extends the Oracle Deep Data Security data grants lab to show how authorization can propagate from one table to another. In a real application, the sensitive data a user can see rarely lives in one table. This FastLab extends the Oracle Deep Data Security data grants lab to show how authorization can propagate from one table to another. In a real application, the sensitive data a user can see rarely lives in one table. An employee record may have related paystubs, contact details, goals, documents, orders, attachments, or line items. You do not want to maintain separate user-specific predicates for every child table.

A cross-table data grant solves that problem. It grants access to records in a child table only when the end user already has the required data privilege on the matching parent record. The grant has no TO clause. Access flows through the parent object's data grants at run time. LiveLabs FastLab: Cross-table Data Grants with Oracle Deep Data Security 12063 4494 Database  - Security richard.c.evans@oracle.com Workshop Publish Requested Completed This FastLab extends the Oracle Deep Data Security data grants lab to show how authorization can propagate from one table to another. In a real application, the sensitive data a user can see rarely lives in one table. This FastLab extends the Oracle Deep Data Security data grants lab to show how authorization can propagate from one table to another. In a real application, the sensitive data a user can see rarely lives in one table. An employee record may have related paystubs, contact details, goals, documents, orders, attachments, or line items. You do not want to maintain separate user-specific predicates for every child table.

A cross-table data grant solves that problem. It grants access to records in a child table only when the end user already has the required data privilege on the matching parent record. The grant has no TO clause. Access flows through the parent object's data grants at run time. records.searchable: LiveLabs FastLab: Getting Started with Oracle Deep Data Security 12060 4393 Database  - Security richard.c.evans@oracle.com Sprint Published Public Completed Oracle Deep Data Security is a database-native access control system in Oracle AI Database 26ai that enforces fine-grained, identity-aware data access policies directly in the database. It ensures users and AI agents can only see and modify the data they’re authorized to—down to the row, column, or cell level—based on their identity and context, without relying on application code. Oracle Deep Data Security is a database-native access control system that enforces fine-grained, identity-aware data access for users and AI agents. It enables least-privilege access down to the row, column, and cell level using declarative SQL policies (data grants), which are evaluated and enforced inside the database at runtime based on the end-user’s identity, roles, and context—ensuring that only authorized data is ever retrieved, regardless of the query or application. records.searchable: LiveLabs FastLab - Protect sensitive data from privileged users 11999 4300 Database  - Security richard.c.evans@oracle.com Sprint Published Public Completed Learn to protect sensitive data from privileged users using Oracle Database Vault realms. This 15-minute hands-on lab demonstrates separation of duties by blocking even DBAs from accessing customer data unless explicitly authorized. This helps you meet regulatory compliance requirements with technical controls, not just trust. Imagine your Chief Compliance Officer walks in with urgent news: if DBA credentials are compromised, attackers get unrestricted access to all customer data. Regulations demand technical controls, not just trust. This 15-minute FastLab shows you how to implement separation of duties quickly and effectively with Oracle Database Vault. You'll experience a real-world compliance scenario on Oracle Autonomous AI Database. You'll start by demonstrating the problem: as a privileged administrator, you can query all sensitive customer data including names, emails, and phone numbers. Then you'll implement the solution using Database Vault realms. You'll create a mandatory realm that establishes a protected zone around sensitive schemas and objects. This technical control blocks all access attempts, even from DBAs and schema owners, unless users are explicitly authorized. You'll see firsthand how realm authorization works alongside standard database privileges to create layered security. By the end, you'll confidently demonstrate to stakeholders how Database Vault enables regulatory compliance while DBAs maintain their administrative capabilities, proving that your security model relies on technical enforcement, not trust alone Individual author Individual 4300 11999 Sprint Published Public Completed Beginner Database  - Security 2026-07-15 2025-12-17 Individual author Individual sprints Mapped From Current Wms 59 38 59 86 4300 11999 Sprint Published Public Completed Beginner Database  - Security 2026-07-15 2025-12-17 Individual author Individual sprints Mapped From Current Wms https://livelabs.oracle.com/ords/dbpm/r/livelabs/view-workshop?wid=4300 https://oracle-livelabs.github.io/sprints/fastlab/content/database-vault/index.html github_pages richard.c.evans@oracle.com DB Product Management Learn to protect sensitive data from privileged users using Oracle Database Vault realms. records.searchable: LiveLabs FastLab - Select AI 11984 4282 Other - I don't see it linda.foinding@oracle.com Sprint Published Private Completed In this LiveLabs FastLab, you learn to ask questions in natural language and get answers directly from your Oracle AI Database with Select AI. You will configure Select AI, run natural language queries that are translated to SQL, and inspect the generated SQL and results. This is a foundation for self-service analytics, chatbot-style data access, summarization, and intelligent applications. In this LiveLabs FastLab, you learn to use Select AI to turn natural language into precise SQL over your Oracle data. You will enable Select AI on a schema, issue questions against product data, review and refine the generated SQL, and compare alternative responses. This is a foundation for conversational BI, developer copilots, and AI-driven decision support. Each action is executed through controlled database tools rather than direct AI access, demonstrating a structured and auditable workflow for AI-driven database development. The Big Star Memory Agent demo shows how support AI evolves from chatbot replies to trusted, governed operations. Across 11 scenes, you see planning, memory, grounded policy decisions, approvals, and architecture in action. All powered by Oracle AI Database 26ai. LiveLabs LiveStacks are real-working demos!
The Big Star Memory Agent Demo is a business-first learning journey that shows how AI agents move from basic chatbot behavior to trusted, enterprise-ready operations. Through 11 scenes and a conclusion, user follow a realistic customer support case and see how planning, memory, grounded responses, governance, and human approval work together to improve service quality and operational control.

The demo starts by comparing a generic chatbot with a context-aware agent, then shows how planning and memory continuity reduce repeated customer effort and speed up resolution. It demonstrates why policy-sensitive decisions must be grounded in trusted data, how different memory types shape decision quality, and how governed memory writes and decision traces protect reliability. User then explore approval dashboards, lightweight access controls, and a complete architecture view that ties all layers together. 

A central takeaway is that successful AI-agent programs need more than model quality. They need a durable operational foundation where customer context, workflow state, controls, and auditability stay aligned. 
The demo uses Oracle AI Database 26ai as that converged foundation, highlighting how organizations can scale AI-agent workflows with stronger consistency, lower operational friction, and clearer accountability.

User can also download the whole demo and deploy it in their own environment. LiveStack LiveLab - Build Retail Intelligence with Oracle AI Database 26ai 12089 4414 Other - I don't see it pat.shepherd@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA In this hands-on workshop, you will inspect the database objects behind the LiveStack application, including relational tables, JSON Duality views, vector search, property graph, spatial data, Oracle Machine Learning, Ask Retail Data, and AI agent audit records. In this hands-on workshop, you will explore the database foundation behind the Seer Sporting Goods Retail LiveStack. 

Using Oracle Database Actions SQL Worksheet, you will inspect the objects and queries that power the retail application experience, including the command center, customer trend signals, creator influence network, fulfillment intelligence, unified order views, predictive analytics, Ask Retail Data, and AI agent workflows.

The workshop shows how Oracle AI Database 26ai can keep retail evidence close to the work. You will use relational SQL, JSON Relational Duality, AI Vector Search, Property Graph, Oracle Spatial, Oracle Machine Learning, semantic metadata, PL/SQL tools, and audit records to trace retail decisions back to governed database evidence. 

By the end, you will see how one connected data foundation can help retailers observe demand, understand signals, route fulfillment, protect order access, score risk, ask trusted questions, and record AI-assisted actions. records.searchable: Make better predictions with spatial algorithms in Oracle Machine Learning for Python (OML4Py) on Autonomous AI Database 11623 3966 ADB Serverless david.lapp@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete A collection of spatial algorithms are now available with Oracle Machine Learning for Python (OML4Py), enabling you to incorporate location into your data science and machine learning-based solutions. In this workshop you work with spatial algorithms to predict electric vehicle adoption based on demographic features, incorporating the effects of location. A collection of spatial algorithms are now available with Oracle Machine Learning for Python (OML4Py), enabling you to incorporate location into your data science and machine learning-based solutions. Spatial algorithms can enhance ML with predictive models that account for geographical variations of predictive factors, detection of spatial patterns such as geographical hotspots and outliers, and more. In this workshop you work with vehicle registration and demographic data to create predictive models for electric vehicle adoption incorporating the effects of location. You will work with several spatial features of OML4Py:  1)  spatial data prep and pre/post processing , 2)  exploratory spatial analysis and SQL operations (i.e. Python API for Oracle Spatial),  3) spatial algorithms for predictions and pattern detection and 4) map rendering of spatial data in OML notebooks.  Through this exercise, you will gain an understanding and appreciation for the role that spatial algorithms play in optimizing the performance of your ML models. Make Search Trusted, Faster, and Deterministic on your Application with Trusted Answer Search 12045 4388 Database allen.hosler@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Learn to build accurate, secure natural-language interfaces with Oracle Trusted Answer Search. This lab covers installing the platform, configuring search targets using AI Vector Search, and embedding the search widget into web applications to deliver deterministic, data-driven outcomes without the risks and "guesswork" of generic chatbots. Enterprises increasingly demand natural-language interfaces, but traditional LLM-based "chatbots" often introduce unacceptable risks regarding accuracy, predictability, and data security. Oracle Trusted Answer Search addresses these challenges by providing a purpose-built "language-to-report" mapping system.
In this workshop, you will go hands-on with the primary components of the platform. You will start by deploying the core APEX-based administration and portal tools on the Oracle AI Database 26ai, leveraging its native AI Vector Search capabilities to match user queries to vetted business reports.
You will then step into the role of a Search Admin to curate the user experience. You will learn how to define Search Targets associated with specific match documents (JSON), ensuring that your application responds with deterministic actions—like opening a precise URL—rather than generated (and potentially hallucinatory) text. The lab also covers advanced configuration, such as parameter extraction, which allows your search interface to identify specific values like "checking account" or "last Monday" to automatically filter the reports presented to the user.
Finally, you will explore the developer experience by integrating the provided Javascript widget into a web application and the admin workflow for continuous improvement. You will learn how to use query history and user feedback (upvotes/downvotes) to refine search accuracy and use built-in regression analysis to safely manage changes to your search domain. By the end of this lab, you will have a fully functional, secure, and highly accurate natural-language search service. The lab also covers advanced configuration, such as parameter extraction, which allows your search interface to identify specific values like "checking account" or "last Monday" to automatically filter the reports presented to the user.
Finally, you will explore the developer experience by integrating the provided Javascript widget into a web application and the admin workflow for continuous improvement. You will learn how to use query history and user feedback (upvotes/downvotes) to refine search accuracy and use built-in regression analysis to safely manage changes to your search domain. records.searchable:
Manage properly credentials in Oracle Cloud Infrastructure with OCI Vault 11514 3882 OCI andrea.romano@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete This workshop shows what are the common pitfalls in handling keys in OCI. In particular it provides an example of a user storing keys in a public bucket and how an unauthorized person could exploit that. Finally it showcases how to properly manage keys in OCI Vault In the fast-evolving landscape of OCI, safeguarding sensitive information is paramount. This workshop is designed to equip participants with a comprehensive understanding of common pitfalls associated with handling credentials in OCI environments. By delving into real-world scenarios and practical examples, attendees gain valuable insights into the potential risks and vulnerabilities that can arise from mishandling credentials.

The workshop kicks off with a cautionary tale, illustrating a scenario where a user inadvertently stores credentials in a public bucket. This all-too-common mistake serves as a powerful reminder of the potential consequences when security measures are not diligently followed. Participants are guided through the anatomy of such a lapse, exploring how an unauthorized person could exploit the exposed credentials to gain unauthorized access and compromise the security of the entire system.

As the workshop progresses, emphasis is placed on the importance of adopting a robust credential management strategy. The focal point of this strategy is the usage of OCI Vault, a versatile and secure solution for managing secrets and protecting sensitive data in dynamic cloud environments. Attendees will be taken through a step-by-step demonstration of how OCI Vault can be seamlessly integrated into cloud workflows to enhance security and mitigate the risk of unauthorized access.


In this workshop, you will:

Lab 1
- Understand the challenges associated with storing credentials in OCI buckets for automation purposes.
- Recognize the potential risks and security implications of mishandling credentials within an OCI setup.
- Experience the consequences of unauthorized access resulting from the misuse of credentials.

Lab 2
- Comprehend the risks associated with publicly accessible buckets in OCI.
- Explore the perspective of an attacker gaining unauthorized access to a public bucket.
- Analyze the potential exploits and risks involved when managing credentials in publicly accessible storage.

Lab 3
- Learn the importance of secure credential management in OCI.
- Utilize OCI Vault to securely store and manage credentials.
- Understand the proper workflow of accessing credentials from OCI Vault and applying them to interact with REST APIs. Market Basket Analysis is the data mining technique of finding correlations between different entities. It is how retailers recommend products based on purchase history, or how video streaming companies recommend videos based on search history.

records.searchable:
Maximize AIOps Efficiency with OCI Gen AI Agents 11889 4209 AI Services nikhil.nv.verma@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete AIOps represents a transformative  approach that utilizes Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning technologies to enhance and automate various IT operations processes. This workshop demonstrates how to utilize Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI Agents to automate IT operations. A common and impactful use case has been selected for this demonstration—remediation of high CPU and memory utilization alarms. In this scenario, the OCI Generative AI Agent leverages a runbook retrieved via a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) tool to determine the appropriate remediation steps and trigger the necessary tools to resolve the issue.

While this workshop highlights a specific use case, the approach is extensible. Organizations can integrate OCI Generative AI Agents with existing IT Service Management (ITSM) systems to identify various IT operational issues and automatically execute relevant runbooks for resolution.

Key Components and Services Used:

OCI Autonomous Database (23ai) is utilized as the RAG database to store and retrieve operational runbooks.

OCI Email Delivery service is configured to send real-time notification emails to the IT operations team once remediation tasks are successfully completed.

OCI Monitoring is used to define and configure alarms for CPU and memory utilization, triggering alerts when usage exceeds 90%.

A test compute instance was provisioned to simulate CPU and memory stress using synthetic load generation tools (e.g., stress-ng), thereby creating realistic alarm scenarios.

OCI Agent Development Kit (ADK) was employed to develop and deploy the Generative AI agents.

Slack was integrated as the front-end interface, allowing IT users to query system health (e.g., CPU or memory alarms) and authorize the AI agent to perform remediation actions according to the runbook instructions.

This end-to-end setup showcases the potential of OCI Generative AI in streamlining IT operations, reducing mean time to resolution (MTTR), and enhancing operational efficiency through intelligent automation. Maximizing Data Transfer Performance with OCI 11426 OCI tim.clegg@oracle.com Workshop Delete Requested This covers considerations and best-practices around maximizing the performance of large data transfers to/from OCI. This is a detailed look at the tools, techniques and many environmental factors involved in successfully transferring large amounts of data into or out of OCI in a performant manner.

Anyone can move lots of data to OCI, but doing so in the most efficient and performant manner can be a challenge.  There are lots of areas to consider and tune.  Numerous utilities and other tools exist which can aid the effort both in diagnosing, configuring and performing the transfer of large amounts of data to OCI.  This will go through many of these considerations, helping you better understand how you can maximize the performance of data to OCI. records.searchable:
Memory and Context Engineering for AI Agents with Oracle AI Database 12039 Developers - Database eli.schilling@oracle.com Workshop In Development In this workshop, you'll learn how to engineer memory systems that give AI agents the ability to remember, learn, and adapt across conversations. Moving beyond simple RAG, we implement a complete Memory Manager with six distinct memory types—each serving a specific cognitive function. Without engineered context, AI systems can suffer from context poisoning (repeatedly referencing a hallucination) or context distraction (irrelevant data confusing the model's logic). Proper engineering transforms a reactive chatbot into a proactive, reliable collaborator that understands project-wide dependencies.

Memory context engineering is the structured discipline of designing systems that dynamically manage what an AI model "sees" and "remembers" to ensure reliable, personalized, and efficient performance. It represents a shift from prompt engineering (crafting a single message) to system design (managing the entire lifecycle of data entering and exiting the context window).

Modern context engineering often categorizes AI memory into layers inspired by human cognitive architecture:

Short-Term Memory (Session Memory): Maintains the current conversation thread. It acts as a "scratchpad" for the AI to track its reasoning and intermediate steps during a single task.
Long-Term Memory: Persists across different sessions. This stores durable facts (e.g., "the user prefers Python") and episodic events (e.g., "the last deployment failed due to a specific flag").
Semantic vs. Episodic:
Semantic Memory: Durable, general facts and procedures.
Episodic Memory: Recalling specific past interactions or events to maintain continuity. Microservices and Kubernetes for an Oracle DBA 11372 3734 Database john.lathouwers@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Oracle DBAs often have limited exposure to Microservices and Kubernetes.  In a step by step guide, learn how to deploy a Microservice application in Oracle Kubernetes Engine, connect it to an Autonomous Database, and manage the life cycle of an Oracle Database using the Oracle Operator for Kubernetes - in the new environment for modern applications. Oracle DBAs often have limited exposure to Microservices and Kubernetes.  Learn from an ex Oracle DBA who built a Microservices, Multicloud Platform with the Oracle Database.  In a step by step guide, learn how to deploy a Microservice application in Oracle Kubernetes Engine, connect it to an Autonomous Database, and manage the life cycle of an Oracle Database using the Oracle Operator for Kubernetes - in the new environment for modern applications.

A production-ready platform is deployed from the OCI Marketplace and its provisioning is shown with Terraform and Ansible, with both application insights and database operational details.  This is designed by an Oracle DBA for the Oracle DBA. Migrate Data from NoSQL Cloud Service to OCI Object Storage 11934 4265 NoSQL ramya.umesh@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Use Oracle NoSQL Database Migrator utility to copy data from Oracle NoSQL Database Cloud Service table to a JSON file in the OCI Object Storage bucket. Oracle NoSQL Database delivers extreme availability and highly predictable, single-digit millisecond response times for simple queries at scale. Oracle NoSQL Database Cloud Service is a fully managed offering designed to handle large volumes of high-velocity data.

The service supports the Oracle NoSQL Database Migrator utility, which enables seamless migration of Oracle NoSQL tables between different data sources.

In this workshop, you will learn how to use the Oracle NoSQL Database Migrator utility to copy data from an Oracle NoSQL Database Cloud Service table to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Object Storage. You will upload sample data to an Oracle NoSQL Cloud Service table, prepare a configuration template for the Migrator utility, and run the utility from the Cloud Shell to perform the data migration. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) provides customers with high-performance computing and low-cost cloud storage options. Through on-demand local, object, file, and block storage, Oracle Cloud addresses key storage workload requirements and use cases.

Oracle supports online data transfer with Rclone and OCI Command Line Object Storage Sync, customers can also use other migration tools that support Amazon S3 Compatibility API. records.searchable: Mitigate SQL Injection risks with Oracle Database Security Central 12161 Database  - Security angeline.dhanarani@oracle.com Workshop Approved Learn how Oracle Database Security Central lets you mitigate SQL Injection risks by using Oracle SQL Firewall. Oracle SQL Firewall is a built-in database security feature introduced in Oracle AI Database 26ai that provides real-time protection against SQL injection attacks and compromised accounts by intercepting commands directly inside the database kernel. Because it runs inside the database engine, it cannot be bypassed by encrypted traffic or compromised application layers. Database Security Central lets you manage SQL Firewall policies for the database target. One can also monitor SQL Firewall violations from the console. Modern Application Development with Oracle Kubernetes Environment and Verrazzano 7661 3323 Weblogic adrian.padilla@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Delete Requested This lab offers an intro-level, hands-on session with Helidon and Verrazzano. You can learn how to make and assemble services and deploy them on an enterprise container platform. This lab offers attendees an intro-level, hands-on session with Helidon and Verrazzano. You will learn how to make and assemble services and deploy them on an enterprise container platform.

This is a BYOL (Bring Your Own Laptop) session, so bring your Windows, OSX, or Linux laptop. You will need JDK 11+, Apache Maven (3.6), and Docker installed before you begin.

During this lab you will install Helidon CLI tools and develop the HTTP microservice application. For Verrazzano you will set up Oracle Kubernetes Engine (OKE) on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure using Oracle Cloud Free Tier account. The Free Tier account is sufficient to explore and learn how to run and operate microservice applications on an enterprise level.

The goal of this workshop is that you learn the basics of using Helidon and Verrazzano and understand how they can help you in your projects. If you want to learn more about the capabilities of these projects, then continue to explore using your Oracle Free Tier cloud account and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. Modern Data Warehouse Workshop 11325 3570 ADB Serverless javier.x.de.la.torre@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete In this workshop we are going to use different capabilities to integrate structured and non-structured data and provide new business value. In this workshop we are going to use different capabilities to integrate structured and non-structured data and provide new business value. We are going to be a company who is shipping different products to our customers. As many of them buy in as a “guest mode”, it is difficult to find patterns or improve the business. Therefore, we are going to collect Twitter data to discover them. As a result of the workshop, we will learn which customers are at risk of “churn” or they are not happy with our service and identify patterns inside of our data.

During this workshop, we are going to use these capabilities: JSON, Oracle Text, Graph, Blockchain, Spatial, AutoML and APEX. Modernization of Oracle Forms to Oracle APEX 11716 4026 APEX ankita.beri@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Welcome to our Oracle Forms to Oracle APEX Transition Workshop! This hands-on workshop will equip you with the knowledge and skills to modernize your legacy Oracle Forms applications using Oracle APEX. Whether new to APEX or looking to refine your skills, this workshop will provide valuable insights and practical experience. Welcome to our Oracle Forms to Oracle APEX Transition Workshop! This hands-on workshop will equip you with the knowledge and skills to modernize your legacy Oracle Forms applications using Oracle APEX. Whether new to APEX or looking to refine your skills, this workshop will provide valuable insights and practical experience. Throughout the workshop, you will learn to understand the fundamental differences and similarities between Oracle Forms and APEX and how to map components from one to the other.

You will also analyze and extract crucial business logic from your existing Oracle Forms applications, set up the necessary database infrastructure to support your APEX applications and use the Create Application Wizard to develop a web-based application. Additionally, you will learn best practices and advanced techniques to enhance your APEX applications' functionality and user experience.

By the end of this workshop, you will be well-prepared to transform your Oracle Forms applications into powerful, user-friendly APEX applications, leveraging modern web technologies to enhance performance and usability. Join us as we explore the exciting possibilities of APEX and take your applications to the next level! Modernize Oracle Database 19c Workloads with AI Agents Using AI DB Private Agent Factory 12044 Database jadd.jennings@oracle.com Workshop Approved In this hands-on learning workshop, you’ll provision an Oracle 19c database on DBCS to mimic an on prem setup, then install ORDS and APEX. You’ll deploy AI DB Private Agent Factory, connect it to 19c, and learn how to create data analysis agents on sample APEX data. Finally, you’ll build a guided custom flow that orchestrates multiple agents. In this hands-on learning workshop, you will learn how to build and orchestrate AI agents for legacy database environments using Oracle Database 19c and AI DB Private Agent Factory. Many enterprise workloads still run on established database versions, and this session is designed to help you apply modern agent-based patterns while keeping data access controlled and aligned with typical enterprise security expectations.

You will start by provisioning an Oracle Database 19c instance using Oracle Database Cloud Service (DBCS) to simulate an on-premises deployment. Once the database is available, you’ll install and configure Oracle REST Data Services (ORDS) and Oracle APEX to enable API access and load sample APEX data.

Next, you’ll provision AI DB Private Agent Factory and walk through the key configuration steps required to connect it to your Oracle 19c environment. With the connection in place, you’ll create data analysis agents that can work with the sample APEX data, focusing on how agents retrieve context, interpret requests, and produce reliable outputs.

Finally, you’ll design and build a custom flow that orchestrates multiple agents into an end-to-end experience—such as analyzing data, generating summaries, and guiding follow-on actions—so you leave with a repeatable blueprint you can adapt to your own legacy database use cases. By the end of the workshop, you’ll have a working reference implementation and a clear understanding of the steps, components, and best practices needed to operationalize AI agents with legacy database technologies like Oracle 19c. You’ll perform data discovery, migrate your collections, and repoint your unmodified MongoDB app to Oracle’s MongoDB API—demonstrating zero code changes and perfect data integrity. In this lab, you’ll experience a seamless “lift and shift” migration from an existing MongoDB database to Oracle Autonomous JSON Database (AJD) by using the MongoVibeAssist_Migrator CLI. Guided by Oracle Code Assist and interactive vibe coding, you will discover your source data, execute a full migration, and verify data integrity. Finally, you’ll repoint your original MongoDB application to Oracle’s MongoDB-compatible API, showing that your app runs unmodified on Oracle’s cloud platform. This hands-on lab highlights the simplicity, speed, and power of migrating to Oracle AI Database—no code rewrites required. Service metrics provide administrators the ability to monitor the health and performance of many OCI services and resources. Monitor Traces for WebLogic Server Deployed on Kubernetes using Oracle Application Performance Monitoring 9104 932 OCI O&M yutaka.takatsu@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Enable monitoring (tracing and metrics) for a WebLogic app on Kubernetes using Oracle Application Performance Monitoring (APM) In this workshop learn how to configure a WebLogic-on-Kubernetes for monitoring with the Oracle Application Performance Monitoring (APM) service. This enables automatic OpenTracing instrumentation, and metrics collection that are used to provide full, end-to-end monitoring and diagnostics for the application. One way to deploy an APM Java agent in a Docker container-enabled Kubernetes cluster, is to first, provision the APM Java agent in the location where docker image was originally created, second, build a new Docker image with the APM Java agent, and third, push the image to the registry. You can then configure Kubernetes to use the new Docker image to enable the APM agent in the pods.

However, this method assumes you have administrator access to the Docker working directory to recreate the image, which may not always be the case. In this workshop, we will use an alternative approach, to provision the APM Java agent in a file system mounted in the Oracle Cloud, and deploy it to the Kubernetes cluster, without updating the Docker image. Monitoring and Troubleshooting Issues in Large Enterprises Using Advanced Machine Learning 5721 3345 OCI O&M anand.p.prabhu@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Learn to monitor and troubleshoot Issues using advanced Machine Learning using an Oracle Integration Cloud example. In this workshop learn how to monitor applications, technology stack and infrastructure, including compute, and network logs in a hybrid cloud environment using logs. See how to create KPIs and executive grade visualizations and dashboards. Monolith to Microservice - 3D app modernization adventure 11378 3802 OCI wojciech.pluta@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Get your game on! 

In this workshop, you will learn how to deploy a multiplayer Three.js game to the cloud, then iterate through the modernization process to enhance the application and ultimately deploy it to Kubernetes. This workshop leverages a broad array of OCI services to illustrate how simple it can be to deploy, migrate, and modernize applications in the cloud. We start with a VM deployment via Terraform, then containerize the application and move to OCI Container Instances. In the final phase, the application design is enhanced to provide scalability while being deployed to Oracle Container Engine for Kubernetes (OKE) with Database to keep the score. 

The best part is, you get to play a really cool 3D "Save the Wildlife" game when you finish the deployment. records.searchable: Move a WebLogic Applications to OKE with the WebLogic Kubernetes ToolKit UI 11004 3237 Weblogic sid.joshi@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete This workshop shows an end to end workshop of the migration of an on-premise WebLogic Server Domain into the containers and makes it runable in OCI with Oracle Container Engine for Kubernetes (OKE). Oracle facilitates the modernization of the WebLogic Server environment through the adoption of container architecture and seamless integration with Kubernetes. With the WebLogic Kubernetes Toolkit, we offer a comprehensive set of open-source tools engineered to streamline the migration process from traditional VM-based infrastructure to containerized environments. In this lab, you will learn how to orchestrate an end-to-end migration. Discover how to introspect a WebLogic domain, create metadata model of the WebLogic Domain and create images that are used by the WebLogic Kubernetes Operator to instantiate pods with running WebLogic instances. You will practice some crucial lifecycle operations including scaling, patching and upgrading. And, microservices is the most popular architecture to create cloud-native applications. The MicroProfile specifications enable existing Java EE developers to leverage their existing skills and quickly transition them into developers of microservices. 
MicroProfile APIs provide the foun Adopting the microservices architecture is the prevalent trend in the Application Development industry today. And, microservices is the most popular architecture to create cloud-native applications. The MicroProfile specifications enable existing Java EE developers to leverage their existing skills and quickly transition them into developers of microservices. 
MicroProfile APIs provide the foundation for developing microservices applications by adopting the subset of Java EE and Jakarta EE standards and extending them to address typical microservices patterns. Oracle delivers an open-source project that delivers an easy to adopt framework for microservices in Java called Helidon. Helidon is available in two editions – Helidon SE and Helidon MP. While Helidon SE is a simple, reactive, and lightweight framework, Helidon MP offers the developer community the ease of implementing MicroProfile specifications. Helidon offers an easy path for Java EE developers to enter the microservices development community.  
Please join our hands-on-lab to experience an introduction to Helidon MP. You will gain first-hand knowledge on how to get started with your first Helidon MP application development project. NAMD - Scalable Molecular Dynamics 3041 705 HPC breanna.mendonca@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Deploy a GPU machine on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, install NAMD, and run a model using NAMD software. This workshop provides the steps to deploy a GPU machine on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, install NAMD, and run a model using NAMD software.
NAMD is a molecular dynamics software that simulates the movements of atoms in biomolecules under a predefined set of conditions. It is used to identify the behavior of these biomolecules when exposed to changes in temperature, pressure and other inputs that mimic the actual conditions encountered in a living organism. NAMD can be used to establish patterns in protein folding, protein-ligand binding, and cell membrane transport, making it a very useful application for drug research and discovery.

NAMD is built on Charm++ and Converse, and can run on high performance computers to execute parallel processing. It was developed by the University of Illinois. Leverage the power of NVIDIA GPUs and advanced deep learning frameworks, such as Triton and TensorRT, to gain hands-on experience deploying scalable Llama 3.2 models for large language model inference. OCI Cloud Native Fast Track 11113 3827 OCI LAD SE Workshop Delete Requested Public Completed Workshop focado no público desenvolvedor, com apresentação de conceitos e laboratórios  para os serviços OCI Cloud Native e DevOps. Os participantes poderão implantar seus próprios recursos no Oracle Cloud e aprender durante todo o processo. Full Day Workshop, focused on the developer audience, with presentation of concepts and hands on labs for the OCI Cloud Native & DevOps services. Participants will be able to deploy their own resources in the Oracle Cloud and to learn during all the process.

The workshop aims to allow the participants to learn about the "Dev" services in OCI, but also, to also to prepare them for the prepare them for the Oracle certifications:
. OCI Developer Associate 2021
. OCI DevOps Professional 2022

The sections of the workshop are as follows:

1. Resource Provisioning
2. Developing Cloud Native Applications - Part 1
3. Developing Cloud Native Applications - Part 2
4. Automating Deployment
5. Operating Cloud Native Applications

The main OCI services presented are:
. Resource Manager
. API Gateway
. OCI Registry
. OKE
. Functions
. Streaming
. Events
. Vault
. WAF

OCI Database Management Database Fleet Performance Diagnostics and Management 4761 OCI O&M sriram.vrinda@oracle.com Workshop In Development Database Fleet Performance Diagnostics and Management As a Database Administrator, you can use the Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Database Management service to monitor and manage your Oracle Databases.

Database Management currently supports External Oracle Databases, which are Oracle Databases located on-premises and connected to a resource in the Oracle Cloud Infrastructure External Database service.

Database Management supports Oracle Database versions 11.2.0.4 and later and using Database Management you can:

Monitor the key performance and configuration metrics of your fleet of Oracle Databases. You can also compare and analyze database metrics over a selected period of time.
Group your critical Oracle Databases, which reside across compartments into a Database Group, and monitor them.
Create SQL jobs to perform administrative operations on a single Oracle Database or a Database Group. There are many ways to test the service but for this lab, we will be using an OCI free tier eligible ARM compute VM where we will then install and configure Postfix and MailX. records.searchable: OCI Gen AI: Leveraging Gen AI models to label and standardize text data - examples from industry 11646 4018 AI Services david.e.miller@oracle.com Workshop Published Event Completed Join us to discover how the power of Generative AI can be leveraged to automatically map text data to standardized terminology or lexicon terms, enabling organizations to improve data interoperability, streamline analysis, and unlock valuable insights. This hands-on lab focuses on leveraging Generative AI models to standardize and label text data, with a particular emphasis on healthcare terminology. The lab explores the challenges of inconsistent terminology across various industries, highlighting how it hinders data aggregation, analysis, and system interoperability. Participants will learn about a specific challenge in healthcare, where variability in radiology protocol names can impact data interoperability, research, and patient care. The lab demonstrates how Generative AI can be applied to map non-standard terms to standardized lexicons like LOINC or RADLEX, offering a more efficient and scalable solution compared to manual mapping or rule-based systems. This workshop will walk you through the process of migrating an existing eCommerce application from an on-prem environment to being natively deployed within the cloud. It will walk you through how to capture a custom image of this app and deploy it on OCI with the necessary infrastructure like Networking, Security Lists, and route rules. The workshop will also walk you through the process of making the application highly-available. Later you will learn how to handle the case of high availability by leveraging Oracle's Load Balancer and DNS services for traffic steering. The workshop also focuses on how to connect your eCommerce application to MDS (MySQL Database Service) on OCI. Finally, the workshop will leverage PaaS services such as Autonomous Data Warehouse (ADW), Oracle Analytics Cloud (OAC), and Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC) to show how you can gain even more insight into your application data. OCI Network Load Balancer 11860 OCI gabriel.fontenot@oracle.com Workshop Approved Cloud applications often require load sharing across application members to support resiliency and desired scale. OCI users can consume the Network Load Balancer to design flexible and fault tolerant application. Learn how to deploy Network Load Balancers within your OCI network. With the rapid growth of cloud-based applications, have you considered how to leverage OCI to build a more resilient and scalable application that meets the growing need of your business.  OCI has the technology and tools to support building a best-in-class network load balanced application.

In this session we will demonstrate how to effectively deploy a network load balanced application that will consume OCI cloud network and compute resources. We will begin by creating a foundation with the virtual cloud network (VCN), associated subnets and security lists, internet gateway and the corresponding compute resources that represent your application. The focus of the session will include all the networking, compute and load balancer configurations needed to simulate a network load balanced application. At the end of the session, you will walk away with a complete understanding of the OCI components required to create the foundation of a network load balanced application. OCI Open LZ - Configure your Tailored Landing Zone 11489 OCI paola.juarez@oracle.com Workshop Approved The OCI Open LZ simplifies the onboarding of organizations, business units, and subsidiaries into OCI. It is a reference blueprint and a repeatable design process of an end-to-end solution.  With this LiveLab you will setup the OCI Open LZ through simple IaC configurations, with human-readable JSON/HCLs, giving you the ability to master the approach to create and tailor your own landing zones. Welcome to the OCI Open LZ  LiveLab, a guided process to create and run the OCI Open LZ blueprint in your own tenancy, and scale your abilities to setup and run any OCI resource topology. The main benefits are:

Focus on Value: Focus on configuring the design and resources, instead of coding them. This means shorter time-to-value, lower effort, and lower risk.  
Best Practices: Use existing top-quality terraform modules that are open and full of best practices. It's possible to leverage this to evolve OCI terraform skills and apply future IaC best practices. This also means lower risk and lower efforts.
Scale Day Two: Being able to split operational configurations from code is a game change in cloud operations, and will simplify drastically the day-two operations, opening the path for a GitOps operating model and potentially simpler automation. The cloud operators will only work with configurations, not code.


With this LiveLabs you will be able to setup and run the OCI Open LZ or any tailored landing zone normally used in these use cases (but not limited to):

Mirroring existing landing zones on other CSPs.
Onboarding and reflecting organization structures such as business units, operating entities, OpCos, into a cloud operating model.
Fine-grained segregation of duties and responsibilities across resources and teams.
Network structure with different areas and security postures, with fine-tuned north-south and east-west traffic scenarios.
Heterogeneous and/or large workloads landscape.
Adopting a highly scalable operating model, such as control versioned operations.


The OCI Open LZ use the configurable Terraform CIS Landing Zone Enhanced Modules (IAM, Networking, Security, and Observability & Monitoring), a collection of repositories created to help customers align and configure their OCI implementations with the CIS OCI Foundations Benchmark recommendations. These modules work under the same approach:

Allow the definition of arbitrary resource topologies in a JSON/HCL format.
Enforce CIS Benchmark recommendations when appropriate.
Require minimal Terraform knowledge to be utilised.

With the OCI Open LZ configurable approach used on this LiveLabs you be able to avoid the common pitfalls, such as:

Hard-coding. Changing or adapting code to create a new landing zone different than an existing solution is complex and time-consuming. This also means that any change to the landing zone will be executed by code and not configurations.
Waste & Late Time-to-Value. The time spent on adapting code, or re-coding over and over for the OCI landing/core resources is time wasted and not used on the business value/workloads.
Limited Scaling. Doing OCI changes manually can work for some tactical solutions, but it will always limit the scaling and add complexity and cost to the day-two operations. Note that, for example, CIS LZ creates 100+ OCI resources.
Scarce Skills. IaC Terraform coding skills are not as common as we should expect, which makes these efforts a higher risk and challenge to solve. OCI Queue : Decouple application components, message filtering and fairness using OCI Queue 11828 4104 OCI abhishek.bhaumik@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Queue is a fully managed, high-throughput messaging service designed to enable secure communication between decoupled application components or microservices. By leveraging OCI Queue, developers can implement scalable, resilient, and loosely coupled architectures to support asynchronous messaging and ensure system flexibility. In this workshop, you will learn to create and manage OCI Queues and integrate them with various SDKs and APIs to develop decoupled applications. Whether you're using the OCI SDKs or open-source protocols like STOMP, this hands-on experience will help you understand key features like message fairness, channel management, and more.
In this workshop, you will learn:
Create an OCI Queue
Learn how to provision and configure an OCI Queue to enable asynchronous communication for your applications.
Decouple application components using the OCI Queue SDK
Implement decoupling patterns between microservices using the OCI Queue SDK.
Produce and consume messages with fairness using OCI Queue SDK
Explore how to send and receive messages from specific queue channels while ensuring messaging fairness and proper load distribution.
Use open-source STOMP API to decouple application components
Understand how to integrate OCI Queue with the widely adopted open-source STOMP protocol.
Produce and consume messages with fairness using STOMP APIs
Combine the capabilities of OCI Queue and STOMP APIs to develop messaging systems with channel-specific fairness. OCI Resource Analytics Product Demo - Oracle AI Cloud World 11942 Analytics sowjanya.yaddanapudi@oracle.com Workshop Approved Resource Analytics centralizes resource inventory across multiple tenancies and regions, offering easy access to configurations and relationships through a SQL endpoint in an Autonomous Datawarehouse . Resource Analytics synchronizes customers resource metadata into a relational data model, allowing them to query inventory in near-real time. Product Definition
Resource Analytics centralizes resource inventory across multiple tenancies and regions, offering easy access to configurations and relationships through a SQL endpoint in an Autonomous Datawarehouse . Resource Analytics synchronizes customers resource metadata into a relational data model, allowing them to query inventory in near-real time. With standardized views and seamless integration with tools like Oracle SQL Developer, accessing and analyzing inventory data has never been easier.
 
Product Features
 
Advanced troubleshooting using Graph Studio
To simplify troubleshooting, Resource Analytics uses Graph Studio, an integrated Autonomous Data Warehouse feature, to visually represent resource relationships. This intuitive graphical interface helps you quickly understand connections between resources, enabling faster issue resolution. With a right-click, you can access detailed properties or navigate directly to the resource for immediate action, making resource management and addressing issues more efficient and accessible.
 
Built-in inventory insights via OAC (Oracle Analytics Cloud)
Customers can configure Resource Analytics to provision an Oracle Analytics Cloud (OAC) instance, providing built-in dashboards and reports that offer a comprehensive view of your resource inventory. These preconfigured analytics allow you to easily analyze data by region, tenancy, and compartment. You can extend these dashboards or create custom ones to meet your specific needs and even bring in custom datasets for enriched insights. OCI Tagging: Streamline searching, filtering, and managing resources at scale 12032 4417 OCI eli.schilling@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Learn [almost] everything there is to know about resource tagging in Oracle Cloud. From freeform to pre-defined and cost tracking tags, to automated search and filter of resources across your account, to implementing programmatic solutions to enforce tag-based governance. Tagging plays a crucial role in organizing and managing cloud resources. A tag is essentially a key value pair that can be added to cloud resources to enhance visibility and control. In Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), tagging is built into the Identity and Access Management (IAM) service, enabling users to systematically categorize and manage resources. The use of tagging further allows for activities such as cost tracking, resource discovery and management, filtering, and logical organization.
In this workshop, you will learn about a wide array of tagging capabilities and use cases. You will leverage command line tools for making bulk changes, provision resources with cost tracking tags, explore advanced search functionality, and deploy serverless apps (e.g. OCI Functions) to programmatically enforce tag policies. OCI Vision: Introduction to Stored Video Service 11554 OCI aparna.chaturvedi@oracle.com Workshop Approved Explore Stored Video Service within the OCI Vision Service to perform tasks like label detection, object detection, text detection and face detection on a stored video Enterprise video data has significant value related to core business activities and their customers. To gain business and customer insights effectively and at scale from this data, vision capabilities are needed. For example, identifying key requirements to understand customer perception of their products to address gaps. Some core capabilities include labeling videos, detecting objects, text & faces from the video. These capabilities are typically machine learning algorithms custom built, tuned by Data Scientists and productized for use in applications. Doing this is a time consuming and expensive proposition.

Stored Video Service reduces time and effort to perform Vision tasks like label detection, object detection, text detection and face detection by providing key vision capabilities via production-ready REST APIs. The service enables applications to automate sophisticated stored video analysis at scale without needing ML expertise. The service functionality is implemented with pre-trained ML models which are often useful. They may also be further customized to understand the patterns of the customer’s context by providing additional data. One-Click Deploy Stable Diffusion 11835 4129 OCI zhizhen.yan@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA How to deploy an open-source generative AI model in OCI with minimum setup using Terraform, GitHub Actions and OCI Compute/GPU. Many companies want to be able to harness the power of AI models (large language models or diffusion models), but don’t know where to start. OCI offers a wide variety of deployment options such as our Generative AI service. OCI GenAI service is a fully managed Oracle Cloud Infrastructure service that provides a set of state-of-the-art, customizable large language models that cover a wide range of use-cases, including chat, text generation, summarization, and creating text embeddings. However, what if you only want to pay for the underlying infrastructure and use one of the tens of thousands of open-source generative AI models that are available?  

Using OCI high performance GPU compute and common CI/CD tools, you can deploy open-source generative AI models to the cloud and integrate with existing services with ease.

In this workshop, you will learn how to quickly deploy an open-source diffusion model leveraging different tools such as Terraform, GitHub Actions, and OCI infrastructure. This unique combination of tools will allow you to one-click deploy an open-source generative AI model on OCI to use in your own use-cases.
