Optimize Oracle Kubernetes Engine (OKE) costs with OpenCost 11794 4084 OCI NA Cloud SE Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Complete Discover how to use OpenCost for detailed insights into your Kubernetes cluster's cost structure. OpenCost offers visibility into resource usage and spending across Kubernetes resources such as namespaces, nodes, deployments, and others. This enables accurate analysis and optimized resource allocation. Dive in to better manage and control your Kubernetes costs! Unlock the full potential of OpenCost to gain detailed insights into your Kubernetes cluster's cost structure and enhance cost management. OpenCost is a powerful tool designed to provide comprehensive visibility into resource usage and spending within your Kubernetes environment. By tracking key resources such as namespaces, nodes, deployments, and more, OpenCost enables you to monitor costs at a granular level.

With OpenCost, you can identify cost inefficiencies, uncover spending patterns, and perform in-depth analyses to ensure optimal resource allocation. This tool helps you make data-driven decisions to optimize your Kubernetes workloads, improve cost efficiency, and ensure that your resources are being utilized in the most effective way possible.

Whether you’re looking to manage costs at the cluster level or drill down into individual components, OpenCost empowers you to gain a clear understanding of where your resources are going. By leveraging OpenCost’s powerful reporting capabilities, you can proactively manage your Kubernetes infrastructure and maintain full control over your cloud expenses. Start using OpenCost today to take charge of your Kubernetes costs and make informed decisions that drive better performance and savings. Optimize WebLogic clusters with Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler and the WebLogic Monitoring Exporter 11515 3865 Weblogic kwan.wan@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete In this workshop, we will scale up/down a WebLogic cluster, based on WebLogic metrics provided by the Monitoring Exporter, using the Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA). We will use the Prometheus Adapter to gather the names of the available metrics from Prometheus at regular intervals. This workshop shows an end to end migration of an on-premise WebLogic Server Domain into the containers and makes it runable in OCI with Oracle Container Engine for Kubernetes (OKE). We demonstrate the graphical interface of WebLogic Kubernetes Toolkit UI as well as WebLogic Deployer Tool and Weblogic Kubernetes Operator. We demonstrate how the migration process could be simplified and accelerated by using a DevOps-oriented set of tooling

Later, we will see how to scale a WebLogic cluster, based on WebLogic metrics provided by the Monitoring Exporter, using the Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA). We will use the Prometheus Adapter to gather the names of the available metrics from Prometheus at regular intervals. A custom configuration of the adapter will expose only metrics that follow specific formats. It consists of a basic example of AI Vector Search and the integration with OCI Generative AI service for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) execution. Oracle APEX Developer Professional - Enhance the Applications using Progressive Web Application 11548 3907 APEX roopesh.thokala@oracle.com Workshop Published Private Quarterly QA Complete Oracle APEX allows developers to create Progressive Web Apps (PWAs) that can be easily installed on any desktop or mobile device, offering users a more native app experience. This application is a valuable reference for developers looking to incorporate key PWA features into their applications, helping them create more engaging and user-friendly apps. Oracle APEX allows developers to create Progressive Web Apps (PWAs) that can be easily installed on any desktop or mobile device, offering users a more native app experience. This application is a valuable reference for developers looking to incorporate key PWA features into their applications, helping them create more engaging and user-friendly apps.

This sample dataset collects customers, stores, products, and orders. You will then add new columns to the PRODUCTS table. In this lab, you learn how to install sample tables and views from Sample Datasets in APEX. This sample dataset is a collection of customers, stores, products, and orders used to manage the shopping cart. 

The PRODUCTS table includes columns such as image, price, and details. But there are other characteristics that customers would appreciate knowing about a product, such as colour, type of clothing, and department. In this lab, you will add these columns to the PRODUCTS table. You also learn how to add three new columns to the PRODUCTS table and create lookup tables for those new columns.

Then, you learn to create database objects for your APEX application. This package contains functions and procedures to add products to the cart, remove products, create an order, clear the cart, and more. You also learn to create and use collections.

You will also learn how to create database objects using Quick SQL and then view the objects in Database Actions. You will then use the Data Workshop page in Oracle APEX to load data from a file into your workspace. Oracle Cloud Event Notification 9321 OCI OSPA Workshop Approved Learn about OCI events and notifications. Notifications should be an important part of any customers cloud infrastructure as they can save a lot of time and money. Notifications from applications can send emails or alerts to their users when something happens. For example: a file or order has been processed.

The Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Notifications service broadcasts messages to distributed components through a publish-subscribe pattern, delivering secure, highly reliable, low latency and durable messages for applications hosted on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and externally. Use Notifications to get messages whenever alarms, service connectors, and event rules are triggered. Oracle Data Safe for On-Premises Databases 9801 930 Database  - Security bettina.schaeumer@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Explore options for connecting your on-premises databases to Oracle Data Safe. With Oracle Data Safe, you can protect all your Oracle databases, whether in the cloud or on-premises, with a consistent set of security features; the only difference is how Data Safe connects to your databases in a secure and reliable manner. 

This workshop walks you through the simple, one-time network setup that gives the same visibility and protection across all your Oracle databases. We’ll demonstrate two connectivity options: (1) the Data Safe private endpoint for Oracle databases running in a private virtual cloud network (VCN) within Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) or for your databases connected via FastConnect or VPNConnect configured between your network and OCI; (2) and, the Data Safe on-premises connector for Oracle databases outside of OCI without either of those two network connections. 

Once your database is connected, you can explore all the key capabilities of Data Safe through the 'Get Started with Oracle Data Safe Fundamentals' LiveLab, ideal for DBAs and cloud architects looking to streamline and scale database security. For customers who need end-to-end Observability, Oracle Database, SQL monitoring and tuning, management, and capacity planning capabilities not available in Azure native monitoring, learn how you use Enterprise Manager, OCI Database Management, and Operations Insights in this workshop.

Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Database Management service and Ops Insights provide the best of Oracle’s industry-leading manageability capabilities from Enterprise Manager into Oracle Cloud as a managed cloud services. 
OCI Database Management provides database performance and management capability for all types of Oracle Database deployments, providing DBAs and DevOps a lifecycle solution encompassing monitoring, performance management, tuning, and database administration. OCI Database Management is part of the Oracle Cloud Observability and Management platform.

OCI Ops Insights enables administrators to uncover performance issues, forecast consumption, and plan capacity using machine-learning based analytics on historical and SQL data. Organizations can use these capabilities to make data-driven decisions to optimize resource use, proactively avoid outages, and improve performance.
This workshop details the steps to configure and use OCI Database Management service and Ops Insights to manage Oracle Database@Azure. Oracle Database Consolidation 4481 Database tejus.subrahmanya@oracle.com Workshop In Development Oracle Databases consolidation workshop Database consolidation involves placing multiple databases onto a single set of computing infrastructure, either on-premise or in the Oracle Cloud. Database consolidation is different from server consolidation, which involves consolidating multiple physical servers into a single physical server running Virtual Machines. The primary purpose of database consolidation is to reduce the cost of database infrastructure by taking advantage of more powerful servers that have come onto the market that include dozens of processor cores in a single server.

Databases consolidation may involve any of the following configurations:
Multiple databases on a single physical server
Multiple databases on a single virtual machine
Multiple databases on a cluster of physical servers
Multiple databases on a cluster of virtual machines

Database consolidation allows more databases to run on fewer servers, which reduces infrastructure, but also reduces operational costs. Each physical server represents an Information Technology asset or “Configuration Item” (CI) that must be placed into a data center rack, connected, secured, and maintained. Each Virtual Machine represents another Configuration Item (CI) that also must be deployed, connected (virtually), secured, and maintained.  Database consolidation can significantly reduce the number of CI’s that need to be managed, thereby reducing operational expenses.
 
Database Consolidation also applies in Cloud environments such as the Oracle Database Cloud Service and Oracle Exadata Cloud Service. Oracle databases can also be consolidated into a cluster of physical servers or virtual machines. Oracle Database clustering capabilities include active/passive clustering, as well as active/active clustering using Oracle Real Application Clusters. Clustering is used to increase availability of Oracle databases, enable rolling patching, and to provide for scalability across multiple physical servers or virtual machines.
 
Oracle databases can also be further consolidated into what are known as Container Databases using the Oracle Multitenant option that was first introduced in Oracle Database 12c. The Multitenant option allows multiple databases to be managed under a single Container Database, with a single backup, single disaster recovery configuration, and single clustering configuration. Oracle Database custom audit events 11762 4128 Database valentin.tabacaru@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Collect custom audit information from an Oracle Database 23ai instance and use it to build customized charts and reports using Oracle Application Express (APEX). For this example, you will use an Oracle Autonomous Database (ADB) running in Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). One of the projects that is ongoing inside Oracle is improving the database error messages. Sometimes it is the small things that really improve life for developers, like more informative error messages. Oracle Database 23ai has improved error messages that provide useful problem diagnosis in context and suggest actionable solutions.
Oracle Database 23ai introduces a new unified audit capability with selectivity at the column level that lets you create more narrowly targeted audit policies that reduce "noise" from unnecessary audit records.
If you want to transition to unified auditing after you have upgraded to Oracle Database 23ai, note that most of the traditional auditing features will continue to exist in Oracle Database 23ai to help you transition smoothly.
Unified auditing was introduced in Oracle Database 12c with significant enhancements to auditing functionality. Unified auditing enables you to capture audit records from many sources, and write the audit records into a single consolidated unified audit trail.
In this workshop, you will learn how to collect custom audit information from an Oracle Database 23ai instance and use it to build customized charts and reports using Oracle Application Express (APEX). For this example, you will use an Oracle Autonomous Database (ADB) running in Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). Companies are now able to query their unstructured data, simply by leveraging Oracle Database 23ai and OCI Generative AI Services.

In this LiveLab we will build a fully modular RAG pipeline using Oracle AI Vector Search, Oracle Generative AI Services. For LLM orchestration, we will use Llama Index Python package. Generative AI represents the next frontier in enterprise innovation, enabling organizations to unlock insights and value from their unstructured data like never before. The pipeline integrates cutting-edge Oracle AI Vector Search technology, enabling precise retrieval of relevant documents or data points from unstructured datasets. Oracle Generative AI Services then enhance these retrievals by generating detailed and contextually accurate responses, unlocking actionable insights in real time.

To orchestrate and streamline interactions with Large Language Models (LLMs), we will leverage the LlamaIndex Python package. This powerful framework simplifies LLM integration, allowing for seamless querying and data processing. LlamaIndex serves as the backbone for managing and optimizing data flow between Oracle’s AI tools and the LLMs, ensuring a robust, scalable, and efficient RAG pipeline.

Learn directly from Oracle Database Product Management how to identify threats and remediate them by leveraging Oracle Database Security features. Users like Marvin and Emma authenticate via Entra ID and see different results from the same query. This lab walks you through configuring Microsoft Entra ID authentication for Oracle AI Database 26ai and then layering Oracle Deep Data Security — end users, data roles, and data grants — so the database enforces per-user access based on Entra ID app role assignments. By the end, Marvin (a manager) and Emma (an employee) will authenticate with Entra ID and see completely different data from the same SQL query, enforced by the database kernel. records.searchable: Oracle Fleet Patching and Provisioning (FPP) - Quick Start 1840 599 Database - MAA philippe.fierens@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Explore basic operations for a novice user of Oracle Fleet Patching and Provisioning (FPP). Oracle GoldenGate Microservices for Big Data 11103 3318 GoldenGate madhu.kumar.s@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Create Realtime Changed Data to Big Data Targets using Oracle GoldenGate (MA) for Big Data This hands-on lab is designed to demonstrate how  Oracle GoldenGate Microservices Architecture and  Oracle GoldenGate (MA) for Big Data can be used to set up a replication environment by a mix of web pages, shell scripts, and Rest API interfaces. All labs will use shell scripts to facilitate the building of the environment while providing insight into how to use the web pages and AdminClient. The labs will walk the end-user through how to add all components of Oracle GoldenGate replication. This hands-on lab focuses on GoldenGate Real-Time Data Replication demonstrating five scenarios that you can use (both on-premise and in the cloud) to capture real-time data changes from your sources.

records.searchable: Oracle Integration 3 - Automate ERP Cloud and B2B Integration with Trading Partners 11475 3803 OIC - Integration kishore.x.katta@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete This workshop showcases Oracle Integration by automating tasks. When a Purchase Order (PO) is made in ERP Cloud, OIC captures and synchronizes data with Custom VBCS application. The PO is also translated into an EDI 850 document for the Trading Partner and an approval process is initiated, linking Letter of Credit (LOC) details. Oracle Digital Assistant interacts to fetch Order Status and Details This workshop introduces Oracle Integration (OIC) capabilities through a step-by-step scenario. When a user creates a Purchase Order (PO) in ERP Cloud, a real-time PO event is generated. Oracle Integration captures this event and transforms the relevant data, pushing it to a custom table in Visual Builder Cloud Service (VBCS). The B2B component within Oracle Integration translates the PO payload into an EDI 850 document using the X12 Business Protocol, which is then delivered to a Trading Partner via FTP based on the Trading Partner agreement. Additionally, an approval workflow is initiated by an ERP Process user who selects the order and attaches Letter of Credit (LOC) information via a web form. Once approved, the PO record in ERP Cloud is updated with the LOC details for cross-referencing. Furthermore, OIC facilitates seamless interaction: Oracle Digital Assistant (ODA) initiates a conversation, requesting an Order Number, then connects with Integration to retrieve Order details and presents them to the user. details: This workshop showcases Oracle Integration by automating tasks. When a Purchase Order (PO) is made in ERP Cloud, OIC captures and synchronizes data with Custom VBCS application. The PO is also translated into an EDI 850 document for the Trading Partner and an approval process is initiated, linking Letter of Credit (LOC) details. Oracle Digital Assistant interacts to fetch Order Status and Details

This workshop introduces Oracle Integration (OIC) capabilities through a step-by-step scenario. When a user creates a Purchase Order (PO) in ERP Cloud, a real-time PO event is generated. Oracle Integration captures this event and transforms the relevant data, pushing it to a custom table in Visual Builder Cloud Service (VBCS). The B2B component within Oracle Integration translates the PO payload into an EDI 850 document using the X12 Business Protocol, which is then delivered to a Trading Partner via FTP based on the Trading Partner agreement. Additionally, an approval workflow is initiated by an ERP Process user who selects the order and attaches Letter of Credit (LOC) information via a web form. Once approved, the PO record in ERP Cloud is updated with the LOC details for cross-referencing. Furthermore, OIC facilitates seamless interaction: Oracle Digital Assistant (ODA) initiates a conversation, requesting an Order Number, then connects with Integration to retrieve Order details and presents them to the user.

Oracle Integration 3 - Automate Invoice Processing with OCI Document Understanding 11664 3979 OIC - Integration kishore.x.katta@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete In this Live Lab, we'll explore leveraging the OCI AI Services feature in OPA to build an automated invoice processing Orchestration workflow. This workflow will read invoice PDF documents, extract relevant data using AI powered document understanding service, validate the extracted information, and store it in a database. The workflow will notify the user if the extracted data is not approved. This tutorial will cover the following steps:

1. Ingesting Invoice PDF Documents: We'll start by ingesting invoice PDF documents into the workflow. This will be done by the stakeholder uploading the document by launching a processing application web form.

2. Extracting Invoice Data with OCI Document AI Service: Next, the workflow leverages OCI's Document AI Service to extract key information from the invoice PDFs, such as invoice number, date, total amount, line items, and vendor details. This AI Services document control leverages advanced machine learning models to understand the structure and layout of documents, enabling accurate data extraction.

3. Validating Extracted Invoice Data: After extracting the invoice data, we'll implement a validation process to ensure the integrity and completeness of the extracted information. This could involve checking for missing or inconsistent data

4. Triggering OIC Integration flow for saving the Invoices: If the extracted invoice data is deemed valid during the validation process, we'll trigger an OIC Integration flow. This Integration flow will initiate a series of actions to save the invoice in the database. We will OIC Event system to publish the Invoice details.

5. Storing Valid Invoice Data in a Database: A subscriber Integration flow will transform and persist the invoice details in a database for further processing or integration with other systems, such as accounting or enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems. For this Live lab we will consider the invoice records to be stored in a database. However, the design pattern can easily be extended to create another seamless subscriber integration flow and create an invoice record in ERP cloud.

Throughout the Live Lab, we'll explore the usage of OCI AI services- Document Understanding form control and extend the use case to invoke an integration flow to persist the invoice record in DB. We will also explore OPA Analytics to identify the process trends, and errors, and understand how long processes take to complete and why.

By the end of this Live Lab, you'll have a comprehensive understanding of how to build an end-to-end invoice processing Integration using OCI AI Services, ensuring accurate data extraction, validation, and storage, while streamlining the processing of valid invoices through automated workflows. Oracle Integration 3 - Build Intelligent Invoice Automation with OCI Document Understanding and OIC Decisions 11903 4193 OIC - Integration kishore.x.katta@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete - AI-powered invoice processing system using Oracle Integration
- Automated data extraction from PDF invoices without manual entry
- Smart approval routing based on business rules and risk factors
- Payment terms optimization for better cash flow management This comprehensive hands-on workshop will equip you with the skills to build intelligent document processing solutions by integrating Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC) with Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Document Understanding services. In today's digital business environment, manual invoice processing represents a significant operational bottleneck, and this workshop addresses that challenge by walking you through the creation of a real-world enterprise automation scenario where invoice documents are automatically extracted, analyzed, and routed through intelligent business rules.

During this workshop, you will learn to build an end-to-end intelligent automation flow that combines artificial intelligence for document understanding with sophisticated business decision logic for approval routing and payment optimization. Whether you work in accounts payable, financial operations, business process automation, or enterprise integration, this workshop will provide you with the practical experience needed to implement solutions that dramatically reduce manual effort, improve accuracy, and accelerate business processes.

Key Learning Objectives

- Extract Structured Data from Unstructured Documents
- Implement Intelligent Business Decision Logic
- Orchestrate End-to-End Automated Flow
- Design Event-Driven Architecture for Scalability

What You Will Learn

- Advanced Document Intelligence Integration:

How to integrate OIC with OCI Document Understanding to automate invoice data extraction, creating scalable workflows that eliminate manual data entry while maintaining high accuracy and reliability. You'll master the configuration of document understanding models, data mapping techniques, and error handling strategies for production deployments.

- Sophisticated Business Rules Implementation:

Practical use of OIC Decisions components to implement complex business logic using the FEEL (Friendly Enough Expression Language), including multi-variable decision tables, contextual risk assessment, and hierarchical decision structures that mirror real-world business policies and approval processes.

- Enterprise Integration Architecture Patterns:

Best practices for cloud-native integration design, including event-driven architecture, business rules design patterns.

- Real-World Financial Business Automation:

Hands-on experience with practical business scenarios on how to implement business rules such as vendor risk assessment, approval routing optimization, payment terms calculation, and cash flow management, enabling you to apply these skills directly to your organization's financial operations and accounts payable processes. Oracle Integration 3 - Cookbook - HCM Cloud Bulk Data Import 11355 3603 OIC - Integration kishore.x.katta@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete This workshop explores the use of Oracle Integration 3 HCM Cloud Adapter capabilities to load new hires data from third party sources, generate HCM Data Loader compatible file, and import Pending Workers into HCM Cloud. Pending Workers are imported to HCM in bulk using HCM Data Loader (HDL). In this use case, a new hires extract has been pseudo generated as a structured XML file to simulate generic external system export. Extracted file has been sent to the FTP server.
  
OIC 3 will trigger a scheduled integration to retrieve this file. Data from the file is imported into a structured schema. Using OIC 3 mapping capabilities the data is transformed into HCM Data Loader compatible file format with native schema definition and subsequently zipped, sent to UCM, and imported using HDL. Oracle Integration 3 - Get Started with Agentic AI in Oracle Integration 11983 4283 OIC - Integration kishore.x.katta@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Build an AI-powered clinical quality assurance agent using Oracle Integration Cloud. Learn to transform integrations into agentic AI tools, leverage Model Context Protocol (MCP) for tool discovery, and create intelligent agents that automate patient utilization reviews with adaptive decision-making powered by LLMs. - Build an intelligent Clinical Quality Assessment Agent that automates patient utilization reviews—evaluating medical necessity, ensuring guideline compliance, and identifying clinical improvement opportunities

- Master Agentic AI fundamentals: Learn how AI agents use Large Language Models to reason adaptively and orchestrate multiple integrations based on clinical context, unlike traditional fixed workflows

- Work with a healthcare use case featuring five specialised tools:
  - Patient record retrieval from healthcare systems
  - Clinical guideline matching for procedure-diagnosis pairs
  - Compliance validation against clinical criteria
  - Escalation decision-making based on quality scores
  - Evidence-based care plan recommendations

- Leverage Oracle Integration's Agentic AI framework to register integrations as tools, configure thinking patterns (ReAct, Plan and Execute), and build intelligent agents

- Enable Model Context Protocol (MCP) to expose your integrations as discoverable tools for external agent frameworks like Langflow and other AI platforms

- Gain hands-on experience creating an end-to-end AI agent that conducts comprehensive quality audits, validates guideline adherence, determines escalation requirements, and generates actionable audit reports

Oracle Integration 3 - Healthcare Accelerator - SCM to EHR Item Synchronization 12112 4446 OIC - Integration subhani.italapuram@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Learn how to use the Oracle Fusion Cloud SCM – Oracle Health EHR Item Synchronization Accelerator to automate the synchronization of item master, item location, and item cost data using Oracle Integration. Configure the accelerator, activate integrations, execute synchronization processes, and validate data exchange between Oracle Fusion Cloud SCM and Oracle Health EHR. The Sync Items from Oracle Fusion Cloud SCM to Oracle Health EHR workshop demonstrates how to implement and configure the Oracle Fusion Cloud SCM – Oracle Health EHR Item Synchronization Accelerator using Oracle Integration. This accelerator enables healthcare organizations to automate the exchange of item master, item location, and item cost information between Oracle Fusion Cloud SCM and Oracle Health EHR, reducing manual effort and improving data consistency across supply chain and clinical systems.

In this workshop, you will learn how the accelerator orchestrates item synchronization by extracting item data from Oracle Fusion Cloud SCM, storing the data in Oracle WebCenter Content, and using Oracle Integration to transform and load the information into Oracle Health EHR interface tables for downstream processing. You will also explore how Oracle Health transactions can be integrated with Oracle Fusion Cloud Inventory Management and Procurement processes.

Participants will install the accelerator, configure required connections, activate integrations, execute synchronization processes, monitor integration activity, and validate synchronized data. By the end of the lab, you will understand the end-to-end integration architecture and gain hands-on experience with a healthcare inventory synchronization solution that improves operational efficiency, data accuracy, and visibility across Oracle SCM and Oracle Health environments. records.searchable: Oracle Integration 3 - Intelligent Expense Automation with Agentic AI 12026 4340 OIC - Integration subhani.italapuram@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed This expense agent showcases an intelligent end-to-end automation flow that converts receipt images into validated expense entries with minimal manual effort. Using AI for data extraction, classification, and policy evaluation — with optional human approval when required — the process is orchestrated through Oracle Integration. This expense agent use case demonstrates an intelligent, end-to-end automation flow that transforms raw expense receipts into validated expense records with minimal manual intervention. The agent reads receipt images from a file server and sends them to OCI Document Understanding for structured data extraction, while OCI GenAI assists in classifying the expense type with contextual accuracy. A decision service evaluates policy rules to determine whether approval is required; when explicit authorization is needed, a human-in-the-loop (HITL) step is triggered to maintain governance and compliance. Once validated, the agent creates the expense entry in Oracle HCM Cloud. The entire process is orchestrated through Oracle Integration, where an agent built using a ReAct-style pattern dynamically invokes the appropriate tools based on defined guidelines. This architecture combines AI-driven insight, rule-based decisioning, and enterprise workflow orchestration to deliver a scalable, auditable, and intelligent expense processing experience. Oracle Integration 3 - Search FHIR Resources in an EMR Application 12052 4385 OIC - Integration subhani.italapuram@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Learn how to use Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC) to connect to an EMR system and retrieve healthcare data using FHIR APIs.
This live lab demonstrates how to search patient, appointment, medication, and practitioner data using a prebuilt integration recipe. Healthcare organizations rely on multiple systems such as Electronic Medical Records (EMR), insurance platforms, and clinical applications to manage patient data. However, integrating these systems and accessing healthcare data in a standardized way remains a significant challenge.

Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) is a widely adopted standard that enables seamless exchange of healthcare information across systems. By leveraging FHIR APIs, organizations can efficiently retrieve and manage critical healthcare data such as patient records, appointments, medications, and practitioner details.

In this Live Lab, you will learn how to use Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC) to integrate with an EMR system and search FHIR resources using a prebuilt integration recipe. The lab guides you through installing, configuring, and executing integration flows to retrieve healthcare data in real time, providing hands-on experience with healthcare interoperability and cloud-based integration. Healthcare organizations rely on multiple systems such as Electronic Medical Records (EMR), insurance platforms, and clinical applications to manage patient data. However, integrating these systems and accessing healthcare data in a standardized way remains a significant challenge.

Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) is a widely adopted standard that enables seamless exchange of healthcare information across systems. By leveraging FHIR APIs, organizations can efficiently retrieve and manage critical healthcare data such as patient records, appointments, medications, and practitioner details.

In this Live Lab, you will learn how to use Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC) to integrate with an EMR system and search FHIR resources using a prebuilt integration recipe. The lab guides you through installing, configuring, and executing integration flows to retrieve healthcare data in real time, providing hands-on experience with healthcare interoperability and cloud-based integration.

Oracle Integration 3 - Using OIC Native Actions to Harness OCI Services 11754 4041 OIC - Integration kishore.x.katta@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA - Learn to automate data workflows by integrating Oracle Integration (OIC) with Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI)
- Transfer Excel files from an FTP server to OCI Object Storage using OIC native actions.
- Convert Excel files to CSV format with an OCI serverless function.
- Process and stage CSV files in OIC for further data operations. This comprehensive hands-on workshop will equip you with the skills to automate and streamline data workflows by integrating Oracle Integration (OIC) with Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) services. In modern businesses, efficient data handling is critical, and this workshop addresses that need by walking you through the creation of a real-world integration scenario where data in Excel files is transferred, processed, and transformed automatically.

During this workshop, you will learn to build an end-to-end integration flow that automates file handling from an FTP server, converts files to a new format, and prepares them for further processing. Whether you work in data integration, IT operations, or business process automation, this workshop will give you the practical experience needed to implement solutions that save time and reduce manual effort.

Key Learning Objectives:
Transfer Excel Files to OCI Object Storage: You will learn how to use OIC native actions to list, download, and transfer Excel files from an FTP server to OCI Object Storage for secure and temporary storage.

Invoke Serverless Functions to Convert Excel Files: You will deploy an OCI serverless function that converts Excel files (.xls/.xlsx) into CSV format, automating data transformation.

Process CSV Files in OIC: After converting the files, you will use OIC to read and stage CSV files, preparing them for further integration tasks like reporting, analytics, or updating business applications.

What You Will Learn:
How to integrate OIC with OCI services to automate file transfers and transformations, creating scalable workflows.
Practical use of OIC native actions to manage Object Storage and invoke serverless functions.
Best practices for data security and processing, ensuring that file handling is efficient, secure, and streamlined.
Hands-on experience with real-life business cases, enabling you to apply these skills in your organization’s data operations. Oracle Linux Virtualization Manager (OLVM) on OCI 12098 4490 OCI perside.foster@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Hands-on workshop for deploying Oracle Linux Virtualization Manager (OLVM) on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. Participants must use their own OCI tenancy with the required IAM permissions, service limits, and VLAN support. This workshop guides participants through building and validating a complete Oracle Linux Virtualization Manager (OLVM) environment on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure using their own OCI tenancy.

Participants are responsible for bringing access to an OCI tenancy and target compartment where they have permission to create compute, networking, storage, public IP, VLAN, and NAT Gateway resources. The tenancy must also have sufficient service limits and Layer 2 network virtualization / VLAN support enabled in the target region before the workshop begins.

During the workshop, participants create a temporary bootstrap instance and use Ansible to provision the OCI infrastructure required for OLVM. They then install and configure the OLVM Engine, add two KVM hosts to the default cluster, configure logical networking and shared storage, import virtual machine templates, and validate VM connectivity.

The workshop also covers OCI-specific integration tasks, including VLAN-backed VM networking and configuring an OCI NAT Gateway for outbound internet access from virtual machines. Participants deploy a multi-tier application from prebuilt OVAs, review OLVM user and role administration, and complete the workshop by performing live migration of a running VM between KVM hosts. records.searchable: Oracle Machine Learning: Analyzing Social Media Sentiment with Oracle Database 11373 Machine Learning blake.hendricks@oracle.com Workshop Delete Requested In this 90-minute workshop, you will learn how to use Oracle Machine Learning (OML) with Oracle Database 23c to analyze social media sentiment in real-time. Oracle Machine Learning AutoML User Interface 4907 Machine Learning DB Product Management Workshop Approved Automated machine learning for data scientists, simplified machine learning for citizen data scientists, and accelerated machine learning model deployment for application developers Oracle Machine Learning (OML) in Oracle Autonomous Database provides access to in-database machine learning (ML) algorithms and functionality.  The AutoML User Interface (UI) makes machine learning easy. OML AutoML UI automates repetitive, time-consuming tasks typically taken by expert data scientists, simplifies machine learning for citizen data scientists, and accelerates machine learning model deployment for application developers. With just a few “clicks”, users specify a data table and the target attribute and OML AutoML UI data builds a model. OML AutoML UI automatically preprocesses the data, picks the best candidate algorithm(s) for the defined task from OML’s library of available in-database algorithms, and selects the right number of input data samples and features to improve model quality while speeding up model tuning.  OML AutoML UI builds OML models using the identified algorithms, tunes the hyperparameters and displays accuracy metrics so users can select the best model.
Using AutoML UI, data scientists and citizen data scientists can focus on the important phases of ML: Defining the problem, assembling the “right data”, disseminating the model’s insights and predictions and deploying the model enterprise-wide.  Perform this LiveLab to experience how easily machine learning can be with Oracle Machine Learning AutoML UI. Oracle Next React DB23ai Features and Framework 11497 Developers - Converged Workshop Approved This lab is designed to show how easy it is to build a Next-React app with Oracle 23ai as the backend. This lab begins with a minimal set of steps needed to customize a pre-built environment for building Oracle-Next-React (ONR) apps. It then it gives the bare-bones code required to develop a Oracle Next React full-stack web application with pages that respectively use each of the following Oracle 23ai converged database features:

ONR–Duality: This page will demonstrate that JSON-Relational Duality Views are a revolutionary, must-have technology for React-like developers because it reduces the complexity of storing JSON documents in normalized relational tables.

ONR-PGQ: Property Graph Query. PGQ is now part of the ISO standard SQL. This page will demonstrate how useful PGQ is for developers doing graph analytics in their application.

ONR-OML: This page will demonstrate the power of doing machine learning in the database using Oracle Machine Learning and having the ML models available in the database for applications to use directly. Oracle Real-World Performance Training 2100 Database jennifer.leung@oracle.com Workshop In Development Learn to use proper techniques to get exceptional performance from the Oracle Database in the real world for OLTP, and DW (analytical queries, batch processing)  and mixed workloads. The Real World Performance Group is part of the Oracle Database Development organization and focuses on achieving the maximum performance from the Oracle Database and hardware in the real world. We do this by identifying inefficiencies in current systems and applying modern database design and tuning techniques.

Goals
 1.  Identify the most common Oracle Database performance issues faced by customers
 2.  Use the correct tools to diagnose the root cause of a database performance issue

records.searchable: Oracle Sagas: Simplifying Distributed Application Development 11902 Database amit.ketkar@oracle.com Workshop In Development Explore Oracle Sagas—a native Oracle Database saga framework. In this hands-on session, you will use PL/SQL commands and Java annotations to orchestrate multi-step workflows, automatically trigger compensation on failure, and monitor saga execution in real time—equipping you with the skills to implement and manage resilient distributed transactions within Oracle Database. Modern applications increasingly span multiple services and systems, making it difficult to manage complex, long-running transactions that must maintain data consistency without locking resources indefinitely. Oracle Sagas offers a powerful, database-native solution—embedding the saga pattern directly into Oracle Database so developers can model, execute, and compensate distributed transactions without external orchestration tools or heavy locking. This six-lab LiveLab series, Oracle Sagas: Simplifying Distributed Application Development, delivers a step-by-step, hands-on journey through every aspect of the framework: from initial concepts and environment setup to coding, deploying, and testing real sagas in both PL/SQL and Java. By the end of these immersive labs, you will have built practical skills and reusable patterns for embedding lock-free, compensating workflows into your own applications. It is well suited to running in containerized environments and, combined with the TimesTen Kubernetes Operator, provides a simple and robust solution for high performance, highly available The TimesTen Operator is designed for simple deployment of your active standby pairs of TimesTen Classic databases and for automated failure detection and recovery. The TimesTen Operator performs all these functions and works to keep the databases up and running with minimal effort on your part.

Oracle Verrazzano Fundamentals 7022 853 Weblogic adrian.padilla@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Delete Requested This lab shows how to install Verrazzano platform on a single Kubernetes cluster and deploy sample application using Verrazzano concepts. About Product/Technology:
Verrazzano is an end-to-end enterprise container platform for deploying cloud-native and traditional applications in multi-cloud and hybrid environments. It is made up of a curated set of open source components – many that you may already use and trust, and some that were written specifically to pull together all of the pieces that make Verrazzano a cohesive and easy to use platform.

Verrazzano includes the following capabilities:
-Hybrid and multicluster workload management
-Special handling for WebLogic, Coherence, and Helidon applications
-Multicluster infrastructure management
-Integrated and pre-wired application monitoring
-Integrated security
-DevOps and GitOps enablement

Bob’s Books sample application consists of three main parts:
-A back-end “order processing” application, which is a Java EE application with REST services and a very simple JSP UI, which stores data in a MySQL database. This application runs on WebLogic Server.
-A front-end web store “Robert’s Books”, which is a general book seller. This is implemented as a Helidon microservice, which gets book data from Coherence, uses a Coherence cache store to persist data for the order manager, and has a React web UI.
-A front-end web store “Bobby’s Books”, which is a specialty children’s book store. This is implemented as a Helidon microservice, which gets book data from a (different) Coherence cache store, interfaces directly with the order manager, and has a JSF web UI running on WebLogic Server. Oracle WebCenter Content - Using Folios and Content Basket 11872 WebCenter cordell.melgaard@oracle.com Workshop Approved Oracle WebCenter Content Server provides a quick and effective way to assemble, track, and access logical groupings of multiple content items from within the secure environment of Oracle WebCenter Content Server. For example, you can assemble all items relevant to an upcoming brochure, such as images, logos, legal disclosures, and ad copy, and send them through a workflow process. Technically, a content folio is an XML file checked into the repository that uses elements to
define the hierarchy of nodes, slots, and specified content items in Content Server. In practice,
a content folio is a logical grouping, or a framework in which content stored in the repository
can be structured. A simple folio is a flat container, while advanced folios can nest content in a
hierarchy within folders. In an advanced folio, the hierarchy may be established prior to
assembling content items, or it may be created during content assembly
Perhaps a new project requires a virtual place to assemble all relevant content items in a particular hierarchy, whenever they are checked in, with restricted access to particular areas of the hierarchy. Or a video may have to be associated and tracked with release waivers and narration text. ORDS: Create a Python Web Application in Oracle Autonomous Database using ORDS REST APIs 11130 3382 Developers - Database chris.hoina@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Your Python applications need to use MongoDB or SQLite if you want to persist data and do 'fancy' data calculations. And of course, you'll have to be a SQL or JSON expert, right? Wrong!

Learn today how you can leverage your favorite Python libraries (Flask, WTForms, Folium, etc.), and simply plug in our existing REST APIs for our Oracle Database! Your Python applications need to use MongoDB or SQLite if you want to persist data and do 'fancy' data calculations. And of course, you'll have to be a SQL or JSON expert, right? Wrong!

Learn today how you can leverage your favorite Python libraries (Flask, WTForms, Folium, etc.), and simply plug in our existing REST APIs for our Oracle Database!

Oracle REST APIs allow you to submit transactions, pull data, and even generate interactive maps. Our managed Oracle Cloud Autonomous Database takes care of your backups, upgrades, and high availability. If you want to add a row to your table, simply do a POST to the appropriate HTTPS endpoint!

We'll give you an OpenAPI spec / Swagger set of REST APIs and some Python code. You'll get to plug them in and bring your Python app to life! ORDS: Create a Python Web Application in Oracle Autonomous Database using ORDS REST APIs 11130 4024 Developers - Database chris.hoina@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Your Python applications need to use MongoDB or SQLite if you want to persist data and do 'fancy' data calculations. And of course, you'll have to be a SQL or JSON expert, right? Wrong!

Learn today how you can leverage your favorite Python libraries (Flask, WTForms, Folium, etc.), and simply plug in our existing REST APIs for our Oracle Database! Your Python applications need to use MongoDB or SQLite if you want to persist data and do 'fancy' data calculations. And of course, you'll have to be a SQL or JSON expert, right? Wrong!

Learn today how you can leverage your favorite Python libraries (Flask, WTForms, Folium, etc.), and simply plug in our existing REST APIs for our Oracle Database!

Oracle REST APIs allow you to submit transactions, pull data, and even generate interactive maps. Our managed Oracle Cloud Autonomous Database takes care of your backups, upgrades, and high availability. If you want to add a row to your table, simply do a POST to the appropriate HTTPS endpoint!

We'll give you an OpenAPI spec / Swagger set of REST APIs and some Python code. You'll get to plug them in and bring your Python app to life! ORDS: Create RESTful APIs for your Oracle Autonomous Database with ORDS 580 578 Database chris.hoina@oracle.com Workshop Delete Requested Public Delete Requested Load data, REST enable a table and protect the service quickly and easily with Oracle REST Data Services (ORDS) and the Autonomous Database. Oracle REST Data Services (ORDS) bridges HTTPS and your Oracle Database. A mid-tier Java application, ORDS provides a Database Management REST API, a SQL Worksheet, a PL/SQL Gateway, SODA for REST, and the ability to publish RESTful Web Services for interacting with the data and stored procedures in your Oracle Database. 

In this workshop, you will start by loading data into a table in an Autonomous Database. Then, with a single click, see how ORDS can REST enable that table so that it may be used by applications or exposed as APIs. Finally, secure these REST endpoints so that only authorized clients can utilize them. records.searchable: Perform Access Reviews with Oracle Access Governance using OIG integration 11315 3595 OCI indiradarshni.balasundaram@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA This workshop gives you the complete end to end experience of Oracle Access Governance. In this workshop, you will be able to create OAG service instance, install the OIG agent, connect to OIG which is pre-provisioned as part of the workshop, import data into OAG, and run various OAG use cases including  campaigns, access reviews, event based access reviews and much more. Oracle Access Governance is a SaaS IGA solution that addresses the growing challenges security owners face in dealing with the increase in advanced security threats and regulations. This cloud native solution helps meet governance and compliance requirements across many applications, workloads, infrastructures, and identity platforms. It provides organization-wide visibility and capabilities to identify anomalies and mitigate security risks across cloud and on-premises environments. Using prescriptive analytics, Oracle Access Governance offers an intuitive user experience, provides recommendations and insights into access entitlements, behaviors, and risks. This lab will take you through the steps to create Access Governance instance, agent installation, identity orchestration with OIG, create campaigns, perform access reviews, try out event based access reviews and much more. records.searchable: Perform machine learning on streaming data using OCI Data Flow 11204 3438 OCI sujoy.chowdhury@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA In this Hands On Lab, you will perform machine learning on streaming data using OCI Data Flow. To tackle predictive maintenance in manufacturing, fraud detection in financial services, or detect diseases early in healthcare, data engineers and data scientists need capabilities for real-time data processing from various sources. OCI Data Flow, a fully managed spark service, enables you to do the heavy lifting of stream processing with Spark and perform machine learning on streaming data using MLLib. Attend this hands on lab to discover different use cases for machine learning on streaming data and how Spark Streaming in OCI Data Flow service simplifies this process for a Data Scientist. We will walk you through a practical example from the industry and build Spark apps in OCI Data Flow to predict remaining useful life of an equipment. records.searchable: Pinpoint suspicious financial transactions with Oracle Spatial and Python 11388 3683 Database - Spatial and Graph david.lapp@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Fraud detection relies on the ability to identify outliers and anomalies compared to "normal" behavior. The analysis of location patterns plays an essential role in the process. In this workshop you will prepare data and perform feature extraction in Oracle Spatial and operate on that data with spatial ML algorithms in a Python notebook to identify potentially fraudulent financial transactions. You've been alerted to possible fraudulent use of your credit card. How was it determined that fraud is likely? Fraud detection relies on the ability to identify outliers and anomalies compared to "normal" behavior. The analysis of location patterns plays an essential role in the process. For example, within a narrow time window is there a transaction far from a geographically concentrated set of typical transactions? Oracle Autonomous AI Database includes Oracle Spatial with features for geospatial data management and analysis. Combining Oracle Spatial with robust Python libraries for geospatial ML provides a robust platform to address the challenge of transaction fraud. In this workshop you will prepare data and perform feature extraction in Oracle Spatial and operate on that data with spatial ML algorithms in a Python notebook to ultimately find the needle of fraud in the haystack of financial transactions. Postgres GoldenGate Replication Using Standard Backup/Restore for Initial Load 11748 GoldenGate sugandha.kher@oracle.com Workshop Approved GoldenGate migration from on-prem or other CSP PostgreSQL or OCI Managed PostgreSQL using pg_dump and pg_restore with LSN based backup. Oracle GoldenGate Extract does not support seamless role transitioning from a primary to a secondary Extract with PostgreSQL high availability configurations. However, manual procedural operations could be followed to provide continuity from the new primary Extract.
In this Lab we are running a solution to avoid the manual operation and instead use pg_dump and pg_restore utilities with LSN based backup which would avoid the unneccessary use of deploying extra EXTRACT and REPLICAT for doing the initial load. This solution cuts the initial load drastically and at the same time data consistency is maintained for Change Data Capture (CDC) part of Oracle GoldenGate. Visualize the data using Oracle Application Express. Automotive insurance fraud involves someone deceiving an insurance company about a claim involving their personal or commercial motor vehicle. It can involve giving out misleading information or providing false documentation to support the claim. This workshop highlights the use of two Oracle Machine Learning notebooks working in conjunction with automobile insurance claims investigators in a two-step process. First, we use Oracle Machine Learning to “flag” for the investigator anomalous insurance claims using an unsupervised learning algorithm (1-Class Support Vector Machine). We help the claims investigators focus on the most suspicious claims using their expertise and knowledge using an Oracle APEX application. Expected goals (xG) is a predictive model used to assess every goal-scoring chance, and the likelihood of scoring. The xG model computes for each chance, the probability to score based on factors such as distance, position of defenders, type and speed of pass, type of shot, shot angles and various other aspects (Event-based variables).

You will prepare match data on Autonomous to make it ready for analysis, visualize data on a football pitch, train your own xG machine learning model and apply your model to recent matches to understand team and player performance. records.searchable: Prevent and Detect Fraud with Immutable and Blockchain Tables on Oracle Autonomous Database 11831 4142 Database amit.ketkar@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Learn how Oracle Blockchain Tables and Immutable Tables provide tamper-resistant data storage within your database. This LiveLab walks you through their key features, ensuring data remains secure, verifiable, and unchangeable. Oracle Blockchain Tables and Immutable Tables offer a structured approach to maintaining data integrity, security, and verifiability within the Oracle Database. This LiveLab demonstrates how these technologies use cryptographic signing, digest generation, and verification to preserve trust and support auditability. In Blockchain Tables, each row is cryptographically chained to the previous one, forming a secure and traceable record history. The digest feature captures periodic snapshots of table state, which can be independently verified to detect tampering or anomalies. Through hands-on exercises, you'll learn how these capabilities support compliance, fraud detection, and secure transaction logging. Both features are available in Oracle Database 19c, 21c, and 23ai. We'll start with two key components of MovieSteam's architecture. MovieStream is storing its data across Oracle Object Storage and Autonomous Database. Data is captured from various sources into a landing zone in object storage. This data is then processed (cleansed, transformed, and optimized) and stored in a gold zone on object storage. Once the data is curated, it is loaded into an Autonomous Database where it is analyzed by many (and varied) members of the user community - from data analysts to data scientists. These users will take advantage of a variety of Autonomous Database capabilities: advanced Oracle SQL to glean customer insights, Oracle Machine Learning to predict churn, and Oracle Spatial and Graph to provide targeted promotions. Project Panama Hands-on Labs 11194 3440 Other - I don't see it david.delabassee@oracle.com Workshop Published Event Quarterly QA In this lab, you will learn how to access native libraries from Java using the Foreign Function & Memory API. You will also learn about SIMD programming and how to use the new Vector API to write more efficient code that is portable across CPUs.

Join this lab to learn how Project Panama helps securely bridge Java with the native world, and get some initial hands-on experience with its APIs. Project Panama is about interconnecting the Java Virtual Machine and native code. Panama's Foreign Function & Memory API and tool work together to provide a safe, modern, and efficient way to access foreign memory and foreign code from Java. The Vector API, another Panama API, enables SIMD (Single Instruction Multiple Data) programming from plain Java.

During this hands-on lab, you will learn how to access native libraries from Java code using the Foreign Function & Memory API. You will also see how to leverage the new Vector API to write more efficient code that is portable across CPUs.

In this workshop, you will learn how to protect and recover Oracle AI Databases running on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) in the event of a ransomware attack. Get hands-on experience using the Zero Data Loss Autonomous Recovery Service to protect Oracle AI Database 26ai. Gain a clear understanding of ransomware protection and cyber-resiliency when operating in a cloud environment. High Performance Computing is changing product development and research enabling customers to solve complex problems faster. This means fewer prototypes, accelerates testing, and decreases time to market. Oracle offers on-demand HPC infrastructure, suitable for any HPC workload, based on the most advanced compute, storage, networking, and software technologies. You get all this at a fraction of the cost of building it yourself and avoid capacity utilization issues.

Oracle provides the most elastic and scalable cloud infrastructure to run your HPC applications. With virtually unlimited capacity, engineers, researchers, and HPC system owners can innovate beyond the limitations of on-premises HPC infrastructure. Oracle delivers an integrated suite of services that provides everything needed to quickly and easily build and manage HPC clusters in the cloud to run the most compute intensive workloads across various industry verticals. These workloads span the traditional HPC applications, like genomics, computational chemistry, financial risk modeling, computer aided engineering, seismic imaging, and weather prediction, as well as emerging applications, like machine learning, deep learning, and autonomous driving. Provision Kafka clusters with OCI Streaming with Apache Kafka service 11954 OCI abhishek.bhaumik@oracle.com Workshop Approved OCI Streaming with Apache Kafka is a fully managed Kafka service which allows you to build real-time, distributed data streaming pipelines, which can, collect, process, store and move millions of events per minute in a cost-efficient manner. 
In this workshop you will learn to deploy OCI Streaming with Apache Kafka clusters through CLI and console. OCI Streaming with Apache Kafka is a fully managed Kafka service which allows you to build real-time, distributed data streaming pipelines, which can, collect, process, store and move millions of events per minute in a cost-efficient manner. 
You can use OCI Streaming with Apache Kafka for:
Real-time AI Training Data Foundation: Stream and aggregate real-time data from diverse sources, providing up-to-date, high-quality datasets essential for training and retraining AI and large language models (LLMs) on fresh business or operational signals.
Vector Database Pipelines for GenAI and RAG: Stream processed data, including vector embeddings, directly to integrated vector databases (such as those used in AI search or Retrieval-Augmented Generation scenarios), enabling AI models to leverage contextual and up-to-date information to enhance output relevance and accuracy.
AI Agent and Multi-Agent System Orchestration: Establish real-time communication and event sharing between AI microservices or agents, support agent state management, and coordinate dynamic workflows with streaming pipelines for more responsive and autonomous AI solutions.
Realtime Data Analysis: Continuously stream IoT and patient device data for proactive health monitoring, predictive analysis, and timely intervention.
User Behavior Analytics: Capture and process real-time data on user interactions across web and mobile applications to gain actionable insights and  personalized recommendations. 
Demand Forecasting: Stream and analyze live sales and operational data to improve on-the-fly predictions, forecasting accuracy and support data-driven business decisions.
Fraud Detection: Continuously monitor financial transactions in real time to identify suspicious patterns, anomaly detection and respond swiftly to potential fraud threats.
Change Data Capture (CDC): Seamlessly stream database changes into analytics platforms or data lakes to keep downstream systems synchronized with the latest data with low latency.
In this workshop, you will learn: 
How to create a cluster from console and OCI CLI
How to create, update and delete topics and partitions through Kafka CLI

records.searchable: Quickstart your records disposition program with WebCenter Content : Records 11021 3327 WebCenter NA License SE Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete This workshop will help set up an Enterprise Records Management Solution. WebCenter Content: Records enables organizations to define, manage, and execute records and retention policies for all enterprise content from a single application. In this workshop, you will create a disposition schedule for the Legal Documents category. There will be one record folder for each agreement where records related to a specific agreement will be assigned to the correct folder. The Legal Documents category will contain record folders like MOU's, Non-disclosure Agreements and Software Agreement Documents each having specific disposition rules that have custom triggers and periods. We will then set up the disposition schedule to use folder inheritance so that all of the records in the same folder will be disposed of together. All the records prior to disposal are subjected to review by authorized users in a workflow. In order to retain certain documents after the disposition condition is met, legal holds will be placed on records to prevent accidental or intentional deletion of documents. details: This workshop will help set up an Enterprise Records Management Solution.

WebCenter Content: Records enables organizations to define, manage, and execute records and retention policies for all enterprise content from a single application. In this workshop, you will create a disposition schedule for the Legal Documents category. There will be one record folder for each agreement where records related to a specific agreement will be assigned to the correct folder. The Legal Documents category will contain record folders like MOU's, Non-disclosure Agreements and Software Agreement Documents each having specific disposition rules that have custom triggers and periods. We will then set up the disposition schedule to use folder inheritance so that all of the records in the same folder will be disposed of together. All the records prior to disposal are subjected to review by authorized users in a workflow. In order to retain certain documents after the disposition condition is met, legal holds will be placed on records to prevent accidental or intentional deletion of documents.

records.searchable:
R2RML Engine: Bridging Data Type Diversity for Seamless Data Integration 11858 Database - Spatial and Graph maryam.sajjadian@oracle.com Workshop In Development R2RML in converged databases facilitates seamless information exchange by converting diverse data types into a unified RDF format. Converged databases handle heterogeneous data types such as JSON, XML, and CSV, which have different structures and often belong to separate domains or come from various sources. These data types do not naturally connect. However, the R2RML (RDB to RDF Mapping Language) engine provides a solution by transforming these diverse data types into a unified and interconnected RDF(Resource Description Framework) graph format.

This semantic layer helps define complex relationships between data, preserving the unique features of each source while connecting them in a flexible manner. It is referred to as a semantic layer because it adds meaning to the raw data by establishing relationships and context between different data types. Through this process, R2RML enables a better understanding and utilization of data across different domains, without the extra effort required to link data together through the various join functionalities typically used in traditional relational databases.

While traditional relational databases struggle with RDF support, applications like Spatial Studio can leverage APIs or views to access and visualize this unified RDF graph. By exposing RDF data through APIs or materialized views, even non-RDF users can seamlessly interact with and benefit from enriched spatial relationships. This approach enables applications that do not natively support RDF to still consume and utilize the data, making it more accessible for spatial analysis and visualization without requiring expertise in semantic technologies. Refreshable bidirectional read-only clones at the pluggable database level and cross-container operations can be used for data replication and reporting purposes. This workshop use case has two sites, Site A and Site B, but these principles can be applied to a multi-site configuration. Data in local pluggable databases can be updated, and data from read-only refreshable clones can be used for reporting. These clones can be used in read/write mode for testing purposes, too, and re-created when finished because it's not possible to turn them back into refreshable read-only clone mode. Red Bull Racing Honda Win: Develop an Interactive Map of a Racetrack 7941 896 Analytics catalin.dinescu@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Explore Red Bull racing Honda win by developing an interactive map of a racetrack with GeoJSON in Oracle Analytics Cloud. On September 5, 2021, Red Bull Racing Honda, a leading Formula 1 team, took the podium at the Formula 1 Heineken Dutch Grand Prix 2021 at Circuit Zandvoort in the Netherlands using Oracle Cloud Infrastructure as its official cloud platform. 

Winning the race required driver Max Verstappen to complete 72 laps around the 4.259 km circuit with an overall distance of 306.648 km or just over 190 miles.

Reducing Container Pull and Startup Time on OCI VMs with FSS/Lustre Caching 12021 4378 OCI adina.nicolescu@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed A hands-on workshop that walks through deploying an automated OCI demo (Terraform + cloud-init) that mounts FSS/Lustre as a shared container layer cache, configures Podman additionalimagestores, and then benchmarks cold vs warm pulls/starts to quantify the startup-time gains on OCI VMs. This workshop provides a step-by-step guide to reducing container image pull and startup time on OCI VMs by introducing a shared, network-attached cache for container layers using OCI File Storage Service (FSS) and Lustre. You will provision the required OCI infrastructure with Terraform (VCN, compute, and shared storage), then use a cloud-init–driven VM bootstrap to install and configure Podman with additionalimagestores pointing to the shared cache paths.

You will run a repeatable benchmark workflow to compare cold vs warm container pulls and container starts, validate that cached layers are being reused across runs, and capture concrete timing results that demonstrate the impact of shared caching on startup latency. The lab progresses incrementally—starting with FSS for simplicity, then extending the same approach to Lustre for higher-performance scenarios—so participants leave with a practical reference implementation and a clear decision framework for when to use FSS vs Lustre for large-scale deployments. Reimage-ing Search: AI Vector Search with Oracle Database 23ai 11648 4000 Database david.start@oracle.com Workshop Published Private Completed In this workshop we dive into the exciting world of leveraging images and text with powerful Large Language Models (LLMs) with your Oracle Database. Whether you’re interested in enhancing your queries with Oracle’s AI Vector Search capabilities or simply want to dive into the Vector data type, this workshop will guide you through the process. In this workshop we dive into the exciting world of leveraging images and text with powerful Large Language Models (LLMs) with your Oracle Database. Whether you’re interested in enhancing your queries with Oracle’s AI Vector Search capabilities or simply want to dive into the Vector data type, this workshop will guide you through the process. Get ready to unlock the full potential of your data.

This workshop outlines a two-step approach to tackle a problem by leveraging two different models. The first model generates descriptions for images, while the second model creates vectors for these textual descriptions. The second model is loaded in the database allowing for both vector generation and AI Vector Search without leaving the database. By separating the tasks, the complexity is reduced, making it easier to use existing models, as very few can handle both images and text simultaneously. This approach not only simplifies the problem but also broadens the range of available large language models (LLMs) since each task is more straightforward on its own. Rocky DEM Runbook 4281 HPC breanna.mendonca@oracle.com Workshop In Development This Runbook will take you through the process of deploying a Rocky DEM on Oracle Cloud with low latency networking between the compute nodes. Running Rocky DEM on Oracle Cloud is quite straightforward, follow along this guide for all the tips and tricks. This Runbook will take you through the process of deploying a GPU machine on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, installing Rocky DEM, configuring the license, and then running a model.

Rocky DEM simulates particles and can be coupled with Computational Fluid Dynamic or Finite Element Method. It adds another layer of complexity which results in increased simulation time. To help speed up the run, Rocky DEM provides the option to parallelize to a high number of CPU. For even more speed, it can unleash the full power of one or multiple GPUs.

Running Rocky on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, there is no special setup needed and no driver headache. Import your model, choose the number of CPUs or GPUs and off you go. This removes the wait time for resources that you may have on your on-premise cluster. It avoids having people battling for high-end GPUs at peak times and having them idle for the rest of the week. Running AI workloads in Oracle Kubernetes Engine (OKE) is easier than you think. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) provides a wide variety of GPU-enabled nodes, both virtual and bare metal, tailored to run as worker nodes in your Kubernetes cluster. These come pre-installed with NVIDIA drivers and device plugin daemon-set, simplifying setup.

Oracle Database can access data from any source, structured or unstructured. This challenge can be achieved on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, where you have all the resources you need at a click. It is possible to use even a free cloud account if we consider a simple task like this. Wouldn't it be awesome to query PowerPoint presentations using SQL to find some information in the slides or the notes? Oracle Database can access data from any source, structured or unstructured. You must find a way to ingest those sources into the database and understand their format. This workflow can be built and deployed on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, where you have all the resources you need at a click. Running AI workloads on Oracle Kubernetes Engine (OKE) is more straightforward than you might expect. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) provides a variety of GPU-enabled nodes, available in both virtual and bare metal options, designed to act as worker nodes within your Kubernetes clusters. These nodes come pre-configured with NVIDIA drivers and a device plugin daemon-set, making setup quick and easy.

Oracle DB 23ai adds significant value by offering robust vector storage capabilities, which are critical for managing complex, high-dimensional data such as embeddings used in AI applications. Utilizing Oracle DB 23ai as a vector store allows AI systems to efficiently store and retrieve data for more advanced operations. With OCI, you can securely run Large Language Models (LLMs) in your own environment, enabling them to draw insights from your enterprise’s specific data. The implementation of Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines further enhances LLM functionality, allowing these models to provide accurate answers based on new data, improving overall performance while cutting down on training and fine-tuning costs. Schröedinger's Document: JSON Relational Duality Views in Oracle Database 23ai 11425 3753 JSON/XML ramona.magadan@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Completed Author: Jim Czuprynski, Oracle ACE Director, Zero Defect Computing, Inc.

Explore how the new JSON Relational Duality Views (JRDVs) in Oracle Database 23ai make it simpler than ever for your DevOps teams to build robust applications at extreme speed without having to worry about how data is stored within your database. Author: Jim Czuprynski, Oracle ACE Director, Zero Defect Computing, Inc.

NoSQL databases have proliferated in recent years because they often use JSON documents as their basis for data storage and retention. But the advantages of JSON – simple datatype mapping, schema-less development, easy-to-understand hierarchies, and best of all, no curmudgeonly DBAs to deal with! – often neglect the myriad advantages of relational databases, including guaranteed data consistency, dramatically efficient queries, and high availability and recoverability in case of system failures.

This session will demonstrate how the new JSON Relational Duality Views (JRDVs) in Oracle Database 23ai make it simpler than ever for your DevOps teams to build robust applications at extreme speed without having to worry about how data is stored within your database. It will also illustrate how modern Oracle DBAs can use JRDVs to provide extreme availability and consistent data modeling standards while providing a single platform solution for future development efforts that fulfill applications that demand using analytics, machine learning, spatial, and graph to provide answers to tough business questions. Search Documents and Images stored in Object Storage using OpenSearch, AI Vision, Text Recognition 11272 3442 Developers - Converged marc.gueury@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Search Documents uploaded to Object Storage in a Google like search engine.
Document could be 
- Word, Excel, PDF, ... , 
- Images using Artificial Intelligence:
  - Image Labelling 
  -Text Recognition.
- Custom document: Images of Belgian ID cards Search Documents uploaded to Object Storage in a Google like search engine.
Document could be 
- Word, Excel, PDF, ... , 
- Images that are preprocessed using Artificial Intelligence, Image Labelling and Text Recognition.
- Belgian ID cards using Text recognition

It uses LowCode development both for Integration and Visualisation.

It works like this:
- a document is uploaded to the Object Storage.
- an event is raised and queue in Streaming (Kafka)
- the event are processed in Oracle Integration Cloud 
- based on the file type, it will process it in the adequate way

AI agents are creating new paths to enterprise data. Traditional application-layer controls, proxies, sidecars, and perimeter defenses may not be enough when the database sees only an overprivileged service account or broad application role.
