records.searchable: Secure SSH to OCI Bastion Host 11722 4019 OCI olivia.maxwell@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Completed Use core OCI concepts such as compartments, VCNs, subnets, security lists, Internet/ NAT Gateways to create and connect your Bastion Host instance to your private instance via SSH access in the CloudShell. Connect to your secure OCI bastion host through SSH for a secure and controlled gateway to access your private instances in your VCN. This LiveLab walks you through generating an SSH key, creating a compartment, creating a VCN with public & private subnets, and two compute instances (one public and one private). After the preparing your resources, you will then securely connect through the Cloud Shell using SSH. You will connect to the instance by using your private instance ssh key and your public instance IP address. You will then create your private key file, change security on the file so other users cannot access and re-connect to private instance using your private key and private IP. This allows you to establish a secure connection using SSH to your private instances while maintaining integrity of your OCI environment. With OCI Vault « Bring Your Own Key » and External KMS features, you stay in control of your keys, storing them where you want, and you can still use the advanced IaaS and pass features of OCI. Did you know you can manage your encryption keys outside of OCI? That’s an important security requirement from many customers around the world, specifically to answer Sovereignty requirements. In this HOL, you will learn how to manage your encryption keys outside of OCI using a Thales HSM. With OCI Vault « Bring Your Own Key » and External KMS features, you stay in control of your keys, storing them where you want, and you can still use the advanced IaaS and pass features of OCI. This Hands-On Lab will walk you through how to enable the feature, link your HSM outside of OCI to your OCI tenant and start encrypting data in OCI, for storage encryption and OCI Database encryption through TDE support. Now your Master Encryption Keys never leave your own HSM. Securing your Apps and Users with Identity Cloud Service 2600 OCI alejandro.casas@oracle.com Workshop Approved As part of this Lab, you will use Oracle Identity Cloud Service APIs and integrate IDCS with a custom app developed in Node.js

Upon completion of this Lab you will be able to:

- Navigate Oracle Identity Cloud Service Console
- Create a confidential app
- Provision the app to a user
- Integrate Oracle Identity Cloud Service with custom apps by leveraging the available SDKs Oracle Identity Cloud Service (IDCS) is an Identity-as-a-Service (IDaaS) solution available in Oracle Public Cloud (OPC). It is designed to extend enterprise controls by automating PaaS and SaaS account provisioning and de-provisioning, simplifying the user experience for accessing cloud applications by providing seamless integration with enterprise identity stores and authentication services, and facilitating compliance activities by clearly reporting on cloud application usage.

As part of this Lab, you will use Oracle Identity Cloud Service APIs and integrate IDCS with a custom app developed in Node.js

Oracle Identity Cloud Service provides a Software Development Kit (SDK) that you download from the console, and can be used to integrate Node.js web applications with Oracle Identity Cloud Service.

Upon completion of this Lab you will be able to:

- Navigate Oracle Identity Cloud Service Console
- Create a confidential app
- Provision the app to a user
- Integrate Oracle Identity Cloud Service with custom apps by leveraging the available SDKs
- Experience Oracle Identity Cloud Service Single Sign-On Capabilities Individual author Individual Content to review/remove Missing LiveLabs ID in current WMS export; review as a draft or unpublished row 2600 Workshop Approved OCI 2025-08-14 2020-10-09 Individual author Individual No Repository Url 2600 Workshop Approved OCI 2025-08-14 2020-10-09 Individual author Individual No Repository Url No repository URL is present in the current WMS export. alejandro.casas@oracle.com OSPA As part of this Lab, you will use Oracle Identity Cloud Service APIs and integrate IDCS with a custom app developed in Node.js

See what your network in OCI is doing 11622 3989 OCI Marketing Workshop Published Disabled Completed Almost every source in your OCI environment uses the network, but how much, when, and where to? Are you using more than expected? Is traffic going where you didn't expect? Learn how to use Flow Logs to understand the traffic patterns and then use traffic mirroring to investigate traffic for specific resources. With the rapid growth of cloud deployments, have you considered how to monitor and explore your Oracle Cloud Infrastructure with existing OCI resources.  Can you imagine the insights and power you and your team can harness with an understanding of how deployed cloud resources are being utilized and consumed? OCI has the built-in tools and services that provide the insights across all your deployed resources.

In this session we will demonstrate how to effectively deploy an infrastructure consuming of network and compute resources.  We will begin by creating a foundation with the virtual cloud network (VCN), include subnets, security list, routing and the corresponding compute representing client and server resources. The focus of the session with them shift to using Virtual Tap Access Points (VTAPs) and Flow Logs to facilitate troubleshooting, provide security analysis and explore data monitoring. At the end of the session, you will walk away with a complete understanding of the OCI components required to create your application foundation and the tools and services required to effectively monitor and manage your resources. Set up live data sharing between Oracle AI Databases using Cloud Links and PL/SQL APIs 11522 3881 ADB Serverless lauran.serhal@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Learn how to share live data between Oracle AI Databases using Cloud Links and PL/SQL APIs. Data Sharing allows customers to improve their business and open up new opportunities by making the same data available to one or many consumers. Cloud Link allow to share real-time data without need to copy or replicate it. Learn how to share live data with Cloud Links using PL/SQL in Oracle Autonomous AI Database. The benefits are:
- Data is securely shared
- Data is not replicated as it's managed in a single place
- Easily manage data access privileges
- Easy to find data you're interested in

Set up live data sharing between Oracle AI Databases using Database Actions 11613 3983 ADB Serverless lauran.serhal@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Learn how to set up live data sharing between Autonomous AI Databases using Data Studio. Data Share allows customers to improve their business and opens new opportunities by making the same data available to one or many consumers. With live data sharing, you can share data as of the latest database commit with Autonomous AI Databases in the same region. The views can be queried using SQL scripts. Learn how to set up live data sharing between Oracle Autonomous AI Databases using Cloud links (direct connection) and Data Studio. Data sharing is making the same data share available to one or many consumers. With live data sharing, you can share data as of the latest database commit with Autonomous AI Databases in the same region. The recipient will always see the latest data. To provide access to live shared data, you must define data shares and grant recipients access to consume them.  To consume live data shares, the recipient needs to subscribe to them and create views of tables included in the live share. The views can be queried using SQL scripts. 
Nowadays, the ever-growing amount of data has become a strategic asset for any company. Sharing data - within your organization or externally - is an enabling technology for new business opportunities. Sharing data and consuming data from external sources allows to collaborate with partners, establish new partnerships and generate new revenue streams with data monetization. Set up your database instance as an AI Proxy Database ("sidecar") for federated data access 12047 AI/ML Database sarika.surampudi@oracle.com Workshop Approved Learn how to set up your database instance as an AI Proxy Database to access remote data for use with Select AI. without having to move your data to Oracle. Customers store data in a variety of sources and may be unable to migrate their data to Oracle, but that’s not a problem for Select AI. Using what we refer to as an AI Proxy Database approach, also known as a “sidecar,” you can extend Select AI beyond your database by exposing external data sources as objects in your database schema. If Select AI can “see” such tables or views, it can leverage your chosen LLM to generate federated SQL queries across them. Remote data sources can be both Oracle and non-Oracle data sources, whether in the cloud or on premises.

In this workshop, you'll map sources into your database schema, creating views over database links and define external tables. You can even add local table and column comments or annotations to improve intent and accuracy.

The AI Proxy Database approach can be used on both Oracle AI Database and Autonomous AI Database 26ai and 19c. records.searchable: Setting Up Data Safe for On-Premises Oracle Databases 8441 Database  - Security NA Cloud SE Workshop Cancelled Secure your On-Premises Oracle Databases with Data Safe on Oracle Cloud Data Safe is a native Oracle Cloud service that empowers organizations to understand data sensitivity, evaluate data risks, mask sensitive data, implement and monitor security controls, assess user security, and monitor user activity—all in a single, unified console. Setup IPSec Site-to-Site VPN on Palo Alto NGFW inside OCI 12068 OCI iwan.hoogendoorn@oracle.com Workshop Self QA Complete Learn how to build inter-region IPsec VPN connectivity in OCI that combines OCI-managed VPN services with Palo Alto NGFW, covering single-instance, active/passive, and active/active firewall deployment models. This lab shows you how to deploy a Site-to-Site IPsec VPN between two OCI regions using a hybrid termination model: Palo Alto Networks NGFW in Frankfurt on one side, and OCI-native Site-to-Site VPN on a DRG in Milan on the other. The result is a flexible, enterprise-ready inter-region design that combines the simplicity of OCI-managed VPN services with the advanced security capabilities of Palo Alto NGFW.
What makes this lab different from a standard VPN tutorial is that the same end-to-end connectivity is built against three different Palo Alto deployment models in the Frankfurt region — so you see how the IPsec design adapts to each one:

Single Instance — a standalone NGFW, ideal for proof-of-concept and small production workloads.
Active/Passive HA — two NGFWs where floating IPs move to the active unit during failover, preserving VPN endpoint continuity.
Active/Active — two NGFWs forwarding traffic simultaneously behind an OCI Network Load Balancer, with VPN tunnels terminated directly on each firewall's Untrust VNIC (since IPsec tunnels cannot be load-balanced at Layer 4).

You'll build an OCI Site-to-Site VPN in Milan attached to a DRG, configure the Palo Alto NGFW in Frankfurt as the IPsec peer, align IKE and IPsec parameters for interoperability, set up static routing and Virtual Router configuration, and validate tunnel status and end-to-end workload connectivity between regions. Along the way, you'll work through the design nuances specific to each HA model — especially for active/active, where traffic symmetry matters and VPN termination shifts from a floating IP to per-firewall tunnels.
By the end of the lab, you will be able to:

Explain hybrid VPN architectures combining Palo Alto NGFW and OCI-native VPN.
Create an OCI Site-to-Site VPN in Milan attached to a DRG.
Configure Palo Alto NGFW in Frankfurt as an IPsec VPN peer across single, active/passive, and active/active topologies.
Configure IKE and IPsec crypto profiles, IKE gateways, tunnel interfaces, and Virtual Router + ECMP behavior.
Implement static routing between Frankfurt and Milan over the IPsec tunnel.
Validate VPN tunnel status, HA behavior, and end-to-end workload connectivity between regions.

This lab is aimed at cloud network architects, security engineers, and OCI practitioners who already understand OCI networking fundamentals and have working experience with Palo Alto VM-Series firewalls in OCI. It builds directly on the prior labs in this series — single-instance, active/passive, and active/active Palo Alto NGFW deployments — and extends those topologies into real-world hybrid connectivity scenarios.
Note: OCI inter-region traffic (via Remote Peering Connection over the DRG) already traverses the Oracle backbone and is encrypted with MACsec, so IPsec is not strictly required between OCI regions. This lab uses two OCI regions purely as a convenient and reproducible endpoint pair — in real deployments, the remote side typically represents an on-premises environment or another cloud provider. Setup Remote Access VPN (GlobalProtect) on Palo Alto NGFW inside OCI 12079 OCI iwan.hoogendoorn@oracle.com Workshop Self QA Complete Extend your OCI security perimeter to remote users by deploying Palo Alto GlobalProtect on an NGFW in OCI, with full coverage of Portal, Gateway, certificates, and client onboarding across three Palo Alto deployment topologies. This lab shows you how to deploy Remote Access VPN using Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect on a Palo Alto NGFW running in Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). GlobalProtect extends the firewall's protection to remote users by giving them an encrypted tunnel into OCI from wherever they connect, turning your cloud-based NGFW into the central enforcement point for user-to-cloud connectivity.
As with the other labs in this series, the same end-to-end functionality is built against three Palo Alto deployment models in the OCI Frankfurt region, so you see how the GlobalProtect design adapts to each topology:

Single Instance — a standalone NGFW where the Portal and Gateway are bound to the Untrust public IP.
Active/Passive HA — two NGFWs where the Portal and Gateway are bound to a floating public IP that always follows the active node, ensuring uninterrupted client connectivity during failover.
Active/Active — two NGFWs behind a dedicated VPN Network Load Balancer (NLB) using 2-tuple hashing (source + destination IP) to ensure each remote user consistently lands on the same firewall node, preserving SSL/IPsec session state.

You'll configure both the GlobalProtect Portal (which delivers the agent and configuration to the client) and the GlobalProtect Gateway (which terminates the VPN tunnel and assigns a tunnel IP from the client pool 192.168.1.0/28). You'll provision a dedicated tunnel interface and security zone for VPN users, generate a self-signed CA and server certificate, build an SSL/TLS Service Profile and a local user authentication profile, download and activate the GlobalProtect Client software on the firewall, and install the GlobalProtect agent on a macOS device to validate end-to-end connectivity. Finally, you'll inspect firewall traffic logs to confirm tunneled traffic is being correctly classified and inspected.
By the end of the lab, you will be able to:

Explain the GlobalProtect Portal and Gateway architecture and how it maps to each Palo Alto deployment model in OCI.
Provision a tunnel interface and dedicated security zone for remote VPN users.
Generate a self-signed CA certificate and a server certificate for the Portal/Gateway.
Configure an SSL/TLS Service Profile and a local user authentication profile.
Configure the GlobalProtect Portal, Gateway, and client IP pool across single, active/passive, and active/active topologies.
Deploy a dedicated VPN NLB in front of the Untrust interfaces for the active/active design, including the External Subnet, route table, and security list it requires.
Install the GlobalProtect agent on a macOS client and validate end-to-end Remote Access VPN connectivity.
Review firewall traffic logs to confirm correct VPN session handling.

This lab is aimed at cloud network architects, security engineers, and OCI practitioners who already have working knowledge of OCI networking and Palo Alto VM-Series firewalls in OCI. It complements the Site-to-Site VPN lab in this series — together, those two patterns let you cover both branch-to-cloud and user-to-cloud connectivity using the same OCI-based NGFW. This lab shows you how to deploy Remote Access VPN using Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect on a Palo Alto NGFW running in Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). GlobalProtect extends the firewall's protection to remote users by giving them an encrypted tunnel into OCI from wherever they connect, turning your cloud-based NGFW into the central enforcement point for user-to-cloud connectivity.
As with the other labs in this series, the same end-to-end functionality is built against three Palo Alto deployment models in the OCI Frankfurt region, so you see how the GlobalProtect design adapts to each topology:

Single Instance — a standalone NGFW where the Portal and Gateway are bound to the Untrust public IP.
Active/Passive HA — two NGFWs where the Portal and Gateway are bound to a floating public IP that always follows the active node, ensuring uninterrupted client connectivity during failover.
Active/Active — two NGFWs behind a dedicated VPN Network Load Balancer (NLB) using 2-tuple hashing (source + destination IP) to ensure each remote user consistently lands on the same firewall node, preserving SSL/IPsec session state.

You'll configure both the GlobalProtect Portal (which delivers the agent and configuration to the client) and the GlobalProtect Gateway (which terminates the VPN tunnel and assigns a tunnel IP from the client pool 192.168.1.0/28). You'll provision a dedicated tunnel interface and security zone for VPN users, generate a self-signed CA and server certificate, build an SSL/TLS Service Profile and a local user authentication profile, download and activate the GlobalProtect Client software on the firewall, and install the GlobalProtect agent on a macOS device to validate end-to-end connectivity. Finally, you'll inspect firewall traffic logs to confirm tunneled traffic is being correctly classified and inspected.
By the end of the lab, you will be able to:

Explain the GlobalProtect Portal and Gateway architecture and how it maps to each Palo Alto deployment model in OCI.
Provision a tunnel interface and dedicated security zone for remote VPN users.
Generate a self-signed CA certificate and a server certificate for the Portal/Gateway.
Configure an SSL/TLS Service Profile and a local user authentication profile.
Configure the GlobalProtect Portal, Gateway, and client IP pool across single, active/passive, and active/active topologies.
Deploy a dedicated VPN NLB in front of the Untrust interfaces for the active/active design, including the External Subnet, route table, and security list it requires.
Install the GlobalProtect agent on a macOS client and validate end-to-end Remote Access VPN connectivity.
Review firewall traffic logs to confirm correct VPN session handling.

Simplify distributed transactions with Oracle MicroTx to prevent inconsistent data and financial losses 11371 3691 Developers - Database brijesh.deo@oracle.com Workshop Delete Requested Public Quarterly QA Complete Learn to use Oracle Transaction Manager for Microservices (MicroTx) to maintain data consistency across several microservices by deploying and running a Bank and Stock-Trading application. It is very simple to use MicroTx. After installing MicroTx, you only need to integrate the MicroTx libraries with your application code to manage the transaction that spans across various microservices. As organizations rush to adopt microservices architecture, they often run into problems associated with data consistency as each microservice typically has its own database. 

In monolithic applications, local transactions were enough as there were no other sources of data that needed to be consistent with the database. An application would start a local transaction, perform some updates, and then commit the local transaction to ensure the application moved from one consistent state to another. 

Once the application’s state is spread across multiple sources of data, some factors need to be considered. What happens if the updates succeed in one microservice, but fails in another microservice as part of the same request? 


One solution is to use a distributed transaction that spans across the sources of data used by the microservices involved in a request. To maintain consistency in the state of all microservices participating in a distributed transaction, Oracle Transaction Manager for Microservices (MicroTx) provides a transaction coordination microservice and client libraries.

In this workshop, you will learn how to use MicroTx to maintain data consistency across several microservices by deploying and running a Bank and Stock-Trading application. This application contains several microservices and it uses distributed, two-phase commit transaction (XA). It is very simple to use MicroTx. After installing MicroTx, you only need to integrate the MicroTx libraries with your application code to manage transactions. In this workshop, you will learn how you can integrate the MicroTx client libraries with the Bank and Stock-Trading application. During the transaction, each microservice also makes updates to a resource manager to track the change in the amount and stocks. When you run the Bank and Stock-Trading application, you will be able to see how MicroTx ensures consistency of transactions across the distributed microservices and their resource managers. You will also integrate MicroTx with the Kubernetes ecosystem by using tools, such as Kiali and Jaeger, to visualize the flow of requests between MicroTx and the microservices. records.searchable: Smart Project Management App with AI-Assisted Development in Oracle APEX 1072 633 APEX apoorva.srinivas@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Build a dynamic application using Oracle APEX AI Assistant using the sample project management dataset. In this lab, you will build a dynamic application using Oracle APEX AI Assistant. You will start by installing a sample project management dataset, then create an initial application with the help of an AI Assistant, demonstrating how AI can accelerate development. Next, you will customize your application the lowcode way, making quick adjustments using pre-built components. You will also enhance your application by writing SQL queries with APEX Assistant, simplifying complex query construction. Finally, you will implement an AI chat assistant using Dynamic Actions and Chat Widget, creating a responsive chat interface for real-time user engagement. By the end of this lab, you'll have practical knowledge in using AI with APEX to efficiently build and customize powerful applications. Speed Up Queries: OCI Redis Caching Meets Urban Mobility Data 11612 3917 OCI rashmi.badan@oracle.com Workshop Delete Requested Public Completed Explore our lab's approach to boosting query speeds and improving data handling efficiency using Redis caching, featuring the NYC taxi dataset in a Flask application. In our lab, we tackle optimising data retrieval within a controlled environment, using the NYC taxi dataset as a test bed to showcase OCI Redis's effectiveness as a caching layer. Our setup features a Flask application querying this dataset from an Oracle Autonomous Database, focusing on specific date ranges for trip data.
We integrate OCI Redis Cache to manage frequently accessed data, streamlining the process: on a data request, the app first checks  OCI Redis Cache, significantly reducing response times if cached. If not, it queries the database, caches the retrieved data, and thus speeds up future requests. This approach not only demonstrates efficient data flow between cache and database but also emphasises the role of caching in minimising database load and enhancing query performance.

details: Explore our lab's approach to boosting query speeds and improving data handling efficiency using Redis caching, featuring the NYC taxi dataset in a Flask application.

In our lab, we tackle optimising data retrieval within a controlled environment, using the NYC taxi dataset as a test bed to showcase OCI Redis's effectiveness as a caching layer. Our setup features a Flask application querying this dataset from an Oracle Autonomous Database, focusing on specific date ranges for trip data.
We integrate OCI Redis Cache to manage frequently accessed data, streamlining the process: on a data request, the app first checks  OCI Redis Cache, significantly reducing response times if cached. If not, it queries the database, caches the retrieved data, and thus speeds up future requests. This approach not only demonstrates efficient data flow between cache and database but also emphasises the role of caching in minimising database load and enhancing query performance.
This lab, utilising the NYC taxi dataset with Redis caching in a Flask app, illustrates practical caching mechanisms to boost data retrieval speeds, aimed at developers looking for tangible improvements in application performance

records.searchable:
SQL Empowerment in Oracle Database 26ai: Leveraging Domains and Features 11427 3742 Database hope.fisher@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Power up with SQL domains in the Oracle Database 26ai - create and use single column and built-in domains, and validate JSON. Then take an in-depth look at features you should know - GROUP BY aliases, optional FROM clause, SQL Boolean, IF [NOT] EXISTS DDL clause, new table VALUE constructor, multi-value INSERTs, UPDATEs with RETURNING or with joins, and annotations. The use case domain functionality is a very powerful new "tool" for application development in Oracle Database 26ai. In general,  use case domains allow users to declare the intended usage for columns with a separate data dictionary objects so that abstract domain specific knowledge can be easily reused. You can use them to provide additional information to a stored column and you can define and validate data with them. Not only relational columns can be validated but also JSON data with the new VALIDATE clause. Like other database objects it can be created, dropped and altered. With it you have the freedom to change the validation logic or information without changing the table definition. 

A use case domain (short domain) is a dictionary object that belongs to a schema and encapsulates a set of optional properties and constraints for common values. Domains provide constraints, display, ordering and annotations attributes. After you define a domain, you can define table columns to be associated with that domain, thereby explicitly applying the domain's optional properties and constraints to those columns. So domains are used to provide additional information to a stored column (JSON or relational), and therefore, used to define and validate data.

You can create, alter and drop a domain in your own schema. To work with domains, you require the privilege CREATE DOMAIN.

There are 3 different types of domains: single column, multi column and flexible domains. In addition there are also built-in domains that you may use.

Overall, we present the following 10 Oracle Database 26ai features: 
- Aliases in GROUP BY clause
- FROM clause - now optional
- Boolean for SQL
- IF [NOT] EXISTS DDL clause
- New table VALUE constructor 
- Multi-value INSERTs
- RETURNING clause of UPDATE and MERGE statement
- Joins in UPDATE and DELETE
- Schema annotations, the new metadata for database objects

details: Power up with SQL domains in the Oracle Database 26ai - create and use single column and built-in domains, and validate JSON. Then take an in-depth look at features you should know - GROUP BY aliases, optional FROM clause, SQL Boolean, IF [NOT] EXISTS DDL clause, new table VALUE constructor, multi-value INSERTs, UPDATEs with RETURNING or with joins, and annotations.

The use case domain functionality is a very powerful new "tool" for application development in Oracle Database 26ai. In general,  use case domains allow users to declare the intended usage for columns with a separate data dictionary objects so that abstract domain specific knowledge can be easily reused. You can use them to provide additional information to a stored column and you can define and validate data with them. Not only relational columns can be validated but also JSON data with the new VALIDATE clause. Like other database objects it can be created, dropped and altered. With it you have the freedom to change the validation logic or information without changing the table definition. 

A use case domain (short domain) is a dictionary object that belongs to a schema and encapsulates a set of optional properties and constraints for common values. Domains provide constraints, display, ordering and annotations attributes. After you define a domain, you can define table columns to be associated with that domain, thereby explicitly applying the domain's optional properties and constraints to those columns. So domains are used to provide additional information to a stored column (JSON or relational), and therefore, used to define and validate data.

You can create, alter and drop a domain in your own schema. To work with domains, you require the privilege CREATE DOMAIN.

There are 3 different types of domains: single column, multi column and flexible domains. In addition there are also built-in domains that you may use.

Overall, we present the following 10 Oracle Database 26ai features: 
- Aliases in GROUP BY clause
- FROM clause - now optional
- Boolean for SQL
- IF [NOT] EXISTS DDL clause
- New table VALUE constructor 
- Multi-value INSERTs
- RETURNING clause of UPDATE and MERGE statement
- Joins in UPDATE and DELETE
- Schema annotations, the new metadata for database objects
- Use case domains

In this workshop, see how SQL Performance Watch provides you SQL execution plan statistics insights and impacts caused by an environment or configuration change so they can be corrected before impacting business. Learn how OCI SQL Performance Watch, a feature in the OCI Database Management service helps you predict and prevent SQL execution performance issues caused by environment changes. In this workshop, see how SQL Performance Watch provides you SQL execution plan statistics insights and impacts caused by an environment or configuration change so they can be corrected before impacting business. By running SQL statements serially before and after changes, SQL Performance Watch generates a comprehensive report for you. The report outlines the net impact on the workload resulting from the system change and identifies any regressed SQL statements. For regressed SQL statements, OCI SQL Performance Watch provides detailed execution plan insights and recommendations for their optimization. Understand why SQL Performance Watch is something every Developer, DBA, DevOps and IT team should be using. Start Polyglot Development with Autonomous Database 11104 3279 ADB Serverless madhusudhan.rao@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA This workshop will demonstrate how to use Python, Node.js, Java, and .NET to connect to the same Oracle Autonomous Database using the same wallet and run SQL queries. Polyglot programming is a computer program or script written in multiple programming languages. Today's enterprise architecture world is a complex set of discrete applications written in different programming languages by multiple developers running under various environments. 

Many of these applications might be interacting with the same database or accessing the same storage layer for commonly used files.

In a real-life example, a front-end customer-facing web application is likely to be written in Node.js or Python or PHP scripts, reading data from an inventory database. At the same time, a Java-based backend application might be doing real-time inventory management. or backend teams might use Apex-based Web or Mobile Applications to interact with the same database. Many Apps might be using PL/SQL cron jobs to sync data between different applications. Machine Learning experts might use Machine Learning Notebooks to run many complex ML algorithms or use python-based clients to interact with data. Framed as a Mars mission support system, it teaches practical AI inference on Oracle Cloud, helping customers build real confidence with OCI infrastructure and local LLMs. Are you feeling like you've missed some steps in your AI journey? Streaming Autonomous AI Database Logs to Grafana Loki with DBMS_LOKI 12134 4475 ADB Dedicated vandana.rajamani@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Build a fully functional log observability pipeline with database logs, streamed to Loki via PL/SQL and visualized in a Grafana Log Explorer dashboard, including a custom DDL change tracker of your own. Oracle Autonomous AI Database on Dedicated Exadata Infrastructure (Autonomous AI Database) generates two critical log streams: the alert log for database diagnostics and the unified audit trail for security and compliance. These logs are accessible only through SQL or the OCI Logging service. In this workshop, you will build a native log push engine that continuously streams these logs to Grafana Loki directly from within the database, with no external agents, Promtail, or file scrapers required.

By the end of this workshop, you will have a built a fully functional log observability pipeline with database logs, streamed to Loki via PL/SQL and visualized in a Grafana Log Explorer dashboard, including a custom DDL change tracker of your own. Successfully protect your database communication using 1-way Transport Layer Security (TLS) 11356 3631 Database  - Security richard.c.evans@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Learn how to implement Transport Layer Security (TLS) to protect your data in transit between the database server and the client The Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol is the gold standard for encrypting and protecting data in transit from the Oracle database client to the server.
TLS requires the server and sometimes the client to authenticate with each other ensuring that the other party is trusted.
In this lab, we will show you how to use a self-signed CA root certificate and use this new CA root certificate to sign a certificate for the database server used in this lab. You will import the CA trusted root certificate into the client default trust store so a client wallet isn’t required. Then establish a one-way TLS connection to the database by setting client-side parameters to specify use of TLS. In this hands-on lab, you will dive into the world of database performance optimization and learn how to effectively utilize Swingbench to test some of the new features in Oracle Database 23c, and push your Oracle system to its limits. Swingbench is a powerful and versatile open-source tool designed for stress testing, benchmarking, and simulating realistic workloads on Oracle databases. This workshop focuses on working with Swingbench to stress test the Oracle Database. Telco Services LiveStack Workshop 12117 4451 Database pat.shepherd@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Build a workshop around the Seer Comms telecom LiveStack to show how Oracle AI Database 26ai unifies subscriber signals, network operations, service orders, field capacity, graph impact analysis, spatial coverage, vector search, predictive assurance, natural-language data access, and auditable AI-assisted actions in one governed data foundation. In this workshop, learners follow Seer Comms through a telecom service-assurance scenario driven by a South Florida 5G demand surge. The labs show how Oracle AI Database 26ai can support the full operations decision loop: inspect the governed data foundation, monitor network experience KPIs, connect subscriber language to services with AI Vector Search, investigate outage and subscriber impact with Property Graph, analyze network sites and field capacity with Oracle Spatial, expose service orders through JSON Relational Duality, review predictive assurance signals, ask governed natural-language questions, and record AI-assisted actions for later audit.
Rather than treating AI, analytics, operational data, and application access as separate systems, the workshop demonstrates how telecom teams can keep evidence close to the database. Learners run SQL against the Seer Comms schema, compare results with expected outputs, and see how converged Oracle Database capabilities help network operations, care, field dispatch, service assurance, and platform teams move from demand signals to explainable action. records.searchable:
Testing eStargz Lazy Pulling on OCI to Reduce Container Startup Time 12104 4444 OCI adina.nicolescu@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Large container images can slow down application startup, especially when workloads run on fresh nodes or scale from a cold cache. This workshop shows how to validate eStargz lazy pulling on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) before introducing it into a production platform. As containerized applications grow, image pull time can become a visible part of startup latency. This is especially true for images that include large frameworks, runtime assets, or model files.
eStargz helps address this problem by enabling lazy pulling. Instead of downloading all image layers upfront, the runtime can fetch only the data needed to start the container and retrieve the rest on demand. Fun, Halloween-based Sherlock Holmes story used as backdrop. This Halloween, Oracle invites LinkedIn members to solve "The Adventure of the Stolen Pumpkin," a Sherlock Holmes mystery that's equal parts entertainment and cutting-edge technical education. In this free, interactive LiveLab, participants investigate the theft of Professor Cavendish's hydrogen research papers—but here's the twist: Watson's traditional SQL keyword searches fail to identify the culprit, while Holmes's use of Oracle's AI Vector Search cracks the case by finding semantic connections invisible to conventional searches. Through this engaging 60-minute experience, learners discover how AI-powered semantic search and vector embeddings can uncover information that keyword searches miss entirely—a critical capability in today's data-driven world. Perfect for data professionals, developers, and curious technologists, this seasonally-timed lab transforms complex concepts like LLMs and Oracle Autonomous AI Database into an accessible detective story demonstrating why searching for meaning rather than words represents the future of information retrieval.

records.searchable: Think Relational, Stay JSON: Oracle’s Duality View Revolution 11912 4223 Database shashank.gugnani@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed This workshop will cover automated migration from a document database to Oracle duality views using the JSON-to-Duality Migrator. We will show you how to leverage your JSON documents to automatically derive possible relational schemas as the underlying foundation for your documents without losing schema flexibility and best practices for doing so. Consider these three issues: (1) Are you looking to move data from a document database such as MongoDB to a relational database, but you are unfamiliar with relational concepts? (2) Are you unsure how to model JSON documents as relational tables and how to create the logical model? (3) Are you interested in transparent and automatic application migration from document databases to Oracle? If the answer to at least one of the above questions is “Yes”, then this HOL is just for you! We will show you how to leverage your JSON documents to automatically derive possible relational schemas as the underlying foundation for your documents without losing schema flexibility and best practices for doing so. The Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Data Science service is a fully managed, self-service platform for data science teams to build, train, and manage machine learning (ML) models in Oracle Cloud Infrastructure.  This lab will go through the steps of setting up a project and a JupyterLab notebook session in OCI Data Science.  We will go through the process of building a time series model, a type of machine learning problem encountered in a variety of industries including finance, retail and transportation.   We will explore a time series dataset and construct data visualizations.  We will build and train time series models with different machine learning packages including Statsmodels and Prophet, and we will analyze and  compare the model performance. records.searchable: Transactional Event Queues: Kafka Java Clients for Oracle Database 11951 4326 Database nithin.thekkupadam.narayanan@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed This workshop demonstrates how Apache Kafka Java producer and consumer applications can migrate seamlessly to Oracle Transactional Event Queues for scalable event streaming directly built into the Oracle Database. This lab walks attendees through the end-to-end process of using Kafka Java client APIs with Oracle TxEventQ. You’ll clone the official sample repo, build and run the Oracle Kafka Java client (okafka) and a demo microservice, create TxEventQ topics, produce messages, and consume them with a Java consumer. The exercises include: (1) running an out-of-the-box Kafka Java app against TxEventQ, (2) migrating a simple Kafka app to TxEventQ, and (3) demonstrating transactional produce/consume patterns and partitioning/rebalancing behavior with Oracle’s Kafka compatibility layer. Practical takeaways include configuration snippets, recommended partition/consumer strategies, and tradeoffs when consolidating streaming into the database. Try Machine Learning and Predict Optimal Pit Strategy with Oracle Red Bull Racing 11228 3403 OCI Data Science ignacio.m.martinez@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete In this workshop, you’ll have the opportunity to experiment with predictive models and choose which variables you think will determine a successful pit stop. You’ll also learn about the steps of creating a machine learning model to try and predict the best pit strategy for a team, become familiar with the entire process, and discover how to tie data science results back to the business. Explore data, deploy a predictive machine learning model … and win a simulated Red Bull Race against your peers.

You’re the race strategist at Red Bull Racing. Your mission? The night before the race, you’ll have to use machine learning to predict which factors contribute to determining the fastest race.

But there are multiple factors that go into predicting the fastest race, including different tire compounds, qualifying performance, historical data on which laps are chosen for pit stops, and expected weather conditions.

What are the variables that make all the difference?
In this two-hour workshop, you’ll have the opportunity to experiment with predictive models and choose which variables you think will determine a successful pit stop. You’ll also learn about the steps of creating a machine learning model to try and predict the best pit strategy for a team, become familiar with the entire process, and discover how to tie data science results back to the business. Two Models, One World: JSON Relational Duality Views in MySQL HeatWave 11973 MySQL sindhuja.banka@oracle.com Workshop Completed Modern development often needs the best of both worlds: the flexibility of JSON and the reliability of relational data. In this workshop, we’ll dive into MySQL’s JSON Relational Duality Views, a practical way to work with both models at once. You’ll get hands-on experience mapping complex data to clean, easy-to-use JSON structures and see how this approach can simplify your applications. Today’s developers are often caught between two worlds: they need the structure and security of relational databases, but also want the flexibility and speed that comes with JSON. MySQL’s JSON Relational Duality Views are designed to bridge that gap. This feature makes it much easier to work with modern data formats, letting teams query and update JSON documents that directly reflect what’s stored in normalized tables.

In this session, we’ll work through examples so you can see how JSON Duality Views can fit into your own projects. We’ll cover the basics what the feature is and when you’d want to use it before moving on to practical tasks like inserting, updating, and deleting data. You’ll also learn how concurrency control works in this context, helping you keep data reliable even as your application scales. Modern development often needs the best of both worlds: the flexibility of JSON and the reliability of relational data. In this workshop, we’ll dive into MySQL’s JSON Relational Duality Views, a practical way to work with both models at once. You’ll get hands-on experience mapping complex data to clean, easy-to-use JSON structures and see how this approach can simplify your applications.

Today’s developers are often caught between two worlds: they need the structure and security of relational databases, but also want the flexibility and speed that comes with JSON. MySQL’s JSON Relational Duality Views are designed to bridge that gap. This feature makes it much easier to work with modern data formats, letting teams query and update JSON documents that directly reflect what’s stored in normalized tables.

In this session, we’ll work through examples so you can see how JSON Duality Views can fit into your own projects. We’ll cover the basics what the feature is and when you’d want to use it before moving on to practical tasks like inserting, updating, and deleting data. You’ll also learn how concurrency control works in this context, helping you keep data reliable even as your application scales.

Unify the Data Layer with Oracle Autonomous AI Lakehouse 12158 4473 AI/ML Database eli.schilling@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Learn how Oracle Autonomous AI Lakehouse unifies relational data, application extracts, and unstructured content within a governed data layer. Through guided, hands-on activities, you’ll explore and build Bronze, Silver, and Gold data products that prepare trusted enterprise data for analytics, semantic search, and agentic AI. In this workshop, you’ll use Oracle Autonomous AI Lakehouse to bring together representative data from enterprise applications, operational databases, and Object Storage. The scenario follows Seer as it unifies simulated extracts from financial, project scheduling, supplier relationship, inspection, and compliance systems with contracts, engineering specifications, and other unstructured project documents.
You’ll learn the principles and benefits of the medallion architecture and see how raw Bronze data is progressively validated, standardized, reconciled, and promoted into trusted Silver and Gold data products. Hands-on activities include configuring cloud storage access, loading and linking data through graphical tools, creating an external table over data in Object Storage, performing a Bronze-to-Silver transformation, exploring lineage, and validating the resulting data products.
The workshop also clarifies how Oracle AI Data Platform and Autonomous AI Lakehouse complement each other. AIDP can orchestrate broader data engineering and catalog-driven workflows, while ALH provides a self-contained, governed environment for storing, transforming, querying, and serving unified data. By the end of the workshop, you’ll understand how a well-designed data layer gives analytics applications, semantic search, and AI agents access to consistent, secure, and business-ready information. Use Data Labeling Service to Create a Biomedical Image Classification Model 11011 3097 AI Services samuel.cacela@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Explore Data Labeling Service and OCI Vision AI Service through a healthcare use case. Biomedical image classification has become increasingly popular in recent years. Many physicians and research facilities are leveraging image classification to assist in classifying biomedical images into distinct categories. This technology can assist physicians in making diagnoses and can also be leveraged in research. Although this lab focuses on biomedical images, the use of the Oracle services highlighted in this lab can be applied across a wide range of industries and use cases.

This tutorial teaches end-users how to bulk upload images to object storage, create a dataset in the Data Labeling Service, bulk label the images, and create/train a custom image classification model using the labeled dataset. Each image contains a scan of a blood sample and is labeled with one of three classifications: cell, debris, stripe. The goal is to leverage DLS and OCI Vision to classify these images. Use HTTP Request Metrics to Autoscale an Instance Pool 11887 4280 OCI ryan.palmaro@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed In this tutorial, you will deploy the infrastructure needed to automatically scale an instance pool based on the number of http requests received by the load balancer. In this tutorial, you will deploy the infrastructure needed to automatically scale an instance pool based on the number of http requests received by the load balancer. The majority of the deployment has been automated with terraform. Once the scaling infrastructure has been deployed you will trigger a load and observe the scaling infrastructure.

Scaling by the http request metric is usefully when applications need to respond to rapid bursts of traffic and scale quickly. Http requests are a leading indicator of application load, while CPU and memory can be a trailing indicator for some applications. details: Explore the process of creating communicating microservices with ATP connectivity, preparing them for use in a cloud native deployment

Cloud native deployments using microservices are one of the latest deployment architectures. This lab will show you how to use the Helidon Micro Profile framework to REST enable existing (or new) code and add security, configuration management and handle the new types of fault that come in from distributed processing. You will see how to easily connect to a database, create communicating microservices, and also how you can easily connect to a microservice from existing code, demonstrating how you can split part of a monolith into a microservice. You will explore how microservices support high availability deployments in Kubernetes, and how to trace the flow of a request across multiple microservices. The simple generation of metrics data for monitoring will be shown

records.searchable: Using Kafka with Oracle Streaming Services 4081 Database david.start@oracle.com Workshop Approved In the workshop the user will create an Oracle Streaming Service and then connect a sample Kafka producer and consumer to it. They will also have a chance to leverage both the Oracle 19c and Autonomous Databases. In this workshop you will provision a virtual machine running the Oracle 19c database, an Oracle Streaming Service, and the Oracle Autonomous Database. Throughout the workshop you will look at, make changes to, compile and run Java code. You will see a producer that will read a CSV file which will generate messages and load them into the Oracle Streaming Service. A consumer that will dequeue messages from the Oracle Streaming Service and load them into an Oracle 19c database. A load testing program that will look at the performance of a table vs a Memoptimized Rowstore for IOT type programs. Then finally you will get a chance to take a look at a PL/SQL program that will connect from inside of the Oracle Autonomous Database to the Oracle Streaming Service. Get started in minutes with zero changes to applications and business operation. A data lakehouse combines the cost and scale advantages of the data lake with the analytics capabilities of data warehouse technologies. It enables you to ingest, store, analyze, and derive business value from large constantly changing data sets. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) provides the foundation for the lakehouse as an open and flexible approach to analyzing any type of data, at any scale, from anywhere. However, migrating data lakes into OCI can be challenging without the right support.

Oracle has partnered with WANdisco to make the unique benefits of WANdisco LiveData Migrator available to OCI users. This migration solution enables organizations to move away from costly high maintenance traditional platforms, such as Hadoop data lakes, without disrupting the operation of those platforms during migration. It helps you to migrate data and metadata to Oracle Cloud quickly and easily so that you can exploit the power and capabilities of OCI and its services, including Oracle Cloud Object Storage, Oracle Big Data Service and Oracle Lakehouse. Win the race with MySQL HeatWave Lakehouse 11472 3836 MySQL perside.foster@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete This exciting lab merges sports with technological innovation. You'll work with the latest MySQL HeatWave Lakehouse features to dive into the secrets behind winning in SailGP! You will learn to work with MySQL HeatWave Lakehouse to query data directly from object storage, and you will pick up skills such as data visualization and machine learning. This exciting lab merges sports with technological innovation. You'll work with the latest MySQL HeatWave Lakehouse features to dive into the secrets behind winning in SailGP!
MySQL HeatWave Lakehouse's power lies in its ability to query hundreds of terabytes of data directly from object storage—as fast as querying data inside the database.
SailGP offers you the perfect playground to try out HeatWave Lakehouse. The high speed, high tech boats contain over 800 IoT sensors that provide more than 12,000 data points, and the teams are continuously looking for insights into that data to improve their chances of winning.
This is your chance to see what it is to be a "Data Athlete" for SailGP and help the sailing teams increase their performance. Along the way, you will learn to use techniques like data visualization and machine learning!
Here’s what you’ll learn:
- How to configure the infrastructure, including MySQL HeatWave Lakehouse and other components.
- How to load data directly into object storage and configure it in the Lakehouse.
- How to create insights from your Lakehouse data by creating intuitive visualizations using Oracle Analytics Cloud.
- How to build, train, and use machine learning models with HeatWave AutoML.
Off to the races! Working with RDF Graphs in Graph Studio 11018 3195 Database - Spatial and Graph ramu.murakami.gutierrez@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Create and query RDF graphs using Graph Studio. Graph Studio in Oracle Autonomous Database enables users to model, create, query, and analyze property graph data. It includes notebooks, developer APIs for executing graph queries using PGQL, nearly 60 built-in graph algorithms, and offers dozens of visualizations including native graph visualization. 
In addition to property graph, Graph Studio now extends support for semantic technologies, including storage, inference, and query capabilities for data and ontologies based on Resource Description Framework (RDF) and Web Ontology Language (OWL).

You Down With OPG? Leveraging Operational Property Graphs in Oracle 23ai 11701 Database ramona.magadan@oracle.com Workshop Approved Oracle 23ai's new Operational Property Graphs (OPGs) offer the ability to analyze interactions among and connections between entities in real time - a useful feature set for fraud detection in finances, social media influence measurement, and hierarchical relationships hidden within our data. There’s an old saying: A lie can circle the globe in the time it takes for truth to put on its shoes. Operational Property Graphs (OPGs) in Oracle 23ai make it possible to analyze influencers and their activities in real time to determine from where negative (or positive!) goodwill is originating, even as those postings are happening. Best of all, we can do this with simple SQL statements against property graph views of our data. This lab will show how to:
- Create OPGs in a 23ai environment
- Identify and analyze key disruptions within a simulated social media network with simple SQL statements
- Deploy and use the latest version of the GraphViz plugin within an APEX 23.1 application Individual author Individual Content to review/remove Missing LiveLabs ID in current WMS export; review as a draft or unpublished row 11701 Workshop Approved Database 2025-09-09 2024-07-31 Individual author Individual No Repository Url 11701 Workshop Approved Database 2025-09-09 2024-07-31 Individual author Individual No Repository Url No repository URL is present in the current WMS export. ramona.magadan@oracle.com DB Product Management Oracle 23ai's new Operational Property Graphs (OPGs) offer the ability to analyze interactions among and connections between entities in real time - a useful feature set for fraud detection in finances, social media influence measurement, and hierarchical relationships hidden within our data. Zero Downtime Migration: Logical Online Migration to Oracle Autonomous Database 7261 3271 Database - MAA sinan.petrus.toma@oracle.com Workshop Published Disabled Quarterly QA Complete Explore migrating On-Premises Oracle Database to the Oracle ADB using ZDM Logical Online methodology Oracle customers are moving Oracle workloads into the Oracle Cloud or onto Engineered Systems at a growingly rapid pace. However, migrating workloads has been a source of challenges for many years. In particular, migrating database workloads from one system to another or into the Cloud is easier said than done.  

Based on years of experience migrating Oracle workloads, Oracle has developed Zero Downtime Migration (ZDM).  ZDM is Oracle’s premier solution for a simplified and automated migration experience, providing zero to negligible downtime for the production system and depending on the migration scenario. ZDM allows you to directly and seamlessly migrate your on-premises Oracle Databases to and between any Oracle-owned infrastructure, including Exadata Database Machine On-Premises, Exadata Cloud at Customer (ExaC@C), and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure.

This workshop covers an in-depth step-by-step guide of migrating your On-Premises Oracle Databases to the Oracle Autonomous Database using ZDM's Logical Online methodology. This workshop introduces Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Zero Trust Packet Routing (ZPR) for securing sensitive databases and applications using simple policies and attributes. It demonstrates how ZPR simplifies access control by requiring fewer configuration steps compared to traditional virtual network setups and security policies. You'll learn how to protect sensitive data without exposing your data in the event of routing changes or network misconfigurations.
